defects.summary: Concurrent create into ONE SHARED directory costs 8.3x more wall per node at 32 nodes than the same creates into per-node private directories (1842 ms vs 222 ms for 8 creates; 9.3x on the mean, 34x on p95), and the cost is ENTIRELY IN THE TAIL -- the shared arm's p50 is 10 ms and flat in N, so every node pays roughly one multi-second stall per 8 creates rather than a uniformly slower create. 74.5% of blocked samples sit in the CAW inode-grant wait (mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait under caw_lock_body), against 7.0% in the SCSI transport, so this is the DLM's EX rotation among 32 contenders on one directory inode. A second, smaller term rides underneath: the PRIVATE arm is not flat either, growing 6x from 1 to 32 nodes (37 -> 222 ms) with nothing shared but the mount. (sess380 re-measured all of this after fixing tests/create_scale_curve.sh, whose private arm had been running a 32-way mkdir on a shared parent INSIDE the measured window; the previously recorded '42x, private scales flat' figures came from that contaminated control.)
evidence:
SESS380 THE LOAD IS READS, AND THEY ARE THE PROBE WALK — NOT THE CAS COLLISION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ENTRY (AND I, EARLIER THE SAME SESSION) SPENT THE MOST EFFORT ON. New harness tests/shared_dir_slot_cost.sh counts every SCSI command the whole cluster issues to the ONE CAW slot of a shared directory while 32 nodes do 256 creates into it. Repeated over 6 runs on 0.15.6-0.15.10, stable:
    READ(16)+FUA       5,844 - 8,587   = 23 - 34 per create
    COMPARE AND WRITE    424 -   515   = 1.7 - 2.0 per create (50-52% MISCOMPARE)
  reads are 93% of ALL traffic on that sector and outnumber writes 13-16 to 1.
P383-SLOTREAD then tagged every one of those reads with its caller (7,653 tagged reads, one run):
    find_slot_skip                6,373   83.3%   <- the open-addressing PROBE WALK
    caw_wait_for_grant              880   11.5%   <- the grant poll loop
    caw_count_resource_slots        398    5.2%
    bast_poll_fn                      2    0.0%
So ~25 of the ~30 reads per create are slot RESOLUTION, re-walked from scratch on every lookup, and the resource's home slot IS the hot sector, so every walk reads it at least once. The grant poll loop — the thing four sessions of this entry's history blamed — is 11.5%.

SESS380 FOUR HYPOTHESES REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, recorded so nobody re-runs them. Each was cheap and each was wrong; together they are what narrowed the search to the probe walk.
  (1) 'The unlock CAS keeps losing to peers REGISTERING INTEREST, so skip the backoff when the miscompare was a pure registration.' Built an exact-transition classifier (reconstructs byte for byte the only image a registration could produce, then memcmps) and ran it with the acting knob OFF: of 475 unlock miscompares, 1 was benign (0.2%), 7 were holder changes, ZERO were yield_to moves, and 467 (98.3%) were MULTI-GENERATION — several unrelated writes landed between our compare image and our re-read. The optimisation would fire on 0.2% of cases. mxfs.caw_unlock_fastretry ships DEFAULT 0 and should stay there; the classifier is retained because its histogram is what produced this finding.
  (2) 'Releases wake the whole waiter field, so every handoff costs N reads.' P382-WAKE says the wake-the-field branch is taken 0.0% of the time: 75.7% mint a single successor, 24.3% use an existing ticket, mean 1.25 nodes woken against 4.70 waiters present.
  (3) 'The 2ms fastpoll window is the amplifier' (a suspicion written into the mxfs.caw_inode_fastpoll knob's own comment years ago). Turning it OFF made reads WORSE: 26.6 -> 32.9 per create.
  (4) 'The reads are exponential-backstop timeouts, and the nudge would carry the grants anyway' — supported by P297-TKT showing 96.6% of ticketed waiters wake by NUDGE with ZERO swallowed nudges. Raising mxfs.caw_poll_max_ms from 25 to 200 made BOTH worse: reads 22.8 -> 29.6 per create and per-node wall 1577 -> 2612 ms. Removing the fastpoll window on top of that: 33.5 reads, 2767 ms.
Also refuted structurally: there is NO I/O and no blocking call between the slot read and the CAW in the unlock loop, so the collision window is pure CPU and cannot be narrowed.

SESS380 MECHANISM, MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SAME SLOT. The contended resource is not the transport and not a long holder doing real work -- it is that ONE 512B CAW slot is the single mutable cell holding a directory's ENTIRE lock state (holder bitmaps per mode, waiter bitmap, waiter_ex bitmap, yield ticket, generation). At 32 contenders, a waiter REGISTERING its waiter bit and the holder CLEARING its holder bit are COMPARE AND WRITE against the same word, so they invalidate each other. Both halves are now counted directly:
  RELEASE SIDE (P381-UNLK-CONTEND, new this session, fires only when the unlock CAS lost a race):
    112 contended unlocks in one 32-node shared-directory create run
    mean retries 1.96, mean MISCOMPAREs 1.96, mean backoff sleep 10.1 ms,
    mean unlock wall 27.9 ms, max 77 ms; the backoff sleep is 36% of that wall and the
    remaining 64% is the extra find_slot READ + CAW that each losing retry issues.
    78 of the 112 were on ino=131, the directory under test.
  ACQUIRE SIDE (P139-LOCKTOTAL -EAGAIN attribution, same run):
    121 acquire retries, of which 109 are ea_regwait -- LOST THE WAITER-REGISTER CAS --
    12 ea_compat, and ZERO ea_claim. The losses are on registering interest, not on
    claiming a free slot.
  HOLDER-SIDE COST BREAKDOWN (P138-BAST, ino=131): dur_us 26,565 / 36,542 / 42,830 / 48,457 with
    sx (the WIRE UNLOCK proper) = 25,976 / 32,919 / 40,624 / 46,384 us, i.e. 95-98% of the release.
    The mandatory drain pipeline (sa+sb+sc+sd) is only 2-4 ms of it. The release is not slow
    because of the durability work; it is slow because the unlock cannot win its own CAS.
THE FEEDBACK LOOP IS THE POINT: every waiter that registers extends the holder's release, the longer release lengthens the queue, and the longer queue brings more registering waiters. Cost is therefore superlinear in N, which is what the 1 -> 32 ladder shows (37 -> 1842 ms, 49.8x). This is precisely the failure mode the sess379 RULE-5 review predicted for this format -- 'every successful update invalidates all competing comparisons ... N simultaneous distinct bit updates approach O(N^2) total work ... no backoff changes the serialization bound' -- and its prescribed fix is the same one that applies here: a writer GATE record plus incarnation-tagged PER-NODE reader records at independently writable locations, so registering interest writes to the node's OWN sector instead of CASing the shared word. See docs/rulings/hot-slot-caw-fix-shape.md.

SESS380 WHY THIS DEFECT RESISTED ATTRIBUTION FOR SO LONG -- TWO BLIND PROBES AND A BROKEN CONTROL, all three fixed this session. (1) P138-WAIT fires when ONE wait_for_grant call exceeds 5 ms, but a contended acquire is many sub-5 ms waits with outer retries between them: on a run whose creates measured p95 424 ms it produced FOUR lines fleet-wide. (2) P139-LOCKTOTAL brackets the whole acquire including retries -- the right probe -- but its floor was hardcoded at 800 ms, ABOVE the entire distribution, so it produced ZERO lines. It is now a knob (mxfs.caw_locktotal_ms, default unchanged at 800); at a 50 ms floor the same workload yields 118 acquires totalling 57.1 s, which matches the workload's own total create time -- i.e. the census now accounts for essentially all of the tail instead of 0.4% of it. (3) tests/caw_grant_wait_anatomy.sh only ever ran the PRIVATE shape and let each node mkdir inside the measured window, so it censused the parent inode's mkdir rather than the shared directory under test; it now takes SHAPE=shared|private, pre-creates every directory from one node, arms the P139 floor on all nodes and restores it, and harvests P139-LOCKTOTAL / P139-TAILCENSUS / P34-ACQ-SLOW as well as the per-wait probes. Any pre-sess380 number from these three tools understates the tail or measures the wrong resource.

SESS380 CLEAN LADDER, on a harness whose private arm is FINALLY a control. tests/create_scale_curve.sh was fixed this session to pre-create BOTH shapes' directories from one node; before that, every node in the `private` arm ran `mkdir -p $dirbase/r$i` INSIDE the measured window, so all P nodes took the same parent inode EX and both arms contended on a shared directory. That artifact is the most likely explanation for the two irreconcilable private-arm numbers already in this entry ('wall 33..41ms, FLAT in N' vs 'mean 5.2..191.8ms, 37x in N'). With the fix, 32 healthy nodes (all mounted, max loadavg 0.56, full 27/27 board green minutes earlier), fresh fs, 8 creates/node, MXFS 0.15.4 sv DACACDDE464B211CF68DE3F on SCST +caw-abort-reclaim.3:
  participants          1      2      4      8     16     32
  PRIVATE wall_p50     37    170    104    125    220    222  ms   <- 6.0x from 1 to 32
  PRIVATE mean        3.9   11.9   10.8   13.3   25.3   25.0  ms
  PRIVATE p50           4     12      8     10     16     19  ms
  PRIVATE p95           7     43     36     46     90     63  ms
  SHARED  wall_p50     37     87    160    385   1000   1842  ms   <- 49.8x from 1 to 32
  SHARED  mean        3.9    8.5   18.1   44.2  122.5  233.2  ms
  SHARED  p50           3      7      7      8     10     10  ms   <- FLAT in N
  SHARED  p95           8     31    105    305   1021   2170  ms   <- ALL the cost is here
SHARED vs PRIVATE at 32 nodes: 1842 vs 222 ms wall = 8.3x; 233.2 vs 25.0 ms mean = 9.3x; 2170 vs 63 ms p95 = 34x. So the shared-directory framing of this entry is CONFIRMED, at 8-34x rather than the previously recorded 42x, and it lives ENTIRELY IN THE TAIL -- the shared arm's p50 is 10 ms at 32 nodes, flat in N and no worse than the private arm's 19 ms. Every node pays roughly one multi-second stall per 8 creates. Separately, the private arm is NOT flat either (37 -> 222 ms, 6x), which is a smaller but real common-mode scaling cost that this entry should not lose sight of.

SESS380 STALL-SITE CENSUS ON THE FIXED TARGET (tests/create_stall_stacks.sh 8 32, 776 blocked samples at 50 ms across 32 nodes). Task state 77.7% S / 22.3% D. Nearest non-generic blocking frame:
  74.5%  mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait   (caw_lock_body <- mxfs_dlm_caw_lock <- mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock
                                     <- mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed <- mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin)
   9.8%  mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin      (xfs_ilock <- xfs_ilock_data_map_shared <- xfs_dir_lookup)
   7.0%  blk_execute_rq            (the SCSI READ(16)+FUA inside read_slot)
   1.5%  mxfs_pal_sleep_ms | 1.4% mxfs_inode_cluster_durable | 1.4% xfs_iget | 1.4% xfs_buf_iowait
This is the SAME verdict as the earlier census (then 75.3% caw_acquire_poll_sleep, since replaced by a condvar) and it is decisive for attribution: the cost is WAITING FOR A DLM GRANT on one directory inode, not transport. The transport share actually FELL from 14.2% to 7.0% once the target's wait-for cycle was fixed, and this entry's own CAW attempt census already measured CAW service time at 1.5% of grant wait with zero I/O errors. Do NOT re-attribute this defect to D-HOT-SLOT-CAW-SERIALIZES-LUN-PER-LBA-379 (DISPROVED sess380): that entry was about per-LBA command serialization at the target, which is now measured at 1.6x, while this is the DLM's own EX rotation among 32 contenders.

Measured on the live 32-node cluster, per-create latency, files written into per-node PRIVATE subdirectories of ONE shared parent so the only contended resource is the parent directory inode (tests/create_scale_curve.sh):
  participants   1     2     4     8    16    32
  p50  ms        5     6     7     8    12    11   <- FLAT in N
  mean ms      5.2   9.2  10.8  26.0  71.7 191.8   <- 37x in N
Shared-dir shape is only ~1.3x worse than private-subdir (247.9 vs 191.8 mean at 32), so dirent/leaf serialisation is SECONDARY; the cost is the parent inode lock. Native local-fs reference on the same nodes: 2.6ms mean. Uncontended MXFS is healthy at 5.2ms.
Stall site read off the kernel, not guessed (tests/create_stall_stacks.sh, 1005 blocked /proc/PID/stack samples): 75.3% caw_acquire_poll_sleep under mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed -> mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock -> mxfs_dlm_caw_lock -> caw_wait_for_grant; 14.2% read_slot's SCSI READ(16)+FUA; 4.2% ilock.
CAW attempt census per logical grant (tests/caw_grant_wait_anatomy.sh, the measurement GPT named as decisive): CAW submissions mean 6.1 max 33; miscompares mean 5.1 max 32; io errors 0; CAW SERVICE TIME 617ms = 1.5% of 42.1s of grant wait; slot poll READs mean 52.6 max 223. So the wait is ~52 poll cycles per grant, NOT transport service time (1.5%) and NOT CAS throughput (~1.2% at 0.65ms per CAW). The contended resource is ONE directory inode with mixed demand: measured slot masks ino=131 req_mode=PR waiters=0xfb4dffff waiters_ex=0x28440804 holders_pr=0x4820000 holders_ex=0 => 28 waiters of which 6 want EX, 3 hold PR, none holds EX.

sess126 ROOT CAUSE PROVEN BY DIRECT WALL ATTRIBUTION (0.11.452/A1C4A05CB6356F02B8625F6, fleet-confirmed). NEW TOOL tests/cc_stackprof.sh + tests/mxfs_stackprof.py: 20Hz /proc/PID/task/*/stack sampling, 8 nodes, 30310 ticks/34300 samples of a virgin-fs crash_consistency run. 26.28% of ALL samples are mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait < caw_nudge_wait < caw_wait_for_grant < mxfs_dlm_caw_lock < mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock; 16.59% are open_last_lookups (queued behind it on the local dir i_rwsem); 39.61% do_wait + 13.59% pipe_read are the parent shells on those same children. Device path, CAS contention and AG locks are ABSENT (<2%). So ~100% of workload blocking wall is the CAW INODE grant wait. THE CONTENDED INODE IS THE MOUNT ROOT, ino 128 (stat /mnt/shared) -- NOT the shared test directory (.crash_consistency = ino 29360256 took ONE >5ms grant, 294ms, all run). Every prior session chased the wrong inode. P138-WAIT is ALWAYS-ON (dlm_caw.c:5918, INODE, >5ms, capped 4000/boot) -- instr=1 is UNNECESSARY and perturbs hard (86s run -> >240s). New harness tests/cc_grantwait.sh arm|disarm|report. 202 grant waits >5ms cluster-wide: ino 128 mode=3(PR) 202 grants, 713681ms summed, mean 3533ms, ffw_share 100%, caw_svc_ms 0.8% of wall, caw_miss p50=0. P139-TAILCENSUS n=172: bit_lost=0 (NOT queue-position loss), chosen nonzero 3/172, free_defer 2/172, foreign_yt p50=15 in ALL 172, doze250 p50=15 in ALL 172 => 15 x MXFS_CAW_DEFER_POLL_MS(250) = 3750ms. THE PROOF -- P204-YT-DEFER raw, test5, ino=128, 12 consecutive samples spanning 3 seconds: yt=20000 FROZEN, hpr=8209288 (7 PR holders) BIT-IDENTICAL AND FROZEN, hex=0 (nobody holds EX), wex=27da0000 (10 EX waiters), w growing, age_ms 2037->4980 then the 5000ms MXFS_CAW_YIELD_TIMEOUT_MS stale-ticket valve fires and the cycle repeats. Ticket age at defer ino=128 n=1141: p50=2873 p90=4588 max=4994ms. Queue shape: waiters 19.2, waiters_ex 10.5, holders_ex 0.00, holders_pr 6.79. modes: 3=PR, 5=EX. MECHANISM: (1) a node wants EX on the mount root -- on a virgin fs `mkdir -p $MNT/.crash_consistency` races on all 32 nodes, and the dir is never removed, which is why the SECOND run is fast (sess125's empty-dir recipe was a correct observation with the wrong explanation). (2) A yield ticket is armed for that EX waiter. (3) The 7 PR holders DO NOT RELEASE under the EX BAST for 3+ seconds -- stack evidence 'msleep < mxfs_drain_ilock_read < mxfs_dlm_bast_process < mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn': the release path drains local ilock readers while all 32 nodes path-walk the root continuously for their dd/md5sum opens, so new readers arrive faster than the drain retires them (read-side livelock; nothing bars new readers once a BAST is pending). (4) Meanwhile every PR requester -- COMPATIBLE with the existing PR holders, hex=0 -- is forced to defer on the foreign EX ticket (strict writer preference) and dozes 250ms at a time. (5) Nothing progresses until the 5s valve fires. The system runs on its safety valve. sess24 already documented half of this at dlm_caw.c:155-245 (mxfs_caw_pr_batch_nodefer, default 0): 'a PR requester is COMPATIBLE the whole time and defers purely on policy: strict writer preference, unbounded... yt_age is the wrong clock, the release path re-arms yield_set_ms whenever the ticket VALUE changes.' sess126 confirms it on the ROOT inode at 32 nodes and supplies the other half: the EX waiter the ticket guards can never be granted either.

sess127 (0.11.452/A1C4A05CB6356F02B8625F6, VIRGIN fs, hostload 12.68 = quiet rig) RE-ROOTED this at the BAST RECEIVE path and REFUTED the sess126 ilock hypothesis. The run FAILED at 90s/90s. NEW INSTRUMENTS: tests/cc_bastcensus.sh (holder side: pairs the always-on P70-BP ENTRY/EXIT=full by realns and prints a STALLED/UNDELIVERED/CHURN discriminator) and a FOCUS section added to tests/mxfs_stackprof.py + cc_stackprof.sh agg (tick occupancy + full signatures for stacks containing mxfs_dlm_bast*/mxfs_drain_ilock_read, i.e. the release side isolated from the requester side). REFUTATIONS: P132-ILOCK-STUCK/-TIMEOUT = 0 on ALL 32 nodes; FOCUS = 1.18% of 30231 ticks over 8 nodes; msleep<mxfs_drain_ilock_read<bast_process = 4 of 724 focus samples (0.55%) -- the ilock drain is NOT the blocker. P36 is also not the cause: 295 P36-MHT-REARM on ino=128 with pr=0 ex=0 pin=0 in 295 of 295 (so the firing predicate is the unprinted i_dlm_acq_inflight>0), strikes max=10 (~80ms/episode) vs the 2500 strikeout. HOLDER CENSUS ino=128: P70-BP ENTRY=332 EXIT=full=158; ENTRY mode PR=137 NL=187(no-op) EX=8; ENTRY->EXIT release wall p50=319ms p90=1670ms p99=3802ms max=5093ms, >=250ms in 53.2%, >=1000ms in 35; held_ms at BAST entry p50=92203ms (the root tenure spans the WHOLE run). Only 145 real PR/EX release pipelines cluster-wide in 90s = ~1.6 handoffs/s for an inode 19 nodes are queued on -- the limiter is handoff RATE, not release cost. THE ROOT, from FOCUS full signatures (724 samples): 35.22% (255) blk_execute_rq<scsi_execute_cmd<mxfs_pal_scsi_read_fua_bdev<mxfs_pal_bdev_read_prio<read_slot<find_slot_skip<mxfs_dlm_caw_held<mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_held<mxfs_dlm_bast_notify<v5_bast_cb<bast_recv_fn; +4.14% (30) the same read under mxfs_caw_orphan_forensic; +0.97% (7) under caw_count_resource_slots<mxfs_dlm_caw_self_held_scan. => ~43% of ALL DLM release-side blocked wall is the single-threaded UDP BAST receive thread doing synchronous SCSI slot reads INLINE. bast_recv_fn (dlm_caw.c:10640) is one thread per node and calls ctx->bast_cb() synchronously inside the recvfrom loop; mxfs_dlm_caw_held() (dlm_caw.c:8493) answers 'do I hold this resource?' -- a question about our OWN bit -- via find_slot() -> a shared-LUN read -> node_held_mode(slot, ctx->node_bit), while the node already keeps ctx->held.slots[]/held.count under held.lock in memory (bast_poll_fn iterates exactly that list) and XFS has ip->i_dlm_mode. CONSEQUENCE MEASURED: test5 /proc/net/snmp Udp InErrors=8085 RcvbufErrors=8085 -- every UDP error on the node is a receive-buffer OVERFLOW, i.e. BAST hints are being SILENTLY DROPPED -- and the socket is NOT under-buffered (mxfs_pal_udp_open, pal/linux/kern.c:2420-2426, already sets sk_rcvbuf=4MB + SOCK_RCVBUF_LOCK from sess8), so overflowing 4MB means the thread stalls for seconds. This closes the loop on every earlier number: the holders are not refusing to release, THEY HAVE NOT BEEN TOLD -- sess126's hpr mask bit-identical for 3s, age_ms 2037->4980 before the 5000ms stale-ticket valve, mean grant wait 3533ms, and ~1.6 handoffs/s are all consistent with multi-second BAST delivery latency plus outright hint loss. PRECEDENT MISSED: dlm_caw.h:311-322 (sess35 NUDGE v2) states this exact mechanism for the GRANT NUDGE path -- 'v1 grant nudges woke EVERY blocked acquirer on every node; each did a READ(16)+FUA re-check, and at a 32-node single-dir create convoy those ~28 serialized reads at the one SCSI target WERE the measured ~21.6ms per-handoff latency' -- and fixed it with wake_mask so receivers skip the disk read. The BAST path never got the same treatment.

2026-08-04 sess130 — MEASURED ON 0.11.453 (BAST dispatch queue live, fleet-confirmed F20024E38213A9E64DB6718), VIRGIN fs, quiet console. FIRST, A CONFOUND THAT INVALIDATES THE MAGNITUDES OF THE sess126 BASELINE: tests/cc_grantwait.sh arm|mark and tests/cc_bastcensus.sh mark ran `dmesg -n 8`, raising console_loglevel to 8 so every mxfs pr_warn is pushed synchronously to each VM's EMULATED isa-serial console (backed by a host log file). run.sh's prep_cluster sets kernel.printk='1 4 1 1' precisely to avoid this; the mark harnesses silently reversed it. `dmesg -n 8` buys NOTHING for harvesting (printk always stores to the ring buffer; console level gates only the console). PROVEN A/B, same build, same virgin-fs recipe, only the console differs: loglevel 8 -> crash_consistency FAIL nodes_pass=0/32 90s/90s NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32 at hostload 11.08, with 7061 mxfs lines written to test1's host serial log; loglevel 1 -> PASS 32/32 79s/90s checks 204/204 at hostload 15.72 — the FAIL was at the LOWER host load. Fixed in tree: tests/quiet_console.sh exports $QUIET_CONSOLE which RE-ASSERTS printk='1 4 1 1'; both harnesses source it. sess126's 'ino 128 mean grant wait 3533 ms' was taken with `arm` (instr=1 AND console 8): its DIRECTION held up, its MAGNITUDE must not be quoted as a clean baseline. SECOND, THE PASS-BAR MEASUREMENTS ON THE QUIET RUN. (a) RcvbufErrors delta across the run = 0, dInErrors = 0, over 614803 datagrams, 32/32 nodes — BAR MET. defects.summary: A node writes the whole 16KB inode CLUSTER to its home location carrying stale images of slots it has no write tenure for
evidence: Captured 32/caw while rooting D-DIRENT-INODE-TYPE-MISMATCH. test30 held ino 10485888 in PR (P71-HOLD mode=3) and its writeback published P170-CLWR 10485888:40755:..6535 -- the PRE-FREE DIRECTORY image -- at realns 1785413079984065412, 2.5s AFTER test15 published the correct new REG incarnation 10485888:100644:..3492 at realns 1785413077486480010. A plain-bio read (P207-COHERENT-TRUTH) then showed the platter holding the pre-free image, i.e. a generation older than that inode's own free. Every P170-CLWR line shows the write unit is the whole cluster: 21+ ino:mode:gen triples per write.

SESS398 NEW INSTANCE OF THIS CLASS via a LOGGED slot: D-RELEASE-DRAIN-RELOGS-DEAD-INCARNATION-WITHOUT-TENURE-TYPEFLIP-398 — the release drain's P146V arm manufactured a tiny re-log transaction at held_mode=0 (after P-ICD-TENURE-REFUSE), the dead-incarnation dir slot became LOGGED, and the P218 per-slot filter (which only drops UN-logged passengers) wrote it over a peer's live file (test18 -> test27 ino 12590567, 0.23.6 lap 6, P56-DIRWRITE logged=1 relflush=1). Fixed at the source in 0.23.8 (mxfs_dlm_relog_authorized: no synthetic re-log without EX tenure). The RULE-5 ruling for -398 restates this entry's blocking_fix: the durable backstop is a tenure/epoch provenance token on every logged slot/publication so a stale publication FAILS rather than overwrites — not dlm_mode, not gen equality.
defects.mechanism: The PHYSICAL WRITE UNIT is the 16KB inode cluster, but the coherency protocol locks at INODE granularity. So a node writing one slot it does own republishes whatever it has cached for every neighbouring slot in the same cluster, including inodes a peer owns and has since modified or reallocated. Per the RULE-5 GPT consult (docs/rulings/publication-authority-and-lru-tenure.md): protection must be at least as coarse as the physical write unit, and a compare-and-write used only to manipulate the DLM record does not fence a subsequent ordinary metadata write. Checking ownership only at dirty/queue time is also insufficient -- already-submitted I/O must be drained before an EX downgrade, since an in-flight write can land after another node's commit.

defects.summary: readdir of a directory a peer created costs ~1.2 s per directory; every other syscall on the same inode costs milliseconds
defects.evidence: MEASURED 32/caw, build 0.11.243 C3D864E1F8AB80753D23D6C, tests/shared_unlink_pace.sh. 32 empty directories in one shared parent, each created by a different node which still holds it cached; then one pass from test1, one syscall class per fresh tree so nothing is confounded: stat 133 ms total (4 ms/op) | open(O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY) 1463 ms (45 ms/op) | rmdir 3846 ms (120 ms/op) | opendir+getdents (`ls -f`) 39701 ms (1240 ms/op). Independently reproduced standalone: 32 dirs, readdir-only pass = 37495 ms (1172 ms/op). CONTROL: the identical 32 children created LOCALLY by the same node and removed by it = 152 ms total (4 ms/op) -- so the shared parent is not the bottleneck and neither is the removal. RULE 0: native XFS readdir of an empty directory is microseconds; this is ~10^5x over the ceiling.
defects.mechanism: ROOT PROVEN (RULE 4 step 2b), build 0.11.245 6764F19681F7272375144DA. xfs/xfs_dir2_readdir.c:1005 -- `for (p48_try = 0; p48_try < 200 && dp->i_dlm_stale && !shutdown; p48_try++) { msleep(1); dp->i_dlm_stale = true; mxfs_dlm_reload_inode(dp, ..., true); }`. 200 x msleep(1) is ~1.2 s at this kernel's timer granularity, which is EXACTLY the observed cost and explains its stability (1201-1215 ms on every sample: the loop always runs its full bound). IT CAN NEVER SUCCEED ON THIS PATH: xfs_readdir holds ILOCK_SHARED across iteration, so the reload's write acquire is blocked by THIS task -- sess14 proved that and made mxfs_dlm_reload_inode bail immediately with P173-RELOAD-SELFREAD. It returns with i_dlm_stale still set, and the loop body re-arms the flag before each attempt, so all 200 rounds bail. P173 was the top probe in the capture (110 lines over 32 dirs = the ratelimited count of 200/dir). The loop's own comment ("ILOCK holds here are sub-ms so waiting is safe") is about OTHER holders; it does not cover the caller being the blocker, which is the case that actually occurs. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENTS: a phase-split probe on P62 showed mxfs_dlm_reload_inode itself costs tot_ms=0/pre_ms=0/bp_ms=0, so the cost is the sleeping, not the reload. Timed per syscall from python (a real open, not bash's `exec 9<` which returns EISDIR on a directory and made an earlier 45 ms 'open' row meaningless): stat=4ms open=0ms getdents=1202ms close=0ms. REFUTED en route: the pre-readdir wait loop at pal/linux/xfs_file.c:1888 -- its probe P95D-READDIR-WAIT is present in the module (strings) and fired ZERO times.

defects.summary: The heartbeat monitor overwrites a KNOWN nonzero cached victim incarnation with 0 when the sector reads 0, treating 'unknown' as an observation.  That is information loss, not an update: it launders an incarnation MISMATCH into the 'never observed' arm, so the next death round publishes a recovery that cannot name which incarnation it is recovering.
defects.evidence: MEASURED sess91 on the live 32-node rig.  With nt->last_epoch holding the victim's real incarnation 1634619062121349274, a sector whose epoch read 0 drove the epoch-change arm to rebase nt->last_epoch to 0 (disklock.c:1156 rebase_epoch, applied at :1358).  Round 1 correctly refused: 'P237-RECOV-INC-MISMATCH ... victim_inc=1634619062121349274 slot_inc=0 ... refusing to publish'.  Round 2, with the cached value now destroyed, took the opposite branch on the SAME facts: 'P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED slot=4 victim=4085327405 on-disk=0 — the caller never observed the victim's incarnation' and published 'P234-RECOV-FENCED ... epoch=0'.  The caller HAD observed it, 62 seconds earlier, and said so in the log.
defects.mechanism: dlm/disklock.c:1147 fires the epoch-change arm on any difference including a transition to 0; :1156 sets rebase_epoch = rhb->epoch unconditionally and :1358 commits it into nt->last_epoch.  There is no inc_valid() test on the incoming value, so 'known E1' + 'observed UNKNOWN' resolves to UNKNOWN instead of retaining E1 and flagging the sector as inconsistent.  A transition E1 -> E2 (both nonzero) may establish supersession under the sess86 rules; a transition E1 -> 0 cannot establish anything.  Related: the P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED text calls the sector 'the authority for which incarnation last owned this slice' — the sector is authoritative for SLOT state, but 0 is not an authoritative incarnation under inc_valid(); it is an authoritative statement that the incarnation is unavailable.
defects.containment: None.  Both branches log correctly and neither reports the downgrade, so the contradiction is only visible by reading the two rounds together.

defects.summary: CONFIRMED BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT (sess93).  A PREEMPT AND ABORT excludes the victim only at the INSTANT it completes.  Seconds later the same node re-registers with a fresh key and writes to the shared LUN — so for the entire duration of the foreign-slice replay that the fence certificate authorises, the only thing keeping a partitioned victim off the shared metadata is that victim's OWN cooperative self-fence.
evidence: STEP 1 baseline — victim writes LBA 131087 with 0xa5: rc=0, post-read matches.  The victim can write before the fence, so the rest of the probe is meaningful.

STEP 2 — test1 issues sg_persist --out --preempt-abort --param-rk=0x434d2436 --param-sark=0x37e3d796 --prout-type=5: rc=0, and READ KEYS then shows 0 descriptors matching 0x37e3d796.  The victim's registration is gone.

STEP 3 — victim writes LBA 131087 with 0x5a: rc=1, and the pre-read still shows a5 a5 a5...  REFUSED.  Exclusion genuinely works at that instant, which is what the certificate claims and all it claims.

STEP 4a — victim issues sg_persist --out --register-ignore --param-sark=0xfeed0001: rc=0.  THE TARGET ACCEPTED THE RE-REGISTRATION.  Nothing in SPC forbids REGISTER_AND_IGNORE from an unregistered initiator, and the WE-RO reservation does not prevent it.
STEP 4b — victim writes LBA 131087 with 0x33: rc=0, post-read '33 33 33 33 33 33 33 33'.  THE WRITE LANDED.  A node the cluster had just fenced put bytes on the shared LUN.

dlm/scsipr.c — MXFS's only defence is cooperative: mxfs_scsipr_self_check notices the key is gone and the node force-shuts-down (MXFS_FENCE_KIND_SELF_PREEMPTED / P131-SELF-FENCE, explicitly 'no auto-re-register').  That requires the victim's kernel to still be running and still scheduling — precisely what is in doubt about a node just declared dead by 62 s of missed heartbeats.

GPT RULE-5 ruling sess93, requirement B, which prompted the measurement: 'If a partitioned old node can simply register its key again, the certificate is only historical evidence and is not enough to protect replay.'
defects.mechanism: The certificate records a true fact with a SHELF LIFE, and nothing enforces the interval it is consumed over.  The window that matters is [certificate durable .. recovery published] — on the rig that is roughly 8 s of foreign log replay writing shared XFS metadata in place.  A victim that is alive but partitioned (CPU-starved, network-isolated, or simply slow enough to miss 31 heartbeat samples) is not obliged to notice anything: it re-registers on its next I/O retry and resumes writing into the same metadata the replayer is rebuilding. Acceptable enforcement per the ruling must sit BELOW ordinary filesystem writes: target ACL revocation for the victim's initiator, fabric/session revocation, or a membership protocol that blocks re-registration until recovery completes.  Making the self-fence faster or more reliable does NOT close it — any cooperative mechanism assumes the victim is healthy enough to cooperate, which is the assumption the fence exists to drop.

Two are viable and they are not exclusive: the temporary-WE gate (in-band, needs a cluster-wide freeze/drain protocol MXFS does not have — that protocol is the bulk of the work and should be scoped as its own unit), and a target/fabric fencing backend with a blocked state when it is absent (D-FENCE-CAPABILITY-UNVALIDATED-AT-MOUNT already requires the admission check that would detect its absence).  4) VERIFICATION, per the ruling: the acceptance test must keep the victim ALIVE and hostile — writing on both multipath paths with the old key, re-registering fresh keys and writing, unregistering and re-registering again, failing paths, and submitting writes before the transition so some are in flight — and must prove from traces that there is NO unreserved or WE-RO gap between the transition and publication, including during owner takeover.  Plus a negative test where the victim deliberately PREEMPTs the WE holder, to document the threat-model boundary.  tests/pr_reregister_probe.sh is the starting point: it already produces the fenced-and-still-running state that no criterion had ever produced. ===== Re-examined 2026-09-23 against the current tree. (a) MXFS itself registers only at mount: every PR REGISTER goes through scsipr_register_locked / scsipr_register_succeed_locked, reached only from mxfs_v5_dlm_init (dlm/v5_mount.c:16632, :17251) and its self-succession arm v5_self_succeed (:6731); the plain path refuses to register over any key already on the nexus (-EEXIST, P305-PR-PREDECESSOR-KEY-PRESENT) and the succession path returns -EBUSY once registered. A fenced incarnation therefore never re-registers; its self-check logs P-PR-ADVISORY 'own key gone' and does not re-register. (b) Measured on the 2/tcp rig (tests/evidence/tcp_peer_freeze_death/20260923T173420, dmesg_test2_after_resume.log): the frozen-then-fenced victim resumed with a writer running and its MXFS DID submit a log write and data writes after resume (queued before the freeze, cmd_age 2 s); the target bounced every one with RESERVATION CONFLICT because the victim was unregistered, and the victim shut down. The exclusion that held was the target's, not the victim's lease gate. (c) So the measured sess93 landing needs an out-of-band REGISTER (sg_persist from a root shell); the one MXFS-reachable variant still unmeasured is the SAME HOST mounting again (a new incarnation registering on the same I_T nexus) while the fenced incarnation's I/O is still queued in the block layer — the new registration would re-authorise that nexus. Next: a lap that freezes a victim with writes queued, lets the survivor fence and replay, resumes the victim and immediately remounts on it, then checks whether any pre-freeze write lands (pattern LBAs + post-replay chk_mxfs). Its outcome also decides this record's node reach, which is still the keyword sweep's. ===== Measured 2026-09-23 on Proxmox (0.89.80, QNAP), REMOUNT_ON_RESUME=1 lap of tests/tcp_peer_freeze_death.sh (tests/evidence/tcp_peer_freeze_death/20260923T202840): the same-host remount path EXISTS — 7 ms after resume, umount -l + mount made a NEW incarnation that registered a new key on the same nexus (P-PRKEY-REGISTERED keys=2) and rejoined (active_count=2) while the fenced incarnation still existed. Nothing old landed: the victim's in-flight file hashed identically on the survivor before resume and 30 s after (120ca0a6…, 1 MiB), and the old writeback of that file was bounced (reservation conflict, 'writeback error on inode 8388757'). NOT A CLEAN ANSWER: the QNAP also dropped the NEW registration after the resume's session disruption, so the new incarnation's own writes bounced and it shut down ~15 s later — the window this record is about (a live new key on the nexus while old I/O drains) was cut short by the target, not by MXFS. Next: repeat on a target that keeps registrations across session events (LIO on serv, 192.168.1.5), where the new key stays live; and the rejoined node had become lock master of the test directory, so the survivor then waited on a twice-dead master (P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE master=3315096614, lock requests failing at +80 s when the window closed) — whether that second death resolves like the first was not observed. ===== Observed after the lap window: the survivor resolved the twice-dead rejoined incarnation the same way as the first death — P238-FENCE-LURESET certified=1 kind=24 against node 3315096614 key 0xb90a72455bd2fbaa at 1400.4 s, TCP grace expiry at 1400.6 s, P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE at 1411.4 s, and a survivor write then succeeded (write_rc=0). ===== CORRECTION to the two 2026-09-23 notes above, from the victim's full kernel log: the REMOUNT_ON_RESUME laps did NOT create a new incarnation. 'umount -l' left the fenced incarnation's superblock alive and 'mount' re-attached that SAME instance in 7 ms (a real MXFS mount takes seconds; the boot scan alone is ~2.5 s): the LIO lap's victim log has exactly one DLM init / envelope / P-PRKEY-REGISTERED (the pre-freeze mount, gen=9, before the fence moved it to 0xa) and none after the resume (tests/evidence/tcp_peer_freeze_death/20260923T205907). The QNAP-lap lines read as a new mount were likewise the pre-freeze mount, stamped before the resumed guest's clock caught up (clocksource 'Long readout interval' 152 s). And there was ONE death per lap, not two: the QNAP-lap fence at 1398-1400 s survivor-time IS the +62 s mark (tests/evidence/tcp_peer_freeze_death/20260923T202840). After resume, in both the QNAP and the LIO lap, the peer rejected the fenced identity (P164-DEAD-REJECT announce/connect — retired identity ignored), the target bounced its writes (RESERVATION CONFLICT; on LIO the victim's key had been removed by a certified PREEMPT_ABORT_PROVEN_V1 at +66 s, generation 6->7), it self-fenced, and the survivor's copy of its in-flight file never changed. defects.summary: The 0.11.422 replay gate is enforced only by the code that runs it.  A pre-0.11.422 binary mounting the same filesystem still replays foreign slices ungated and still mints uncertified FENCED/NONE descriptors, so one old node in the cluster reinstates D-VICTIM-REPLAY-WITHOUT-PROVEN-EXCLUSION for every slice it is elected to replay.  A proto_gen bump alone does not prevent this.
evidence: GPT sess93 requirement A: 'Old binaries can still execute ungated replay and create FENCED/NONE descriptors.  A proto bump alone is insufficient if old and new nodes can mount together.'
0.11.422 retired mxfs_disklock_recovery_begin() in THIS build only; the same function in a deployed older build is unmodified and still writes stage=FENCED with fence_kind=NONE.

Existing uncertified FENCED/NONE records left on disk by older builds are refused by the new gate (mxfs_recov_cert_proves_exclusion -> 'fence_kind does not prove exclusion') but are not quarantined, so they persist as descriptors that block their slot forever with no operator-visible reason.

2026-08-04 sess131 — MECHANISM CHOSEN (next_step item 1 DISCHARGED) + RULE-5 RULING. CODE FACT: the mechanism already exists in-tree and was simply never applied to the 0.11.422 change. Three-layer C7 gate: (1) XFS_SB_FEAT_INCOMPAT_MXFS_PROTOGATE bit 30 (xfs/libxfs/xfs_format.h:412), set by mkfs_mxfs, in XFS_SB_FEAT_INCOMPAT_ALL — pre-gate kernels inherit upstream's unknown-incompat refusal (one-shot, preventative only); (2) envelope MXFS_FORMAT_F_PROTOGATE + cluster_proto_gen, enforced == MXFS_PROTO_GEN at pal/linux/xfs_super.c:3014-3029 with -EPROTONOSUPPORT plus a half-upgraded-format check; (3) disklock HB feature block — P-VERGATE-JOIN (-EPROTO) join refusal and monitor P-VERGATE-FENCE (dlm/disklock.c:1289, 2509). MXFS_PROTO_GEN is 3 (include/mxfs/mxfs_super.h:90); it went 1->2 at sess75 for recovery-descriptor v2 and 2->3 at sess86 for the nonzero mount incarnation. THE 0.11.422 CERTIFIED-REPLAY GATE DID NOT BUMP IT, so a pre-0.11.422 / post-incarnation binary is gen 3, is admitted by all three layers, and performs exactly the ungated replay this entry describes. The sess74 ruling quoted at include/mxfs/mxfs_super.h:56-88 and dlm/disklock.h:293-304 applies verbatim: per-record fail-closed is no substitute because the old replayer REPLAYS FIRST and consults the descriptor only afterwards. RULE-5 RULING (sess131, gpt-5.6-sol; full text in docs/rulings/protogen4-and-quarantine.md): MXFS_PROTO_GEN 3->4 is APPROVED and REQUIRED — the certified-replay rule is a cluster protocol generation change even though the descriptor encoding is byte-identical, because the set of permitted participants and writes changed. FOUR MANDATORY BLOCKERS before this entry may close: (B1) recovery must be unreachable until envelope admission — a gen-3 kernel could begin foreign replay before discovering the envelope says 4, and layer 3 cannot repair replay that already happened; require an immutable proto_admitted mount-state bit asserted at EVERY recovery entry point, and audit normal mount, remount/retry, partial-mount error recovery, deferred recovery workers, mount-time XFS journal recovery callbacks, snapshot/secondary-sb paths, and administrative recover-only entry points. (B2) 3->4 must be an OFFLINE CLUSTER TRANSITION, not an offline metadata write: an already-mounted or suspended gen-3 node does not reread the envelope and may resume and replay before the gen-4 monitor fences it — stop/unmount every member, take an exclusive maintenance/storage lease, revoke/preempt all old PR registrations, invalidate the old membership epoch, and keep suspended nodes off the LUN until remount. (B3) the generation update must be a crash-safe activation transaction: all authoritative envelope copies written with FUA/flush, an unambiguous interrupted-upgrade state, and readers FAIL CLOSED on disagreement rather than picking an older valid copy. (B4) gen 4 names a BEHAVIORAL CONTRACT — certified-replay check, descriptor-write restrictions and mount ordering are conformance requirements for any build claiming 4, with mixed-build tests proving every gen-3 build is rejected BEFORE recovery starts. ROLLOUT: 'accept N and N-1 read-only' is REJECTED as unsafe — a read-only mount may still perform journal recovery and foreign replay IS mount-time recovery. Hard refusal is the correct default. LIMITATION that must be written into the upgrade procedure: the bump is PROSPECTIVE; it does not prove no gen-3 node already performed an ungated replay, and the ABSENCE of a stale FENCED/NONE descriptor is not proof of safety because an unsafe replay may have completed and been purged. Finding legacy or suspicious recovery records must trigger scrub/fsck and an operator-visible 'previously exposed to ungated replay' status.

2026-08-04 sess131 — QUARANTINE DESIGN (next_step item 2) RULED UNSOUND AS PROPOSED. I proposed that any survivor durably set MXFS_RECOV_F_QUARANTINED (dlm/disklock.h:357) on a legacy uncertified FENCED/NONE descriptor, since today such a descriptor merely fails mxfs_recov_cert_proves_exclusion() with reason 'fence_kind does not prove exclusion' (dlm/disklock.c:3483) and blocks its slot forever with no operator-visible reason. REJECTED. (B5) 'one-way and strictly more restrictive' is NOT a substitute for write authority: a survivor can hold a stale sector image and race the victim's heartbeat update, a recovery owner advancing or replacing the descriptor, a purge or reuse for a NEW incarnation, another survivor becoming owner, or a sector-level read-modify-write over unrelated fields — overwriting newer state, quarantining a REUSED slot, or corrupting the CRC-protected sector. (B6) a survivor must not write the victim's sector before the victim is excluded; proven exclusion is required for ANY survivor-side descriptor mutation unless an independent atomic quarantine location exists that the victim never writes. Owner-only quarantine is acceptable ONLY with ownership acquired via the existing owner/epoch protocol, identity + incarnation + sequence + expected-old-contents revalidated at commit, the same durable/conditional serialization as other descriptor advances, and victim-sector write safety already established. OTHERWISE the correct runtime behavior is: refuse replay, leave the descriptor UNCHANGED, and publish a persistent health event / named rate-limited alert. (B7) no disposition or repair model exists yet for legacy obligations — an unmarked blocked descriptor is NOT equivalent to a quarantined one, because the unmarked one can still be repaired by future software while the terminal flag forbids it; choose ONE policy first: permanent abandonment, certified reconstruction (fresh certified exclusion, revalidate identity/incarnation and journal state AFTER exclusion, build a NEW recovery transaction, never bless the old NONE descriptor), or offline administrative discharge. DO NOT add a generic clear-quarantine operation. UPGRADER: chk_mxfs --upgrade-protogate should INVENTORY AND REPORT, not auto-quarantine — scan all descriptor locations and redundant copies, classify each, emit a durable report naming slot/victim identity/incarnation/stage/reason, and offer leave-unresolved-and-activate, an explicit destructive --quarantine-legacy, or a designed reconstruction. (B8) it must NEVER synthesize a fence certificate because the tool believes the cluster is offline; administrative offline status is not proof the victim was excluded at the relevant time. Explicitly REJECTED: refusing the whole generation upgrade whenever a NONE descriptor exists — leaving the volume at gen 3 preserves an old binary's ability to mount and replay ungated, which is strictly worse.
defects.mechanism: Needs one of: an offline all-node upgrade procedure; a cluster feature bit that old versions refuse to mount against; mount-time protocol negotiation that rejects unsafe members; or a format transition old binaries cannot write.  Separately, legacy uncertified descriptors must be explicitly quarantined (MXFS_RECOV_F_QUARANTINED exists already) rather than silently refused forever.

defects.summary: The CAW slot records lock requests as ONE BIT PER NODE, but a node can have more than one local acquire attempt outstanding for the same resource. The bit therefore cannot say WHICH local request it represents. An attempt that gives up clears `waiters`/`waiters_ex` (and its giveup-mode holder bit) on behalf of the whole node, destroying the on-disk request of a DIFFERENT, still-live local attempt — and the same ambiguity misdirects direct-handoff nomination, which can only name 'node N'.
defects.evidence: 32/caw census on 0.11.440 (tests/census_p.sh, 27 of 32 nodes reporting, sess110 board still in the ring buffer): P3A-DEMOTER-SLOWACQ = 0, P6H-ABORT-RECONCILE = 0, 'disk lock acquisition timed out' = 0, P-CAWEXH = 0, P91-CLAIMEXH = 0 on EVERY node, against ~970 P6H-ADOPT per node. So the reconcile arm is never entered under a healthy board and the collision is unobserved — reachable by construction, not by measurement. RULE 6 forbids closing on rarity. GPT (sess111) named this independently as a defect distinct from the holder-adoption race of blocker 6: 'A single waiter bit cannot represent two concurrent local requests, and reg_gen/reg_epoch do not identify which request a handoff satisfies.'
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:2318 caw_drop_own_waiter() CASes `waiters &= ~node_bit; waiters_ex &= ~node_bit;` plus `holders[giveup_mode] &= ~node_bit`, keyed on ctx->node_bit alone — there is no attempt identity anywhere in the slot format or in the call. Three call sites, all post-giveup: grant-wait timeout (dlm_caw.c:3346), claim-exhaustion (4990), convert-exhaustion (6479). Concurrent same-node attempts on ONE resource are possible by design: AG acquires are serialized by pag->pag_dlm_acquire_lock and inode acquires by the MXFS_DLM_ISTATE_ACQUIRING park in mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28138), but the demoter is EXEMPT from that park (!mxfs_is_demoter(ip) at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28141 and 28415) because the BAST drain's trailing xfs_irele must self-reenter. The tree already carries the probe P3A-DEMOTER-SLOWACQ (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28433) labelled in-source as 'the prime suspect for the same-node concurrent-request collision'.

Sequence: A joins EX; demoter B joins EX; B times out and defers holder-clear as owed; B leaves; A is GRANTED EX and publishes tenure[EX]=1; A's own lreq_finish then runs the owed pass and clears A's EX bit.  (B) the plan is snapshotted ONCE and then used across a loop of up to 1000 iterations x 8ms backoff plus disk I/O -- many seconds -- so a plan computed when others==0 && tenure==0 authorizes clearing a bit that became load-bearing later.  The disk CAW serializes against other DISK writers, not against publication of a LOCAL tenure.  (C) [GPT, missed by my own audit] simply passing e to the deferred pass is ALSO wrong: lreq_plan computes others = attempts-1 assuming the caller is still counted, but the deferred pass runs after lreq_finish decremented, so a thread C joining in between is subtracted as if it were the caller and the plan concludes others==0 -- authorized to clear C's bits.  NEXT (implementation, sess114): the exclusion actually required reduces to CANCELLING-vs-JOIN, which is far smaller than the ruling's full 6-state machine -- and TWO CODE FACTS VERIFIED THIS SESSION make the reduction sound.  FACT 1: adoption happens inside caw_wait_for_grant (dlm_caw.c:3348 P6H-ADOPT), which runs ON THE ATTEMPTING THREAD -- there is no callback thread that adopts on an attempt's behalf, so the ruling's hole 2 (one attempt with competing adopt/cancel control paths) is INAPPLICABLE here: for a given attempt, adopt and cancel are the same thread, sequentially.  FACT 2: waiters_ex is set at dlm_caw.c:5292 and :6921 under exactly (mode == EX || mode == PW), which is exactly mxfs_mode_can_write(), so the `writers` counter's mode->bitmap invariant HOLDS (use the predicate at those two setter sites so they can never drift).  THE DESIGN: (1) add `uint8_t op` to struct mxfs_caw_lreq (NONE/CANCELLING/RELEASING) plus a ctx-level condvar; (2) caw_drop_own_waiter claims CANCELLING AND computes the plan IN THE SAME CRITICAL SECTION; (3) lreq_join waits for op==NONE before counting the attempt or issuing anything on disk; (4) therefore `others` cannot grow while CANCELLING is owned, and the only case in which anything is cleared is others==0 -- the canceller is the sole live local attempt and no new one can appear; (5) lreq_finish's deferred pass claims CANCELLING IN THE SAME CRITICAL SECTION that takes attempts to 0 (no unlocked window for C to slip into) and passes an explicit self_joined=false so it does not subtract a thread that is not itself.  NO DEADLOCK: a canceller waits only on disk I/O, never on another local thread, so a demoter blocked behind CANCELLING cannot close a cycle -- unlike the ACQUIRING park, which is precisely why the demoter exemption exists.  Bound the join-side wait and fire a probe if it ever exceeds ~100ms.  THEN the RULE-6 closure test, which a healthy board CANNOT provide: sess111 measured P6H-ABORT-RECONCILE=0, P3A-DEMOTER-SLOWACQ=0 and zero acquire timeouts on every one of 32 nodes, so the reconcile arm is never entered under a passing board.  Build a DETERMINISTIC exerciser (a debugfs trigger under mp->m_debugfs -- idiom at xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:43024 -- driving the registry against a REAL slot on the REAL LUN) that replays sequences A, B and C and asserts the holder bit SURVIVES, plus a NEGATIVE CONTROL (single attempt gives up => the bit IS cleared) without which 'the bit survived' cannot be distinguished from 'the test never ran'.

defects.summary: caw_drop_own_waiter() gives up after 1000 CAS attempts (or on the first hard I/O error, or on a slot read error) and RETURNS NORMALLY. Its callers then return -ETIMEDOUT to the filesystem and the mount continues in normal service with a possibly-leaked waiter or holder bit on the shared LUN. A leaked EX waiter bit has ALREADY caused a measured cluster-wide wedge, so silent exhaustion cannot be treated as successful cleanup.

defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:2318 caw_drop_own_waiter(): `for (attempt = 0; attempt < 1000; attempt++)` with backoff capped at 8 ms; `break` on read error, on magic mismatch, on any non-EAGAIN caw_slot() error, and on loop exhaustion. defects.summary: The node-local record of which locks this mount holds (ctx->held) is published AFTER a grant has already been recognised and removed BEFORE a release is known to have landed, and it carries no mode, no attempt identity and no conversion state. Every correctness decision that reads it as 'not tracked therefore not held' can therefore act on a live tenure. The direct-handoff adopt arm makes this concrete: it validates the slot image, then calls track_held() — an observe-to-track window in which a concurrent cleanup sees nothing tracked and clears the very holder bit being adopted.
defects.evidence: The in-source doc for is_tracked_held() (dlm_caw.c:2016) itself states the property is only 'in steady state ctx->held mirrors our on-disk holder bits exactly'. GPT sess111: 'A flat slot/mode array documented as matching disk state in steady state is tracking or telemetry, not necessarily authoritative synchronization' — it has an observe-to-track window, track/untrack ordering windows, no attempt identity, no local reference count, no conversion-transition representation, and incomplete state after overflow. The overflow direction is already documented as asymmetric at dlm_caw.h:450: 'Declining to reclaim leaks slots; purging a live hold corrupts.'
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:1982 track_held() records a SLOT INDEX only (no mode), scanning ctx->held.slots[] under ctx->held.lock; dlm_caw.c:2120 untrack_held() removes it. Six track sites (2102, 2915, 3204, 4110, 4727, 7953/7979) and seven untrack sites (4211, 4326, 5184, 5556, 6233, 6250, 6625). In the adopt arm (dlm_caw.c:2823) validation happens against cur_slot and track_held() is called at 2915, with no lock held across the pair. ctx->held additionally has a STICKY overflow latch (dlm_caw.h:453 held_overflow) which, once set, leaves tracking permanently incomplete for the mount's life and today only disables one consumer (the post-recovery settle purge, MXFS_CAW_PURGE_SKIP_TRACKED).

defects.summary: The give-up reconcile clears this node's waiter/holder bits at a REMEMBERED slot index without ever checking that the slot still holds the resource it was remembered for. A slot that was tombstoned and re-claimed for a DIFFERENT resource in the meantime carries our node bit as a live registration for THAT resource — and the reconcile cancels it.
defects.evidence: Line-level: the pre-sess112 function body read the slot, tested magic, and went straight to the bit clears with no memcmp against `resource` — and the function did not even take a resource argument, so the check was not merely omitted, it was unrepresentable. The three call sites are the grant-wait timeout, claim-retry exhaustion and convert exhaustion.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c caw_drop_own_waiter(ctx, slot_idx, giveup_mode) validated only `cur_slot->magic == MXFS_CAW_MAGIC` before CASing `waiters &= ~node_bit; waiters_ex &= ~node_bit; holders[giveup_mode] &= ~node_bit`. Live magic is satisfied by ANY live slot, including one now owned by an unrelated resource. Two of the three call sites make this reachable: the grant-wait timeout passes a slot index captured up to a full acquire timeout earlier (MXFS_CAW_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS, liveness-extended), and the claim-exhaustion site passes whatever index the last retry happened to leave in slot_idx — an index the acquire may never have registered on at all. CAW slots are recycled through the tombstone path, so the index is not a stable identity for the resource.

That direction is right but sess113 RULE-5 found the disposition wrong and the debt model structurally broken.  (1) IDENTITY MISMATCH IS NOT DISCHARGE: `if (resource mismatch) { rc = 0; break; }` means 'the remembered location is stale', NOT 'the obligation is complete'.  Recorded debt must survive a mismatch, retarget via a canonical lookup, or escalate.  (2) A SINGLE owed_slot is structurally wrong: several give-ups on one resource can remember DIFFERENT slot indices (the resource moves after a tombstone+reclaim; the claim-exhaustion caller's index is a probe position it may never have registered on), so a later debt silently overwrites an earlier one -- and losing an old waiters_ex clear recreates the measured 16-node wedge. (4) A claim-exhaustion probe position the node never registered on should not become HOLDER debt at all. (5) memcmp on struct mxfs_resource_id is only safe if it has no padding and is canonically initialised -- verify, else compare fieldwise.

Board cell: `FAIL rsync_paired nodes_pass=0/32 states:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED=9,FAIL=23 hostload=21.24 first_fail[test1:checks=6 passed=2 failed=4] faildist[0x9,1x15,4x8] steps[rsync barrier ready=9]` [60s/60s]. rank1's own reason, straight from rsync's stderr: `rsync: [receiver] mkstemp "/mnt/shared/.rsync_paired/node1/d1/.file40.ibjm7M" failed: Invalid exchange (52)` and `rsync: [receiver] mkstemp "/mnt/shared/.rsync_paired/node1/d1/.file5.y8aWuq" failed: Input/output error (5)`, with rc=23, file count exp=400 got=0, content sum exp=23a2d8970f1d3bfae523c69a993401ca got=d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e (i.e. NOTHING transferred). errno 52 on Linux is EBADE, and in this tree -EBADE has exactly ONE meaning: SCSI RESERVATION CONFLICT (dlm/disklock.h:926 'CAS bounces with SCSI RESERVATION CONFLICT (-EBADE)', dlm/v5_mount.h:748, dlm/scsipr.c:569 'D1 (EBADE on write = fencing event)', pal/linux/kern.c:4322 'ret = -EBADE'). Invariant 4 is literally violated today: the losing instance's mxfs_inode_relcert_finish unconditionally writes MXFS_RELSTATE_ACTIVE over the winner's RELEASING (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~15040) — currently harmless only because rel_state is telemetry-only (sess306 grep: no control-flow reader).

defects.mechanism: Per the sess305 GPT ruling (docs/rulings/p283-per-instance-proof-cert.md), duplicate concurrent releases must satisfy: (1) winner-only handoff publication; (2) dup-safe ancillary effects (P6H handoff, epoch bumps, orphan-bit writes); (3) full tenure identity in the wire CAS compare (not just gen); (4) loser's finish must not reset winner state; (5) certificate emission must not cross-contaminate; (6) requeue/strand re-arm must be idempotent under overlap; (7) diagnostic counters must not double-count. None has a targeted test; only (4) has been code-audited (violated, telemetry-only).

defects.summary: Cluster-wide superblock lost-update: each node keeps its OWN in-core m_sb and every SB transaction logs the WHOLE superblock buffer (xfs_log_sb serializes the logger's m_sb over the entire sector), so any peer's SB txn -- including routine lazy icount/ifree/fdblocks counter sync at log cover/unmount -- overwrites another node's persistent non-counter SB changes with the logger's stale copy. Runtime SB mutators are per-node and uncoordinated: feature adds (xfs_add_attr proven live on the rig pre-0.13.3 via first xattr-bearing create, quota flag adds, log_incompat/LARP), growfs geometry, label/UUID set, NEEDSREPAIR. Concrete proven instance (sess353, #94 root): node A's lazy ATTRBIT add was carried in its slice while every peer's m_sb lacked it; beyond causing the #94 false refusal, any peer's subsequent whole-SB log would have durably REVERTED A's versionnum change. 0.13.3 closes only the ATTRBIT arm (mkfs presets 0xB4B5 + cluster mount refuses !xfs_has_attr); every other whole-SB producer remains an uncoordinated multi-writer over one shared sector. GPT ruling: containment for the current profile is to FORBID ALL runtime non-counter SB mutations in cluster mode, rejecting BEFORE mutating m_sb; any future coordination protocol must cover EVERY whole-SB producer, not just feature-changing txns. Evidence: docs/history/94-attrbit-root-and-fix-0133.md; sess353 transcript (GPT ruling item 4).

The cause is structural, not statistical: d_time is stamped in exactly ONE place (pal/linux/xfs_super.c, the ret==1 tail of the coordinated validation) and the affine fast path RETURNS BEFORE REACHING IT, so a dentry taking that exit is never stamped, keeps d_time=0, and can never equal an epoch that starts at 1 (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:38672 sets i_dlm_epoch=1 for exactly that reason). A P165 line naming a SPECIFIC name/ino still places an affine fast-path blessing of that name at that moment, which may remain useful as a positional fact, but it is NOT evidence that the dentry was stale.  0.65.0 fixes the probe to fire only when d_time != 0 && d_time != epoch — a dentry that DID pass coordinated validation at one epoch being blessed under another, which is the real resurrection signature — and counts the fresh population separately as P165-AFFINE-FRESH so the denominator stays visible. defects.summary: A terminal refusal quarantine PERMANENTLY occupies one disklock heartbeat slot (its RECOVERY_GUARD record is the durable verdict, so it must stay). The number of usable slots is the volume's log-slice count. On a cluster formatted with exactly as many slices as nodes -- which is the default (tests/setup/prep_fs.sh MXFS_LOG_SLICES=32) and what the 32-node rig runs -- there is then NO free slot, and the recovered node CANNOT MOUNT AT ALL: 'disklock: no free heartbeat slot in 0..31 -- the volume has 32 log slices ... Cluster is full; reformat with more slices (mkfs_mxfs -n) to admit more nodes' -> claim_slot -28 -> 'MXFS DLM init failed - aborting mount'. One refused slice therefore costs the cluster a node PERMANENTLY, and the operator is told to REFORMAT when the actual state is a quarantine awaiting repair. ESCALATED WITHIN THE SESSION, TWICE: (1) 32 IS A HARD CAP, not a default -- 'mkfs.mxfs: -n must be 1-32 (XFS caps the internal log at 2GiB-10MiB, so at most 32 ~64MB per-node slices fit; the slice count is the cluster's hard node limit for this filesystem)'. So at the maximum supported cluster size there is NO formatting option that leaves headroom, and the mount error's own advice ('reformat with more slices') is impossible to follow. (2) There is NO IMPLEMENTED REPAIR PATH. The quarantine message says 'needs operator repair + remount', but no tool and no knob clears a quarantined RECOVERY_GUARD record: chk_mxfs (-a/-y/-U) does not touch it, caw_slotdump is read-only, and the only in-kernel clear-to-EMPTY path is the clean-release CAS, which refuses any record that is not the caller's own live record. The only way to free the slot is mkfs_mxfs -f -- a reformat, i.e. total data loss, which also destroys the verdict the quarantine exists to preserve. Net effect: one refused slice permanently reduces a 32-node cluster to 31 nodes with no recovery short of rebuilding the filesystem.

defects.mechanism: PROVEN, code + platter. dlm/disklock.c claim path: when no free slot is found and ctx->slot_limit < MXFS_DISKLOCK_HB_SLOTS it returns -ENOSPC with the 'reformat with more slices' message; slot_limit is the volume's xfs_log_node_count (struct mxfs_ondisk_super, byte offset 96) because a slot beyond the slice count would have no journal. The quarantined slot is not free: its sector is a MXFS_DISKLOCK_FLAG_RECOVERY_GUARD (=3) record and recov_desc_present() requires exactly that flag, so the record IS the durable verdict every closure gate reads. Keeping it is correct -- the defect is the interaction: usable slots = slice count, and nothing reserves headroom for the verdict records a refusal will create. Measured on the rig: platter super says max_nodes=64 but log_slices=32, so slots 0..31 only; with 32 nodes mounted the table is 32/32 occupied; after a refusal the table is 31 live + 1 GUARD, still 32/32, and the rejoining node aborts its mount.

defects.summary: When MXFS cannot prove it retired its own PR registration at unmount, it LOGS AND CARRIES ON. The 0.14.11 fix makes the failure detectable (P301-PR-AUTHORITY-NOT-RETIRED / P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE) but nothing acts on it: the node finishes unmounting while its initiator may still be registered on the shared LUN, and no survivor is told. The RULE-5 ruling was explicit that this is not sufficient -- 'verify and log is not enough. The load-bearing invariant is that membership departure and PR authority retirement are coupled by either successful verification or an authorized fail-closed recovery action.' A stale registration on a LIVE initiator nexus can authorize non-filesystem I/O to the shared device even though MXFS is unmounted.
defects.evidence: Code state on 0.14.11 (the fail-closed branch simply does not exist), plus the sess377 rig observation that a pre-fix leftover key persisted across a complete 32-node clean unmount with no cluster-side reaction of any kind. The RULE-5 ruling text is in docs/rulings/3-pr-unregister-leak-fix-shape.md.
defects.mechanism: THREE GAPS, all present in 0.14.11. (a) NO FAIL-CLOSED ACTION. pal/linux/xfs_super.c's late unregister raises xfs_alert P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE and returns; put_super continues and the mount goes away. Nothing isolates the initiator sessions that could still use the registration, nothing self-fences, and no durable record hands the problem to an authorized survivor. (b) NO SERIALIZATION AGAINST RE-REGISTRATION. defects.summary: A node takes a metadata READ error on a healthy, freshly-mkfs'd cluster and shuts the filesystem down, which cascades: every other node's coherency checks against its data then fail. test22 hit 'Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at xfs_trans_read_buf_map+0x178 (xfs/xfs_trans_buf.c:313)' inside an inode create, declared voluntary death, and turned a green board red.
evidence: TIMELINE on a common wall clock derived from matched uptime<->realns pairs (dmesg -T and btime+uptime were ~5 s apart between these two nodes and INVERTED this ordering on the first attempt, so they are not usable here): 04:20:29.399Z test22 'XFS (dm-1): Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at xfs_trans_read_buf_map+0x178/0x320 [mxfs] (/src/mxfs/xfs/xfs_trans_buf.c:313). Shutting down filesystem.' -> P-WITHDRAW-QUEUE -> P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP slot=11 node=3671298124. 04:20:29.871Z test5 P236-FENCE-INTENT slot=11 victim=3671298124, i.e. 472 ms LATER. The fence is a CONSEQUENCE of the withdrawal, not its cause - the withdraw stamp is what tells peers to fence, so the fence cannot precede its own trigger.

The error surfaced inside an inode create: 'P-CREATE-ERR2 dir_create_child err=-5 t_dfops_empty=1 dp_ino=41943175 new_ino=46137488' then 'P-CR3-CANCEL error=-5 dp_ino=41943175 dialloc_ino=46137488 new_ino=46137488 trans_dirty=1 comm=bash', followed by three P-AGMETA-RECLAIM drops (xfs_agi, xfs_finobt, xfs_inobt).

Post-shutdown, reads of the same inodes report 'P9-ICD-MIDLOOP ino=46137487 imap_rc=-5 bp=0 plainrd_rc=0 magic=0x494e ... shutdown=1' - the PLAIN read of that location succeeds and carries a valid XFS_DINODE_MAGIC while the imap path returns -EIO. Those lines are AFTER the shutdown so the EIO there is expected; the valid magic is recorded only because it argues the on-platter content was intact.

BOARD IMPACT: cache_coherency FAILED nodes_pass=0/32 faildist[8x27,9x4,13x1] - 27 nodes failed 8 checks each, which are the cross-node checks against the departed node's data, so the coherency failure is the cascade rather than an independent fault. strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency and zero_silent_loss then all reported 'pre-assert: mxfs not mounted/readable on test22'. A re-prep and re-run of the identical chunk on the identical build passed 8/8, so the trigger is intermittent - which under RULE 6 is a reason to instrument, never to dismiss.

NOT caused by the sess378 fence change: that change is confined to mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_preempt() with abort=true, which runs only in the fence path, and test22 logged no fence activity before its shutdown. A UNIT ATTENTION was seen on test22 (P-FUA-READ-RETRY lba=194241 ret=0x2 resid=8192 key=0x6 try=1) but only AFTER the shutdown, consistent with test5's subsequent preemption.

A SECOND, DIFFERENT shutdown the same session, recorded as a lead rather than a claim: test5 shut down at 04:00:50Z with 'Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at mxfs_dlm_fence_notify+0x53/0x80' - a SELF-FENCE on PR-key-lost - during a 32-node mass unmount, while the fleet was still running 0.14.11. Whether the two share a root is unknown.

defects.mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED. What the evidence orders: (1) a directory's live dirents become unfindable in its data blocks on this node while the scan still counts them (P26-DSCAN-MISS reports scanned=127..135 with ndb=1, i.e. the scan saw >=135 live dirents but the single data block did not contain the name it was looking for); (2) DLM inode acquires on unrelated inodes start returning -EAGAIN; (3) a create's transaction is cancelled DIRTY with -EUCLEAN, which is a structure-integrity verdict, not an I/O error. defects.summary: Three fail-OPEN arms in the consumers of an on-disk TERMINAL recovery-outcome record, found by finally running the sess333 RULE-5 pre-rig unit checks against the real LUN. (A) mxfs_v5_dlm_recovery_scan_outcomes() is a FOURTH import site that performs NO validation: a crc-valid record with outcome=99 (not TERMINAL_REFUSED) was imported as a real AG-scoped verdict and also fed v5_closure_note_terminal(), which authorizes the selective grant purge. sess334 item B deduped three sites behind mxfs_freplay_import_verdict(); this one was missed. (B) mxfs_disklock_recovery_read_outcome() has NO fs_gen gate and the scan iterates all 64 slots blind, so a PRE-MKFS GHOST sector quarantines the freshly-formatted filesystem. mkfs does not reliably zero the disklock region on this target stack, so surviving GUARD sectors are EXPECTED and hb_gen_foreign is exactly the mechanism meant to make them harmless. (C) an FSWIDE quarantine imported by the registration scan does NOT refuse the mount: the barrier's two unconditional FSWIDE gates both run ~0.5s BEFORE the scan, so the mount ADMITS a zombie whose every operation fails EIO -- precisely what xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:48457 says must never happen. Arm C needs no forgery in principle: any legitimate FSWIDE verdict published between the barrier's sweep and registration -- the late-mount case the scan was BUILT for -- admits the same zombie.
defects.evidence: All shapes forged into unused HB slot 40 with tools/recov_forge (SCSI READ(16)/WRITE(16)+FUA, real crc32c identity binding), then test32 unmounted and remounted; sector re-read and compared by crc32c. FAIL (3): ghost/ghost-fswide/ghost-badkind (fs_gen=0xdeadbeef vs live 0x176ec8e4) -> 'P241-RECOV-TERMINAL-SCAN slot=40 victim=4242/7 reason=1 domain=2 ag_mask=0x1 seq=1 -- existing terminal refusal found at registration; importing' + 'P240-QUAR-IMPORT victim_slot=40 fswide=0 ag_mask=0x1' on all three, including the outcome=99 one whose logged reason/domain are the record's raw bytes. late-fswide (CORRECT live fs_gen, stage=5 GRANTS_RELEASED so the barrier's sweep skips it, crc-valid FSWIDE TERMINAL_REFUSED) -> 'P241-RECOV-TERMINAL-SCAN ... importing', 'P240-QUAR-IMPORT victim_slot=40 fswide=1', **mount rc=0 wall=7s -- ADMITTED**. Ordering measured from the `valid` run's dmesg: classify+import at 6318.75, P240-QUAR-REFUSE comm=mount at 6319.26, P241-RECOV-TERMINAL-SCAN at 6319.32 -- the scan is ~0.5s AFTER the barrier. No node took a filesystem shutdown in any shape; the other 31 nodes stayed mounted throughout.
defects.mechanism: Consumers of mxfs_recov_outcome and their scrutiny, measured 0.19.5: (1) disklock monitor (disklock.c ~1430) -- gated on hb_still_dead_stamp, fires the cb only if oc->outcome == TERMINAL_REFUSED; no check of reason/victim_slot/ag_mask, and the outcome-kind prefilter is itself a bypass (an outcome=99 record is silently skipped every pass, so a quarantined slot never quarantines any live peer -- the D-513 park/timeout shape returns). (2) registration scan (v5_mount.c:6916) -- loops 0..63, calls read_outcome, and on rc==0 calls v5_closure_note_terminal(ctx,slot,&oc) + quar_cb(data,slot,&oc) with NO validation at all. (3) shared classifier (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:47038 -> mxfs_freplay_import_verdict:46941) -- the ONLY validating path; rejects wrong outcome kind, unknown reason, bad domain, empty AG mask, oc->victim_slot != slot. The mount admission barrier builds its cut from get_recovery_pending_slots(), which SKIPS hb_gen_foreign records and stage >= GRANTS_RELEASED records; everything in the cut goes through the validating classifier, so the barrier is correct. The scan is what bypasses it, and it runs AFTER the barrier.

defects.mechanism: SESS482 CANDIDATE ARM (e), FROM SOURCE, NOT FROM A REPRODUCTION — THE UNMOUNT AG-RELEASE PATH DOES NOT RUN THE DRAIN PIPELINE, AND THIS RECORD'S SYMPTOM IS "AFTER A CLEAN FLEET UNMOUNT". Arms (a)-(d) are all about REPLAY; none of them looks at what unmount itself does, and that is where the divergence is observed. The facts, each verified by reading the code rather than inferred: (1) mxfs_dlm_ag_force_release_all (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~49924) is the unmount release. Between the top of its per-AG loop and its mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock at ~49970 it runs exactly ONE drain -- mxfs_dlm_ag_drain_alloc_buflist at ~49940 -- and then two cancel_work_syncs and a state-flag block. (2) The COOPERATIVE release path (~49457 to its unlock at ~49710) runs NINE steps first: drain_alloc_buflist, drain_inode_buffers, blkdev_flush_epoch, drain_meta_buffers, blkdev_flush_epoch, xfs_log_force(XFS_LOG_SYNC), a SECOND drain_meta_buffers (the sess43 fix), a bounded meta_pending wait for in-flight bios, and a final flush. The unmount path omits eight of the nine. (3) mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock (dlm/v5_mount.c ~15071) is a PURE release primitive -- a TCP unlock or a CAW slot CAS with a release gate -- so nothing internal covers the omission. (4) ORDERING: the call is made from pal/linux/xfs_super.c:2066 inside xfs_fs_put_super, and xfs_unmountfs -- which is where the synchronous log quiesce, AIL push and buftarg drain happen -- is at line 2175 of the SAME function. Nothing between the top of put_super and 2066 pushes the AIL or forces the log. So the AG grants are published as free BEFORE this node's metadata is pushed to its final on-platter home. (5) The cooperative path's own sess43 comment states the consequence of skipping exactly the step this path skips: the just-dirtied AG-meta buffers -- "AGI (agi_unlinked / freecount), AGF (freeblks), inobt/finobt" -- are "left in-core-ahead-of-disk at unlock ... so the peer's FUA read at acquire MISSES them -> stale-behind AGI unlinked-list head ... -> xfs_iunlink_remove_inode corruption + shutdown". THAT IS THIS RECORD'S SYMPTOM, ITEM FOR ITEM: an AGI freecount disagreeing with the inobt/finobt on the platter, plus an orphan still chained in an AGI unlinked bucket with mode 0 gen 0. (6) A second, independent hazard on the same path, and possibly the sharper one: after the grant is released at 2066, xfs_unmountfs at 2175 pushes THIS node's AIL. If a peer acquired the AG in that window and modified the AG-meta, our later writeback durably REVERTS the peer's change -- the same durable-clobber shape b_mxfs_relepoch exists to prevent for directory blocks. Note the asymmetry that makes it worse: the cooperative release records pag_mxfs_rel_epoch from pag_mxfs_grant_epoch before zeroing it (~39140), whereas the unmount path zeroes pag_mxfs_grant_epoch (~49956) WITHOUT setting pag_mxfs_rel_epoch, so the retiring-token guards that read it (xfs/xfs_inode.c ~8531, ~10051, gated on rel_epoch != 0) are inert on this path. WHY THIS WAS NOT CAUGHT BY THE ORACLE THAT ALREADY RUNS THERE, which matters for reading every clean sweep in this record: mxfs_agifc_release_audit(pag, "unmount") IS called at ~49968, immediately before the unlock, and is default-on (agifc_release_audit=1). It reads the AGI, inobt and finobt straight off the PLATTER and prints P-AGIFC-RELEASE-MISMATCH when the image about to be published disagrees with the btrees on the medium -- exactly this record's divergence, measured at exactly the right instant. But it has TWO systematic blind spots, both read from its source at ~42868: it returns early when xfs_is_shutdown(mp), so a shut-down or force-withdrawn node is never audited; and it bails with "multi-level: leaf walk not implemented" unless agi_level == 1 AND agi_free_level == 1, so any AG whose inobt or finobt has grown past a single level is silently skipped. A zero from this audit therefore does NOT mean the AGI was durable at release -- it may mean the audit declined. THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, cheap and needing no reproduction: instrument the unmount release site to report, per AG, how many AG-meta buffers are dirty or in the AIL at the moment of unlock, and count how many audits RETURNED EARLY and why (shutdown vs multi-level). Nonzero dirty at release proves the invariant is violated in practice and is the reproduction this record has lacked since 2026-08-23; a large early-return count explains the clean sweeps without exonerating anything. Do NOT treat arm (e) as established: this is a source-proven omission plus a symptom match, not a demonstrated causal chain, and the record's mechanism stays UNKNOWN until the measurement lands. || UNKNOWN — RULE 4 open. The three P-AGIFC-MISMATCH lines (site=, agi vs pagi vs ibt_sum) were lost: arm_prep runs dmesg -C and test1 was rebooted as a later arm's victim (its journal boot is gone). Candidate arms, all unproven: (a) AGI image split-publication between the two same-AG victim slices replayed back-to-back by one replayer (slot 6's replay was REDUNDANT_CLEAN=3 with a relmark — a redundant-skip on the AGI buffer while the inobt buffer applied, or vice versa); (b) the orphan in bucket 31: victim test3's unlink/ifree in flight at death — the ifree landed in the inobt (free=62) but the AGI freecount (61) / bucket head did not, or the reverse; (c) a 0.26.4 change (structural foreign-clear CAS rule / caw_repair refusal) refusing a legitimate CAS in the replay-purge path — base_shared rman line shows guard_refused=0, so unlikely; (d) the sess399/400 RMW arms resurfacing under two victims per AG.
