defects.summary: On the TCP transport with the step-3 durable authority ledger (0.34.0), a SHARED (PR) grant that the master commits durably but then refuses to deliver because the membership view moved between commit and finalize (P-TAUTH-GHOST 'committed under a superseded ownership generation; not delivered') leaves the requester's holder BIT set in the on-disk record with no holder that knows about it. The successor master imports the bit as a blocker (owner UNKNOWN during formation, since the heartbeat table has not resolved the slot yet) and nothing ever retires it on a live cluster: every later EX on that resource is refused by the ledger (P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT 'table decided a conflicting grant'). On the rig the resource was the ROOT INODE (ino=128): mount's EX on it timed out after 125-208 s on test17/19/20/32 -> 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable' -> shutdown -> 'Failed to read root inode 0x80, error 5' -> mount EIO ('can't read superblock'); other nodes spun 115x REMASTER (status=12) in one second and abandoned ('lock request failed after 10 retries'), and 13 unmounts hung. A clustered FS on which the join ramp itself makes the root inode permanently unlockable cannot mount.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm.c dlm_txn_finalize (0.34.0): remaster = (commit_rc == -ESTALE) || (ctx->ledger_gen != txn->gen) || page_state != MINE; on remaster after a SUCCESSFUL commit the entry is freed (P-TAUTH-GHOST) and the requester gets MXFS_ERR_REMASTER. The record (holders bit for the requester's slot) is durable; the requester never learns it holds anything and never releases; dlm_import_holder at the successor names the bit's owner via slot_node_cb, which during formation returns 0 -> MXFS_DLM_NODE_UNKNOWN, 'never BASTed'. Reproduced usermode: tests/tauth/formation_test (12-node ramp, PR/EX on ino=128): 2 ghosts -> holders=0x6 stuck -> all 12 workers -110, EX never grantable. RULE-5 ruling docs/rulings/ghost-grant-delivery-and-unresolved-pr-bits.md: a successful commit is the proof of authority (page write + exact readback) and MUST be delivered whatever the view did afterwards (the successor imports the record naming the same holder); compensating release on send failure is UNSAFE; an unresolved shared bit stays an EX blocker until recovery names it (re-resolving on every import is fine); long-term: durable {node,inc} per shared holder.

defects.summary: On the TCP transport with the durable authority ledger (0.35.0), two SHARED holders of one resource releasing concurrently while an EX waiter is queued make the master decide the EX over a holder whose bit is still durable: promote_waiters treated EVERY PENDING_RELEASE holder as already gone, not only the one being retired in the current transition. The bundled ledger transition [release, grant EX] is refused by the ledger (P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT 'req EX vs record holders=<sibling bit>'), and the refusal strands the release: the entry is kept PENDING_RELEASE 'for the releaser to retry', the releaser's retry is ACKed OK as a duplicate, and nothing ever retires the record. The stranded entry blocks every later EX on the resource as a holder and keeps the page 'in flight' forever, so the ordered page handoff can never freeze-drain it (P-TAUTH-FREEZE-DRAIN-TIMEOUT x94 on page 1786 = the ROOT INODE's page on test2), every requester of that page gets REMASTER (P74-GRANT status=12 x4381 fleet-wide), 'lock request failed after 10 retries' x54, 26 mounts abort. A refused grant was also terminal for the requester (MXFS_ERR_LEDGER -> -EIO) although the cause was transient.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm.c: (1) promote_waiters used lk_is_live_holder(), which excludes PENDING_RELEASE — documented as 'the one being retired in this very transition' but applied to ALL of them; releases are processed concurrently on the master (local unlock threads vs the receive thread), so a sibling holder in PENDING_RELEASE (its own commit in flight) was invisible and the EX was decided over its durable bit. (2) dlm_txn_commit bundles release + successor grants in one ledger commit; tauth_ledger.c apply_op refuses the grant with -EBUSY (DOUBLE-GRANT, fail-closed by the sess424 ruling) which fails the whole bundle. (3) dlm_txn_finalize on a refused bundle kept the release entry PENDING_RELEASE ('the releaser retries') and ACKed MXFS_ERR_LEDGER; the releaser's resend hit process_remote_release's PENDING_RELEASE branch, which ACKed MXFS_OK as a 'duplicate' — the releaser stopped, the master never re-drove it. (4) A denied grant (MXFS_ERR_LEDGER) mapped to -EIO at the requester. Reproduced deterministically in usermode (tests/tauth/concurrent_release_test, one-shot ledger commit-delay knob): first lap on the unfixed engine = P-TAUTH-DOUBLE-GRANT 'EX vs holders=0x2', B's EX rc=-5 after 70 ms, platter record holders=0x4 stuck, 1 in-flight entry on the page forever, A's release ACKed OK. defects.summary: The TCP authority ledger's rule that ONLY the bootstrap node (lowest live heartbeat slot) may claim an UNOWNED page assumes bootstrap tenure is exclusive. It is not: (1) a node ranks its own slot first regardless of its own health, so a lowest-slot node whose heartbeat stalled (falsely dead, still running) keeps believing it is bootstrap; (2) every other node drops that slot from 'live' at DEATH DETECTION, before the SCSI-PR fence has landed, so the next-lowest node becomes bootstrap at once. In that window both nodes can pass activate(bootstrap)'s read-then-write on the same UNOWNED page — write + readback is not a compare-and-write: A writes seq1/ACTIVE(A), A reads back its own image, B writes seq1/ACTIVE(B), B reads back its own image; both now cache the page as MINE and both may decide grants on every resource of that page until A is fenced. Two authorities for one page = the double-grant/corruption class the ledger exists to prevent. The 0.35.4 D-0345 route (non-bootstrap masters now actively ASK the bootstrap node to claim) widens the exposure from 'pages the bootstrap decides itself' to 'every never-decided page requested during the window'.

Root (dlm/tauth_store.c mxfs_tauth_page_write, pre-0.36.0): the write re-read only the copies' seqs (next=max+1, target=spare copy) and verified only its own copy's readback; nothing tied the commit to the image the caller patched. The bootstrap election cannot be made exclusive at the requester (a falsely-dead node cannot know), so the ledger write itself must arbitrate. || DESIGN-PROVEN interleaving (RULE 4 step 1/2 pending): A = slot 1 (HB thread stalled > death timeout, process alive), B = slot 2. B: node_track[1].live=false -> lowest_live_slot()==2 -> bootstrap_cb true. A: lowest_live_slot()==1 (own slot short-circuit). Page P UNOWNED. A: activate(P,bootstrap): read UNOWNED, write ACTIVE(A) seq1, readback == own -> MINE. B: activate(P,bootstrap): read UNOWNED (before A's write lands) , write ACTIVE(B) seq1, readback == own -> MINE. Platter ends ACTIVE(B); A's cache says ACTIVE(A). A's later txn commits are page writes that overwrite B's (same-seq race is only -EIO if the readback happens to see the other image). defects.summary: The TCP authority ledger has ONE record per resource-hash slot (MXFS_TAUTH_SLOTS=65536, page=slot/31). Two live INODE resources whose hashes collide cannot both be recorded: the second grant is refused -EEXIST at the ledger (tauth_ledger.c ~644 P-TAUTH-COLLISION, fail closed), the master denies MXFS_ERR_LEDGER, and the requester turns that into -EIO to the file operation (dlm.c ~3452 'if (ret > 0) return -EIO'). With 8000 live inodes in the s429 workload the birthday bound makes collisions certain (44 seen); a production filesystem with millions of live inodes would refuse a large fraction of inode locks. The refusal is correct fail-closed behaviour for the record; the DESIGN cannot serve more distinct live resources than slots, and the caller sees a hard EIO rather than a wait.
defects.mechanism: By construction (sess422 step 3 design, docs/tcp-authority-ledger.md): mxfs_tauth_ledger_slot(res) = resource_hash_raw % 65536; apply_op GRANT on a slot whose ACTIVE record names a different resource returns -EEXIST (l->collisions++). dlm_promote_txn: rc -EEXIST -> it->rc=-EEXIST -> deliver sends MXFS_MSG_LOCK_DENY status MXFS_ERR_LEDGER; requester dlm_lock_impl: any deny status other than REMASTER/LEDGER_BUSY -> return -EIO (no retry: the collision persists as long as the other holder lives). The CAW transport has the same 65536-slot table (MXFS_CAW_MAX_SLOTS) but its slot semantics differ (per-slot waiter bits; D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION covers its own collision class). NOT yet measured: which syscall received the EIO in s429 (the workload's per-file errors were not captured; only rc=124 timeouts) — add errno capture to tcp_token_plumbing_verify.

defects.summary: After a whole-cluster crash (all 32 nodes destroyed with fsynced payload), no node can mount again without operator intervention: each rebooted host's I_T nexus still carries its previous incarnation's SCSI PR key (PTPL), the plain REGISTER returns RESERVATION CONFLICT, and the sess432 D-0355 guard refuses the mount (P305-PR-PREDECESSOR-KEY-PRESENT -> 'SCSI PR register failed (-17) refusing to join unfenced'). With zero survivors nobody can PREEMPT AND ABORT anyone; the only remedy is a manual single_node_exclusive=1 mount on one chosen node. A datacenter power loss therefore leaves the filesystem unmountable until a human acts, and the remedy asserts an exclusion-by-topology that becomes false as soon as the other nodes boot.
defects.evidence: tests/evidence/20260829T024833Z_nosurv/remount.txt (build line + armed=11, no MOUNT_OK); test1 journalctl -k 02:49:05Z lines quoted in mechanism; harness verdict 'FAIL test1 mount: B37DDC300BFDA4B00B0217C armed=11', fails=1.
defects.mechanism: dlm/scsipr.c mxfs_scsipr_register: -EEXIST on the plain REGISTER (predecessor key on this nexus) is refused unless replace_predecessor (single_node_exclusive). PR key = 32-bit per-mount node_id; nothing distinguishes 'predecessor from a previous BOOT of this host (dead by construction)' from 'predecessor from this same boot (may still issue I/O)'. The sess432 ruling covered only the lone-node dirty remount; the all-nodes-dead case has no automatic path. Measured: test1 rebooted at +27 s, insmod OK, armed=11, mount refused at 02:49:05Z (journalctl: P304-PREOBSERVE held=1 type=WE-AR, P305-PR-NEXUS-ALREADY-REGISTERED key 0xcc438ac9, P305-PR-PREDECESSOR-KEY-PRESENT, 'MXFS DLM init failed — aborting mount', 'reservation conflict error, dev dm-1, sector 0 op WRITE').

SHAPE: prep both -> each node writes 60 files with dd conv=fsync (A acked 60, B acked 60) -> destroy BOTH -> start ONLY test1 (asserted 'the absent peer is NOT running (shutoff)') -> mount test1 -> read back -> then bring test2 back. RESULT, DATA INTEGRITY (the point of the lap): the survivor read back 60/60 of its OWN fsynced files AND 60/60 of the ABSENT PEER'S fsynced files, content-checked, with 0 wrong and 0 missing and 120 entries listed. The peer's 60 files can only arrive through foreign replay of its dead slice, and the journal shows it: foreign-replay-complete=2, P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE=2. RESULT, FENCING: kind=EXCLUSIVE_WRITE_GATE(20) x1, kind=BOOT_SUCCESSION_ABSENT(21) x1, kind=NO_RESERVATION(8) x3. RESULT, REJOIN: test2 came back and mounted in 2983 ms, saw all 120 files with 0 wrong content, zero shutdown/BUG/Oops. || WHAT THIS SETTLES FOR THIS RECORD. This record's headline is that after a whole-cluster crash no node can mount again without operator intervention, because each rebooted host's I_T nexus still carries its previous incarnation's PR key and the plain REGISTER returns RESERVATION CONFLICT. The sess504 entry narrowed the live exposure to the mount-time fence path on a target that PURGES registrations with the session (the QNAP TS-453 Pro this rig uses), where a whole-cluster restart with an unreplayed dirty slice finds every victim key absent and can only classify KEY_ABSENT_UNPROVEN - and noted that when the fix lands the mount-time fence must be able to take the gate (kind 20 EXCLUSIVE_WRITE_GATE) when the booting node is provably the only live member. THAT IS EXACTLY WHAT THE s587s JOURNAL SHOWS HAPPENING: kind=EXCLUSIVE_WRITE_GATE(20) x1 on a genuine sole survivor, followed by replay of the absent peer's dirty slice and a mount that completed rc=0 in 92.5 s with no operator action and with every fsync-acknowledged byte from BOTH nodes readable afterwards. So on two-node TCP against this target the operator-required shape does not occur. NOT CLOSED: this record was found at 32 nodes (tests/no_survivor_crash_replay.sh s436g, 32 nodes destroyed with fsynced payload) and its 32-node leg is out of scope under the standing two-node-TCP directive and stays owed. defects.summary: The crash-durable durability domain (fua_disable=0, i.e. target power loss / volatile write-cache loss IN scope) is not a qualified clustered-RW configuration: a tenure can become peer-claimable (release CAS) before its home writes and its newly minted epoch/lineage/token state are durable, so a target cache loss can persist the release while dropping the writes it certified (sess197 F2, HARD). 0.54.0 therefore REFUSES clustered RW mounts with fua_disable=0 (mxfs_durability_domain_admit, P-DOMAIN-REFUSED) and admits only the coherence-only domain (fua_disable=1 target_cache_protected=1). This record is the open requirement to qualify and re-admit fua_disable=0.
defects.evidence: Code inventory sess447 (scout): mxfs_blkdev_flush_durable call sites xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:52460 (mxfs_dlm_foreign_replay_work_fn), :53484 and :54037 (mxfs_dlm_mount_recovery_barrier); readiness macros MXFS_RELGATE_F1/F3/F4_*_READY = 0 at xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:45173-45175; no 'stable-media'/'oracle' harness in tests/ or tools/.
defects.mechanism: sess197 F2: fua_disable=1 makes every tenure-boundary flush_epoch a no-op; fua_disable=0 issues real FUA reads but the RELEASE path still performs no durable flush of the retiring tenure's home writes before the peer-claimable CAS (the only durable flushes are in foreign replay / mount recovery). Required per the sess197 ruling step 7 + sess447 ruling: (1) every obligation of the outgoing tenure completed, (2) data+metadata durably ordered before any peer-claimable CAS (mxfs_blkdev_flush_durable after the last home completion, all classes incl. AG; skip only when the tenure provably created zero obligations; flush tickets coalescable), (3) newly minted epoch/lineage/token state durable before a peer can observe or claim it, (4) flush/FUA/writeback errors prevent publication and lead to bounded defer/fence/fail-closed — never 'release anyway', (5) all release/publication paths obey the ordering incl. recovery/cancel/orphan/error exits, (6) a crash exposes only the old complete or the new complete durable epoch. Plus B2-B4 of D-INODE-CLUSTER-PUBLISH-WITHOUT-AUTHORITY and the step-8 stable-media oracle (per tagged image: payload hash/class/resource/epoch/commit/submit/stable points; accepted<->lineage-valid, rejected-stale<->home-newer, sole-surviving-copy never rejected, new-tenure image never stable before its epoch mint) with target-cache-loss tests (discard acked-unflushed writes, reboot from the stable image) — node kills do NOT cover it.
defects.containment: 0.54.0 refuses the unqualified domain at mount time (P-DOMAIN-REFUSED, -EPERM, before any recovery write) instead of admitting it; the coherence-only domain is admitted with an explicit P-DOMAIN-ADMITTED declaration line. The 32-node rig runs fua_disable=1 (SCST target) and declares target_cache_protected=1 in tests/setup/prep_node.sh.

defects.mechanism: NOT YET PROVEN (RULE 4 loop not started). Hypothesis to instrument first: the victim's RELMARK for the inode cluster was published (marker durable) while the cluster's newest image — the create of agino 129 whose icreate/inobt half is in the same or an earlier txn — had not been published to its home, so the survivor's replay classified the cluster image REDUNDANT_CLEAN (marked tuple => 'on-disk image is current') and skipped it while applying the AGI/inobt/unlinked-bucket images of the same txn: inobt says allocated, unlinked bucket says member, core never landed. The alternative is that the marker refuses REINSTALL (P-RELMARK-ICLUS-REINSTALL-REFUSED) for the successor's lock and the core write is lost on the survivor side. Either way the certificate makes the replay trust an image that the marker did not actually cover.

defects.summary: The fencing-intent path lays a RECOVERY_GUARD on whatever incarnation the victim's sector carries, not the one the survivors declared dead. mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_intent (dlm/disklock.c) checks flags, node_id and fs_gen but never compares cur->epoch with the victim_epoch it was asked to fence; it copies cur->epoch into desc.victim_epoch and the caller then issues the PREEMPT AND ABORT of the key frozen for the DECLARED incarnation. When the sector carries a LATER ACTIVE incarnation of the same node this is a fencing intent + P&A against a live member (the sess86 hazard that recovery_begin() closed and that this function, its replacement as the only descriptor creator, did not inherit); in every case the descriptor names an incarnation nobody observed stop, the pending recovery for the declared incarnation stays behind it forever (chain 61: slot 25 sat at GUARD/E2 for the full 180 s heal budget, P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE=0), and every later prover exits -ESTALE silently at the descriptor-tuple check.
defects.evidence: tests/evidence/sess448_chain61_nonzero_s448d.txt:12-16 (INJECT E1->E2; SECTOR t+0.5 flags=GUARD victim_epoch=E2; final flags=GUARD), :20-33 (heal t+15..186 s flags=3 epoch=E2, never reclaimed), :37 (P163-RECOVERY-PENDING lines=31 nodes=31), :45 (P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE=0), :54 (the 31 identical PENDING lines name epoch=11106674514244621995 = E1). Code: dlm/disklock.c mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_intent (no epoch predicate before desc.victim_epoch = cur->epoch), mxfs_disklock_recovery_slot_status (the predicate that exists elsewhere), dlm/v5_mount.c v5_pr_fence_prove_locked switch (no SUPERSEDED arm before 0.61.2).
defects.mechanism: PROVEN from code + the chain 61 capture. dlm/disklock.c mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_intent: the no-descriptor path (cur->flags ACTIVE/WITHDRAWN, cur->node_id==victim, !hb_gen_foreign, inc_valid(cur->epoch)) proceeds straight to want->recov.desc.victim_epoch = cur->epoch; there is no inc_eq(cur->epoch, victim_epoch) predicate. The monitor's epoch-change arm (disklock.c ~2757) declares the CACHED incarnation E1 dead and dispatches v5_pr_fence_prove(dead_node, slot, E1); prove_locked freezes the victim key for E1 (mxfs_disklock_victim_key) and calls fence_intent, which lays FENCING with victim_epoch=E2 (the sector's value). On chain 61 that is the GUARD at t+0.5 s. The same classifier that the completion path uses (mxfs_disklock_recovery_slot_status ~8285: ACTIVE + feature block OK + both incarnations nonzero + differing => SUPERSEDED, else FOREIGN) is absent from the intent path. The descriptor-present arm (6749) then returns -ESTALE with no log line for every subsequent prover asked for E1, and the caller's P238-FENCE-NOINTENT line cannot name the standing tuple. Reachability outside a forged sector: node_id is a random UUID hash per mount (dlm/mount.c:144), so a same-node_id later incarnation requires the claim pass-1 own-stamp reclaim (sess89: unreachable by construction) or a foreign/torn writer; the E1-vs-E2 mismatch class itself (any writer changing the epoch of a record the survivors are tracking) is exactly what D-MONITOR-INCARNATION-DOWNGRADE-TO-ZERO's probe exists to exercise.
defects.containment: None. On a production build the trigger needs a same-node_id incarnation change on a tracked slot (foreign/torn writer, or the unreachable own-stamp reclaim); the consequence when it fires is a slot frozen at GUARD with the declared incarnation's recovery never completing.

defects.summary: A node that crashes and remounts before any survivor replayed it (PASS-1 reclaim of its own still-ACTIVE heartbeat stamp) recovers its own dirty journal slice as a trusted XFS log. Every shared metadata block it held at death that was last written by ANOTHER node's slice carries that slice's LSN stamp; whenever that stamp is numerically >= the reclaiming node's transaction LSN the buffer image is silently dropped by the upstream on-disk-LSN skip, exactly the D-0517 mechanism (AGI/inobt/finobt images lost while the changecount-gated inode items apply), while the node's own grants were still held so no other writer could have refreshed the block. Result: half-applied transactions on the node's own crash recovery (inobt allocated + unlinked bucket populated + FREE core, or any AG/dir/bmap-block lost update) with no diagnostic. Per-node slices have independent cycle/block numbering, so the comparison is meaningless on a clustered mount regardless of which path replays the slice.
defects.evidence: Code: xfs/xfs_log.c:642-698 (routing: PASS-1 reclaim 'keeps full recovery'); xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:45227-45242 (adopted_slice_full_replay comment: 'A PASS-1 own-stamp reclaim (nobody replayed us) always performs full recovery'); pal/linux/xfs_super.c:3950-3959; pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c:1089-1124 (0.61.2 numbering; the unconditional skip); xfs/xfs_inode_item_recover.c:397-440 (trusted path falls back to the di_lsn compare). Measurement of the identical mechanism on the foreign path: D-0517 chain 80 laps 2 and 3 (tests/evidence/sess456_d0517lab_s456b/lap2, lap3) — see that record's SESS459 entry.
defects.mechanism: CODE-PROVEN, NOT YET MEASURED. (1) pal/linux/xfs_super.c:3953 sets m_mxfs_slice_adopted from mxfs_v5_dlm_slice_adopted (pass-2 fresh claim only); a PASS-1 reclaim leaves it false and m_mxfs_bootstrap_adopted false, so xfs_log.c:656-698 sets neither XLOG_MXFS_BOOTSTRAP_ADOPTED nor XLOG_MXFS_ADOPTED_SLICE and xlog_is_mxfs_untrusted_replay() is false for the whole recovery. (2) xlog_recover_commit_trans's authority loop (xfs/xfs_log_recover.c ~3760-3840, mxfs_report_replay_authority) therefore never runs; no ri_mxfs_verdict, no manifest, no live CAW check. (3) xlog_recover_buf_commit_pass2 then reaches the upstream test 'lsn = xlog_recover_get_buf_lsn(); if (lsn != -1 && XFS_LSN_CMP(lsn, current_lsn) >= 0) skip' for every AGF/AGFL/AGI/btree/dir/da/symlink/SB image; the stamp is whichever slice last flushed the block (D-0517 chain 80 lap 2: AG 6 inobt stamped 0x100001183 by slice 31 while slice 6 replayed 0x100000e48/e4c). (4) The inode-item path (xfs/xfs_inode_item_recover.c:397-440) only uses the changecount gate under xlog_is_mxfs_untrusted_replay(); on this trusted path it too falls back to the upstream di_lsn compare (line 435, '> 0'), so inode images are ALSO exposed to the cross-slice veto here. Trigger: the crashed node held resource R at death; R's blocks were last flushed by a predecessor tenure whose slice position is numerically higher than the crashed node's dirty txn LSNs; the node remounts before fencing/foreign replay (fast reboot inside the death-detection window, or a whole-cluster crash where non-bootstrap nodes reclaim their own stamps in PASS-1).
defects.containment: None on a production build: any own-crash recovery that beats the survivors' death detection takes this path. The survivors' foreign replay (once fixed under D-0517) covers only the case where the node stays down long enough to be fenced.
defects.found: sess459 code audit prompted by the D-0517 root (RULE-5 ruling docs/rulings/d0517-buf-lsn-skip-bypass-stop-ship-6-items.md, required change 6): xfs/xfs_log.c:642-698 routes only BOOTSTRAP_ADOPTED and ADOPTED_SLICE (pass-2 fresh claim) mounts through untrusted replay; a PASS-1 own-stamp reclaim ('our own ACTIVE stamp survived — nobody replayed us', xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:45232 'always performs full recovery') replays the dirty own slice as a TRUSTED log: no authority-token evaluation, and pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c xlog_recover_buf_commit_pass2 applies the upstream 'on-disk LSN >= txn LSN => skip' veto.
defects.next: SESS459 REACHABILITY MEASURED: the pass-1 own-stamp match is by node_id ONLY (dlm/disklock.c:9315-9321) and node_id is derived from /etc/mxfs/node.uuid ONLY when opts->node_uuid_path is set (dlm/mount.c:156-170,1694); nothing in the kernel tree ever sets node_uuid_path (grep: only dlm/mxfs.h:114 declares it and mount.c:1694 reads it), so every mount draws a RANDOM identity — test3 claimed slots 25/20/28/27 as nodes 295788330/3889059426/1496692303/1910695745 across four mounts of ONE boot (tests/evidence/sess456_d0517lab_s456b/lap1,lap3/dmesgw_test3.txt 'claimed heartbeat slot ... fresh claim — slice ADOPTED'), although the rig nodes DO carry a 16-byte /etc/mxfs/node.uuid (Mar 8). CONSEQUENCE: on every current build a rebooted node always takes a PASS-2 fresh claim (slice ADOPTED, images suppressed, untrusted) and its previous incarnation's slice is only ever replayed by the survivors' foreign replay — the trusted own-slice recovery this record describes is a LATENT path (the code comment calls it 'the required own-crash recovery path' and D-437/whole-cluster-restart design assumes persistent identity), not a reachable one. Severity set to high (latent on the designated path; becomes critical the moment node_uuid_path is wired). Also note for D-0517: because of this, every reachable dirty-slice replay today is untrusted (foreign / adopted / bootstrap-adopted), so the 0.61.4 class-gated bypass covers every path that can execute. NEXT: (1) keep the P-OWN-BUF-LSN / P-OWN-INODE-LSN / P-OWN-RECOVERY probes (they will fire only if the path ever executes); (2) the fix (route PASS-1 reclaim through authority admission against the node's own still-held live CAW grants) is owed BEFORE persistent node identity is wired — tie it to that change; (3) DISPROVED is not available: the path exists and is the intended design, only its trigger is absent today. || 1) RULE 4 step 2 — instrument + reproduce: the 0.61.3 P-FR-BUF-LSN probe is gated on xlog_is_mxfs_untrusted_replay(); extend it (or add P-OWN-BUF-LSN) to the trusted path on a clustered mount (mp->m_mxfs_dlm_was_active) and drive a PASS-1 reclaim: churn in a shared AG so the AG blocks carry a peer's higher-numbered stamp, then virsh destroy+start the node fast enough that its ACTIVE stamp survives (or hold the survivors' death detection with the existing heartbeat/fence knobs), mount, and sweep for verdict=SKIP + chk_mxfs after the fleet unmount. 2) Fix design per the sess459 ruling item 6: a dirty own slice on a clustered mount must NOT be replayed as trusted — route the PASS-1 reclaim through authority admission (tokens are in every buffer image's trailer; evaluate them against the node's own still-held live CAW grants — the resources it held at death are exactly the ones still bearing its bit — with the same fail-closed treatment for untagged/unsupported classes) and apply the D-0517 fix's class-gated LSN bypass only on APPLY. The inode path's changecount gate must run on this path too. Never disable the compare globally. 3) Verify with the reclaim reproducer (chk clean, zero SKIP, OVERRIDE-APPLY > 0) plus the whole-cluster-crash restart harness (tests for D-437) with shared-AG churn before the crash. 4) This record blocks D-0517 closure only in the sense that the same mechanism must be closed on both replay paths; D-0517's fix is scoped to the untrusted path and is verified independently.

defects.summary: On a volume whose slice count equals the cluster size, a node that died and reboots CANNOT mount while a survivor holds the transient unclaimed-bucket sweep guard on the dead node's own slot: the claim path counts the table (31 ACTIVE + 1 sweep guard = 32), finds no free slot, and the mount fails immediately with -28 (P300-CLAIM-EXHAUSTED / P300-CLAIM-WITHDRAWN 'retry the mount from a mounted peer's cluster'). The only blocker is a self-clearing transient held by a live peer, yet the mount does not wait for it — the rejoining node's mount unit fails and an operator (or a retry loop) must re-issue the mount after the sweep finishes. The permanent variant (a QUARANTINED verdict occupying the slot) is D-QUARANTINED-SLOT-EXHAUSTS-CLUSTER-ADMISSION-376; this record is the TRANSIENT variant, which the 376 design explicitly classifies as 'retry the mount' rather than 'wait'.

defects.summary: A node shuts its filesystem down (fail-closed AG-release refusal) during an ORDINARY rm of a shared directory, withdraws, and is fenced by the cluster — because the inode FREE publication obligation of one freed inode is left stuck in FREE_PENDING forever by a lost-update race between the ifree commit (mxfs_pubob_free_commit: FREE_PENDING -> FREE) and the concurrent inode-cluster-buffer write completion (xfs_iflush_finish -> mxfs_pubob_discharge('flushed') -> mxfs_pubob_free_pending, which re-marks FREE_PENDING and rewrites i_mxfs_freeob=1 because the write that completed carried the PRE-free UNLINK image staged before the ifree began). The release publish gate then reads 'ifree in flight' for an ifree that committed 7 s earlier, defers for its whole 2+8x2 s budget (P-FREEOB-PENDING every 2 s from 07:50:13 to 07:50:33) and executes P-FREEOB-REFUSED -> xfs_force_shutdown -> P-WITHDRAW -> P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP -> the peer (test8) fences it (P236-FENCE-INTENT/P-PR-FENCE 'EXCLUSION PROVED'). One rm -rf = a node lost and a whole 8-node board blocked. The mirror-image ordering of the same race (free_commit writes freeob=2 BEFORE the completion's discharge reads it) makes the discharge take its 'not pending' arm and DROP the committed FREE obligation entirely (freeob=0, MXFS_IF_PUBOB cleared, store entry deleted): the free image is then never enforced at the AG handoff — the silent D-0351 exposure (peer double-alloc shutdown) — so both orderings are defects.

defects.mechanism: ESTABLISHED TO THE LINE ORDER from test1's kernel log (tests/evidence/sess464_8caw_dirreuse_fence_20260902T074512Z/kernlog_test1.gz, lines 88110-88142 + the ino's 26-line history; /tmp/run_dir_reuse_coherency_20260902T074512Z/kernlog_test1 is the uncompressed copy). rm (pid 200515) is freeing test1's copies of PEER-created files in the shared dir under a held AG-39 EX tenure. Healthy sibling ino 327155846: P291-EXWIN .849 -> P82-REM .852 -> P55C-FREE-FLUSH/P-FREEPUB-CLAIM/KEEP/WRITE/CLAIM-CLEAR(durable) at .856 = FREE obligation published normally. Stuck ino 327155847 (agno 39 agino 0x87, off=7 of startino 128): 88094 P291-EXWIN .853 (unlink); 88112 'P240-COPYIN-ID ino=327155847 bp=ffff8b88bf6c5a00 flush=1 pend=1 comm=xfsaild' .8556 = xfsaild copies the UNLINK image (nlink=0, mode live) into cluster buffer daddr=165215360 with i_mxfs_freeob==0, so xfs_inode.c:8992 sets MXFS_IF_PUBOB_FLUSHED for that image; 88123-88129 the buffer write is submitted (P-FREEPUB-WRITE slots 0-6); 88132-88137 the write COMPLETION runs xfs_iflush_finish over the buffer's inode list (P-FREEPUB-CLAIM-CLEAR why=durable for slots 0-5); 88138 rm: 'P150-FREE-IBT agno=39 off=7' .8561 (xfs_difree of 327155847 — the ifree window is open: xfs_inode.c:4286 set i_mxfs_freeob=1 just before xfs_ifree); 88139 completion: CLAIM-CLEAR ino=327155846 (slot 6); 88142 rm: 'P82-REM ino=327155847' .8562 (xfs_iunlink_remove); the completion's next inode is slot 7 = 327155847 with FLUSHED set -> xfs_inode_item.c:1154-1160 mxfs_pubob_discharge(ip,'flushed') -> xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:37241 reads i_mxfs_freeob==1 -> mxfs_pubob_free_pending: ob->kind=FREE_PENDING, WRITE i_mxfs_freeob=1, set PUBOB, clear FLUSHED; rm: xfs_trans_commit -> xfs_inode.c:4341 MXFS_IF_FREE_COMMITTED set -> 4349 READ freeob==1 -> mxfs_pubob_free_commit: ob->kind=FREE, i_mxfs_freeob=2. Neither transition is atomic with the other: the two functions each read i_mxfs_freeob outside m_mxfs_pubob_lock and write ob->kind under it then i_mxfs_freeob after it, so free_commit's FREE (kind + freeob=2) is overwritten by free_pending's FREE_PENDING (kind + freeob=1) when the completion's read of freeob precedes free_commit's write of 2. Observed end state matches exactly: no P55C-FREE-FLUSH ever for 327155847 (gate never took the FREE arm), 'P88-PUBOB-RECLAIM-REFUSED ino=327155847 clean=1 ili_fields=0x0 flushed=0 nlink=0' x9 from 07:50:10 (PUBOB set, FLUSHED clear, inode clean and committed-free), and at the AG-39 release (bast-inline path, 07:50:13) xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:42083 'P-FREEOB-PENDING ag=39 ino=327155847 — ifree in flight at AG release; deferring the unlock' every 2 s for 11 laps until 47838 P-FREEOB-REFUSED -> 47841 xfs_force_shutdown(SHUTDOWN_META_IO_ERROR) at 07:50:33 ('Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at mxfs_ag_release_publish_gate+0x1a1/0x1b0'). No ifree was in flight: rm had moved on to the next unlink 0.5 ms after P82-REM (88143 P50-RD comm=rm .8567) and P128-INACT-DEFER never printed for this ino. The alternative ordering (free_commit's write of freeob=2 lands before the completion's read) sends mxfs_pubob_discharge down its 37245-37286 arm: i_mxfs_freeob=0, MXFS_IF_PUBOB cleared, entry dropped (kind FREE is not UNLINK) — a committed FREE obligation silently lost; not observed in this run but reachable by the same race. Downstream (all designed, not defects): P-SESSION-POISON, P306-CAW-RELEASE-POISONED ag=39, P-WITHDRAW, P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP slot=0; test8 (slot 3) 'P163-WITHDRAW-SEEN slot=0 ... peer declared voluntary death' -> P236-FENCE-INTENT -> P-PR-FENCE 'preempt-and-aborted dead node 2477736485 ... EXCLUSION PROVED' -> P236-FENCE-CERTIFIED; test5 (slot 1) elected, foreign replay of slice 0 complete at 07:50:40 (P226-ICENSUS intents=0), P163-RECOVERED on all survivors 07:50:41-42; test1's own P305-RESV-HEALTH SELF_GONE / P277-FENCED-SELF-WITHDRAW / P131-SELF-FENCE at 07:50:36 are the fenced node observing its own fence. NOT a false death: no heartbeat-stall or lease-expiry line exists on test1 between 07:45:48 and 07:50:33, and every peer's death declaration cites the WITHDRAWN stamp or test8's certified fence.

What the evidence RULES OUT: (a) the three known SCST memory-safety defects - all are fixed in the installed build (scst 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.5, srcversion 49601BF23C0AF27910B7E2C; scst_pres.c:2634-2665 carries the .4 signed/offset bound with min(buffer_size, cmd->bufflen); .5 carries the PR-abort tryget), and every one of them announced itself with a loud oops/BUG carrying an SCST frame, which this event did not; (b) the PR READ FULL STATUS overflow specifically - its precursor 'Too big response data len' never appeared and the kmsg guard ran the whole boot without a single halt, precursor or flood trip; (c) the GPU PCIe P2P cause of the 09-01 pair - boot -1 has ZERO nv_dma_map_peer lines and ZERO Xid errors (boot -2, which crashed on it, has 12 and 8 respectively); (d) OOM / page-allocation failure - none in boot -1; (e) filesystem-headroom wedge - / at 85% used, 273G free, inside the preflight floor; (f) log flood - peak 1303 kernel lines/min vs the 182 lines/s wedge class. defects.found: sess469 (2026-09-02), investigating the user's report of repeated host reboots. Filed under RULE 2d: a host-kernel death is a first-class defect. Distinct from D-HOST-CLYDE-DOUBLE-CRASH-GPU-PCIE-P2P-NOT-MXFS-0901, which covers the two 2026-09-01 crashes only.
defects.next: This defect CANNOT be root-caused with the instrumentation the host currently has - that is the first thing to fix, and it is the blocking step. The host has NO surviving evidence channel for a fault that does not reach the oops path: (1) no BMC - ipmi_si is not loaded and SMBIOS type 38 (IPMI Device Information) is absent, so the ASMB card is not present or not enabled in BIOS; there is no SEL to read and installing ipmitool alone would not create one. (2) no netconsole (not loaded, no modprobe.d config) - the only channel that survives a hard lockup or triple fault. (3) no kdump - crashkernel= absent from /proc/cmdline, kdump-tools inactive, /var/crash empty. (4) no metrics - sysstat is installed and its cron fires every 10 min but /etc/default/sysstat has ENABLED="false" and /var/log/sysstat is empty, so there is no CPU/memory/IO history across the event. (5) kernel.hardlockup_panic=0 and kernel.softlockup_panic=0, so a lockup prints rather than producing a recorded panic. ACTIONS, in order: [a] enable sysstat collection (no reboot, zero risk); [b] configure netconsole to another host on 192.168.1.x/192.168.120.x (no reboot); [c] decide on crashkernel= and, separately, on restoring the IOMMU in at least a fault-reporting mode - BOTH need a kernel-cmdline change and therefore a reboot, which per RULE 2 only the user may perform, and the iommu=off is presumed deliberate (GPU P2P / passthrough) so it is a user decision with a real trade-off, not a defect to be silently fixed. Until at least [b] lands, a recurrence will again leave nothing.

defects.summary: After a whole-cluster bootstrap the lone survivor's post-recovery ORPHAN SCAN (mxfs_orphan_scan, run after every dead-slot bucket sweep) xfs_iget()s a zombie that IS a member of a not-yet-swept slot bucket (the unclaimed previous-incarnation slot's bucket), finds it 'bucketed' and merely xfs_irele()s it WITHOUT loading its unlinked-chain state (no xfs_inode_reload_unlinked_bucket, no i_unlinked_bucket stamp). The irele queues inodegc; xfs_inactive -> xfs_inactive_ifree -> xfs_ifree -> xfs_iunlink_remove_inode runs with i_prev_unlinked=0 and i_unlinked_bucket=-1, so it computes the LEGACY bucket agino%64 (bucket 4) while the on-disk membership is in the slot bucket (bucket 1); bucket 4's head is NULLAGINO, xfs_verify_agino fails, P71-INSTR agi-unlinked-garbage -> XFS_CORRUPTION_ERROR -> xfs_ifree -117 -> force shutdown -> P-SESSION-POISON. The multi-node fail-closed guards that would have caught the unstamped remove (mxfs_ifree_unlinked_preflight P-UNLPRE-NOBUCKET -EAGAIN, P84, P85) were all DISABLED because the survivor was in dlm_caw single_node=true (sole live member after the bootstrap), so legacy hashing was used against a slot-partitioned on-disk list. Meanwhile the legitimate sweeper of that bucket (P99-UBSWEEP slot=1) could not take the inode (xfs_iget -> -ENOENT: NEED_INACTIVE with nlink 0 cannot be re-grabbed) and 'stays pending'. Net: one rm'd open file + whole-cluster death = the recovering node shuts down (fail-closed, but the cluster's only member is now poisoned).

defects.next: SESS469 RULE-5 DESIGN RULING + FIX LANDED IN TREE 0.64.10 (UNBUILT at this note; frozen dir tests/evidence/sess469_frozen_06410 when the build lands). Ruling: (1) bucket layout is a PERSISTENT property, never the dynamic single_node predicate — a lone survivor's agino%64 inserts leak at the next slot-scoped recovery; (2) the find-across-64-heads walk needs AG DLM EX serialization (an explicit resolve phase, not inside ILOCK_SHARED reload callers); (3) the orphan scan must not instantiate members; a post-iget member is reaped by this node only if it is on OUR slot bucket (stamp + reload), otherwise its inactivation must be suppressed, never irele'd into inodegc. LANDED: xfs/libxfs/xfs_inode_util.c xfs_iunlink_pick_bucket + P84 drop the single_node term (slot layout whenever m_mxfs_dlm); xfs/xfs_inode.c mxfs_iunlink_find_bucket (raw 64-head walk, in-core hops first, P-UNLFIND-NOTENURE if no AG holder) used by mxfs_ifree_unlinked_preflight for an unstamped member (P-UNLPRE-FOUND / P-UNLPRE-NOBUCKET -> -EAGAIN defer) and the preflight gate no longer exempts single-node; xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c mxfs_orphan_scan takes the AG EX and runs mxfs_orphan_on_any_bucket BEFORE the iget (members are never instantiated); the post-iget re-verify stamps+reloads only an own-slot member and otherwise sets MXFS_IF_FOREIGN_ZOMBIE (P98-ORPHAN-MEMBER-LATE), which xfs_inactive honours with P-INACT-FOREIGN-ZOMBIE-SKIP (no DLM, no truncate, no ifree; the shell reclaims and the sweeper's iget recycles it; the flag is in XFS_IRECLAIM_RESET_FLAGS). Recovery scoping (P86) and the lone-node all-64 recovery walk are unchanged. VERIFICATION: chain 106 tests/sess468_chain106_peerloss_rerun.sh (peerloss arm on 0.64.10, gate chain 105) with tests/guard_race_arms.sh's new post-bootstrap verdict (45 s settle; FAIL on P-UNLREM-INCOMPLETE/P71/P-SESSION-POISON/shutdown, on P97-SWEEP-IGET-FAIL, or on a non-writable fs; expects P99-UBSWEEP-DONE rc=0). RESIDUAL to rule on: platters written by pre-0.64.10 builds in single-node mode hold agino%64 zombies that only a lone-node recovery (all-64 walk) or that bucket's slot recovery drains. || SESS469 FILED from the chain 99 peerloss kernel log (mechanism above is line-ordered evidence, not a hypothesis). FIX SHAPE (to be RULE-5 reviewed before landing): (a) mxfs_orphan_scan must never iget a bucketed zombie: run mxfs_orphan_on_any_bucket() BEFORE the iget (it is a raw AGI/dinode walk and needs no in-core inode) and skip members without touching them; keep the post-iget re-verify under the AG EX for the race, and when THAT finds a member, stamp i_unlinked_bucket with the bucket the walk found and reload the chain (xfs_inode_reload_unlinked_bucket) before the irele — the upstream contract for every non-recovery iget of an unlinked inode. (b) Bucket selection for an UNSTAMPED member must be found on the platter, never computed: xfs_iunlink_member_bucket / xfs_inode_reload_unlinked_bucket / mxfs_ifree_unlinked_preflight with i_unlinked_bucket<0 must locate the agino across all 64 heads (bounded raw walk) — independent of the single_node predicate, because a lone survivor (or a knob flip) can face a slot-partitioned list. (c) The single_node gating of the iunlink fail-closed guards (xfs_inode.c 4258, xfs_inode_util.c 1150, xfs_inode.c 10851) is a latent hazard by itself: a membership-dependent predicate is not a 'cluster-uniform knob'; at minimum the P-UNLPRE-NOBUCKET fail-closed arm must apply whenever the mount has EVER been multi-node (ctx->ever_multi) or the platter's slot table shows other slots. defects.mechanism: (1) xfs_icreate -> xfs_inode_init installs only xfs_setup_inode; the i_op/i_fop tables come from xfs_setup_iops, which xfs_generic_create calls itself before d_instantiate. mxfs_dirshard_alloc_parent / alloc_container called xfs_finish_inode_setup without it, so the creator's in-core parent kept the VFS empty_iops; d_flags_for_inode() typed the dentry DCACHE_AUTODIR_TYPE (S_IFDIR with no ->lookup) and walk_component/O_DIRECTORY return -ENOTDIR. The peer igets the parent from disk via xfs_setup_existing_inode, so only the creator is affected (explains cc lap 1 FAIL / laps 2-3 PASS). (2) mxfs_dirshard_iget used XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED; xfs_imap_lookup answers it from xfs_ialloc_read_agi(pag, NULL) + an inobt lookup taken WITHOUT the AG DLM lock — the peer's cached AGI/inobt image predates the creator's dialloc of the holder/containers, so 'untrusted and free' -> -EINVAL (xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c xfs_imap_lookup). mxfs_dirshard_free_container listed -EINVAL among the 'already freed' errnos and cleared the bit. (3) xfs_readdir asserts XFS_IOLOCK_SHARED|EXCL on the directory it reads; iterate_dir holds the PARENT's i_rwsem, a container has no dentry and nobody takes its i_rwsem. The consumer_refresh + i_dlm_stale settle in xfs_file_readdir run on the parent (no entries) and the container's peer-armed reload can only fire inside xfs_readdir under mxfs_dirshard_readdir's own ILOCK_SHARED, where mxfs_dlm_reload_inode must bail.

defects.summary: On MXFS an XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED iget decides 'is this inode number allocated?' from xfs_imap_lookup, which reads the AGI and walks the inobt via xfs_ialloc_read_agi(pag, NULL, ...) with NO AG DLM lock — i.e. from whatever AGI/inobt buffers this node last cached. A peer's allocation of the number is invisible until this node next acquires that AG, so a valid reference to a peer-created inode reads as FREE (-EINVAL) or NOT-IN-ANY-CHUNK (-EINVAL) for an unbounded time. Callers: pal/linux/xfs_export.c xfs_nfs_get_inode (NFS / open_by_handle_at -> ESTALE for peer-created files), xfs/xfs_itable.c bulkstat/inumbers (peer-created inodes silently skipped: 'if (error == -ENOENT || error == -EINVAL) goto out_advance'), xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:36527 P88-REAP-RETRY (an -EINVAL retires the reap entry as 'freed elsewhere / vanished'), xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:51864 orphan scan (iget AFTER the AG lock is dropped), xfs/xfs_zone_gc.c, xfs/xfs_inode.c:6083 xfs_iunlink_reload_next (already under the AG lock — coherent), xfs/xfs_mount.c rootino (mount time — coherent).
defects.evidence: Code: xfs/libxfs/xfs_ialloc.c xfs_imap_lookup (three -EINVAL arms, now named by P-IMAP-UNTRUSTED-FREE / P-IMAP-UNTRUSTED-NOREC probes, 0.64.11+); call sites above. Observation (via the sharding user): D-0526 evidence — peer -EINVAL on every readdir/lookup/create of a freshly published sharded dir while the creator's own view (post-iops fix) and the platter (chk: containers 133.. allocated, manifest valid) said the inodes existed. Direct measurement pending: tests/d0527_untrusted_iget_peer.sh (handle minted on the creator after 200 allocations, opened by handle on a peer that had cached the AG's inobt through an earlier warm handle open; path lookup alongside as the trusted control) — chain 110 (tests/sess470_chain110_d0527_handle_probe.sh, three node pairings, gated behind chain 109 on 0.64.12).
defects.mechanism: xfs_iget(UNTRUSTED) -> xfs_iget_cache_miss -> xfs_imap(pag, tp=NULL, ino, imap, XFS_IGET_UNTRUSTED) -> xfs_imap_lookup: xfs_ialloc_read_agi(pag, NULL, 0, &agbp) returns the CACHED AGI buffer (no _XBF_FUA_FRESH gate applies without the AG lock), xfs_inobt_lookup walks cached inobt blocks; 'if (!error && i == 0) error = -EINVAL' / 'rec.ir_startino > agino || ... <= agino -> -EINVAL' / '(flags & UNTRUSTED) && (rec.ir_free & mask) -> -EINVAL'. MXFS refreshes AG buffers on mxfs_ag_dlm_lock acquisition (Invariant 1 drain on the releaser, FUA-fresh reads on the acquirer); nothing on this path takes it. The trusted path does not consult the inobt at all (arithmetic imap + the inode DLM-coherent cluster read + P-IGET-ENOENT arbitration), which is why dirents and the D-0526 fix work.
defects.containment: None. NFS exports / open_by_handle_at of files created on another node can fail ESTALE until the serving node touches the AG; bulkstat omits them; P88 reap-retry entries can be retired on a false 'vanished' (the unlinked bucket remains the durable record, so that case degrades to a delay, not a loss). The dir-sharding user is fixed separately (D-0526, trusted iget).

defects.related: D-0526 (first observed instance, sharding user); D-INCARN-STALE-SHELL-UNGATED-FILE-READS-512 (iget coherency family); RULE-5 sess470 ruling (untrusted iget review, answer D): fix shape = AG-DLM-bracketed allocation-state lookup (acquire AG DLM -> refreshed AGI + inobt -> xfs_ialloc_read_agi + inobt lookup -> release), a helper aware of an already-held AG lock, documented AG-DLM-vs-inode-DLM order, and error translation so an I/O or corruption error is never reported as 'free'; a coherent AGI read alone is insufficient (the decision also depends on inobt blocks) and trusted iget is not a substitute for handles/scrub, which need an authoritative allocation check.

Pace: the bracket steals the AG from its affine owner once per cold handle open (cached thereafter) — record the handle-open wall in the harness against RULE 0. 4) RULE-5 REVIEW (sess472, of the landed bracket): (a) for lock_flags==0 igets (NFS handles) the cluster-buffer read (xfs_imap_to_bp) runs with NO inode DLM and outside the AG bracket — a peer free/reuse between imap and the dinode read is caught only by the dinode mode/gen checks; extending the AG bracket over xfs_imap_to_bp would be sound ONLY for lock_flags==0 (for ILOCK callers the inode DLM begin must come first to keep ILOCK->AG order) and needs proof that inode-cluster buffers are read fresh under the AG grant, not just AGI/inobt — this is the D-INCARN-STALE-SHELL-UNGATED-FILE-READS-512 family; measure before extending. defects.summary: A valid retained EX holder bit of THIS node (its previous incarnation's grant kept on the CAW slot table) is adopted into in-core tenure only during the mount adoption window. Outside that window nothing at acquire time reconciles 'my own bit is set on the platter while I hold no tenure': the fast paths grant from tracked state only, so the node treats its own bit as a peer's hold, retries with -EAGAIN, BASTs itself (multicast loopback) and depends on the rx-driven readopt/strand repair — a bounded stall at best, sweep exhaustion across every affinity-owned AG (the D-488 all-25-AG signature) or a quarantine at worst. No data loss; availability and RULE 0 pace.
defects.evidence: Code anchors above (scout sweep sess470). Historical: the D-488 sess240 specimen (all 25 AGs EX-held by affinity with no in-core tenure on ~26 nodes, one node livelocked on its OWN bit for 20+ min) is consistent with this shape but its birth was never captured. Not yet measured in isolation.
defects.mechanism: Retained bits exist by design (cached AG grants survive last-holder release and unmount/crash). caw_adopt_retained(ctx, ...) is the only path that turns a retained own bit into tracked tenure and it is gated on ctx->mount_adopt_window; after the window closes, __mxfs_ag_dlm_lock's cached/held fast paths consult only pag_dlm_holders/pag_dlm_cached, and the fresh-acquire path issues a CAS that miscompares against its own bit -> -EAGAIN / bounded sweep (P5G) -> self-BAST -> mxfs_dlm_ag_bast_notify orphan_nak (holders==0, !cached, !bast_scheduled, pending >3 s) -> mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_held read-back -> READOPT_PENDING -> worker P294 readopt mint. Every step is a delay, and each gate (bast_scheduled latch, readopt_pending, the 3 s pending floor) is a place the repair can stall; the sess275 stuck-latch watchdog bounds one of them at 30 s.
defects.containment: The BAST-driven readopt/strand repair (verified by the ag_strand_repair board criterion on every board) recovers a stranded own bit once a BAST for that AG is processed; the mount window covers the common remount case.
defects.found: sess470 (2026-09-02), from the RULE-5 disposition review of D-AGLOCK-ORPHAN-EX-TRACKING-LOSS-LIVELOCK-488 (hypothesis c of that record, never tested). Code-proven, not yet observed in isolation: dlm/dlm_caw.c caw_adopt_retained ~4527-4542 returns 0 immediately when !ctx->mount_adopt_window; xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c __mxfs_ag_dlm_lock ~40872-40892 records that an acquire-side on-disk own-bit check was tried and REVERTED (one slot read per acquire); the only recovery for an own bit without in-core tenure is the BAST-driven orphan-nak/readopt path in mxfs_dlm_ag_bast_notify (~48246-48286).
defects.related: D-AGLOCK-ORPHAN-EX-TRACKING-LOSS-LIVELOCK-488 (parent record; sess470 GPT ruling answer 3: file separately), D-STRANDED-AG-REPAIR-UNVALIDATED (closed; the injected-repair criterion), D-MASS-FALSE-DEATH-FROZEN-GRANT-STALL-482.
defects.next: 1) MEASURE (sess470 ruling): a two-phase directed test — (a) in-window control: retained own bits visible before the adoption scan, remount, allocate in that AG -> tenure established (P294/adopt lines, no P5G); (b) out-of-window: install a valid retained own bit for this node AFTER the adoption window closes and BEFORE the first acquire of that AG (candidate: the ag_strand_inject one-shot on the node's own affine AG with NO peer contention, then allocate in that AG from the same node) and record: acquire outcome (-EAGAIN count, P5G), self-BAST -> orphan_nak -> readopt timeline, wall to the first successful allocation, any P275 quarantine.
