defects.summary: Releasing a CONTENDED inode/directory lock on the CAW transport spends 15-97 ms in the wire unlock alone -- the CAS write that frees the slot, with the AIL/buffer drain that precedes it already complete and accounted separately. On the shared directory of the crash_consistency workload: n=15 samples, p50 14.9 ms, p90 52.7 ms, max 97.1 ms. A single COMPARE-AND-WRITE to one 512-byte slot on the shared LUN should cost the storage round trip, order 1 ms. This is a RULE 0 performance assertion violation in the DLM transport itself, independent of any filesystem workload.
defects.evidence:
tests/evidence/run_crash_consistency_20260904T000831Z/kernlog_test1.gz, probe P138-BAST (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:21738), which brackets one BAST-driven holder-side release. Its su/sw/sx split (documented at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:21750-21753: sw = drain-end -> unlock entry, sx = the wire unlock proper) attributes essentially the whole cost to sx. Three verbatim samples on ino=201343553:
  dur_us=52724 ... sc=730 sd=1567 su=49390 sw=8 sx=49379
  dur_us=50563 ... sc=1685 sd=148 su=48356 sw=43 sx=48309
  dur_us=97143 ... sc=715 sd=154 su=95649 sw=38 sx=95608
In every sample sw is 8-43 MICROseconds while sx is 48-96 MILLIseconds, so the pre-unlock tail is not the cost and the drain (sa/sb/sc/sd, all <= 1.7 ms) is not the cost. Across the 15 samples on that inode the releases total 409.7 ms. The same run's root directory (ino=128) shows the pattern too: n=4, p50 9.3 ms, max 30.8 ms.
defects.mechanism:
SESS481 THE 9.42 ms/ATTEMPT HEADLINE IS INFLATED — QUOTE 5.41 ms INSTEAD.  Two free analyses over the same 17558 samples, no rig time.  (1) THE RESIDUE IS SUPER-LINEAR IN RETRIES, not proportional.  Bucketing (wall_ms - sleep_ms) by retry count: retries=1 n=10181 resid 10.83 ms (5.41/attempt); =2 n=4053 26.66 (8.89); =3 n=1890 49.95 (12.49); =4 n=839 83.55 (16.71); =5 n=413 108.64 (18.11); =6 n=120 138.91 (19.84); =7 n=44 130.82 (16.35).  A least-squares fit returns a NEGATIVE intercept (-36.2 ms fixed + 22.6 ms/attempt), which is the arithmetic signature of convexity, so the linear "per attempt" model the 9.42 figure assumes is simply the wrong shape.  (2) THE SUPER-LINEARITY IS LARGELY SELECTION, NOT AN ESCALATING CODE PATH.  Counting, per sample, how many other P381 events landed in the SAME SECOND on the SAME node: retries=1 -> 31.5, =2 36.3, =3 43.7, =4 58.0, =5 63.3, =6 63.1.  Local contention roughly DOUBLES from the 1-retry bucket to the 5-retry bucket, tracking the 3.3x rise in per-attempt residue.  An unlock that needs many retries is by construction one occurring inside a heavy burst, when the device queue, the scheduler and every mutex are slower — so the tail measures WHEN those unlocks happen at least as much as what they do.
CONSEQUENCE: use the LEAST-CONTENDED bucket as the per-attempt estimate.  At retries=1 (n=10181) the unaccounted cost is 5.41 ms per attempt, and that bucket carries NO caw_inode_backoff at all (it is skipped below retry 2, dlm/dlm_caw.c:8097).  Against a measured slot round trip of 0.77-1.54 ms that leaves roughly 4 ms per attempt genuinely unexplained at low contention — a real defect, but appreciably smaller and better bounded than the 9.42 ms first recorded.  tools/caw_unlock_audit.py now prints this floor beside the aggregate and says which to quote.
WHAT caw_inode_backoff CAN ACCOUNT FOR, modelled rather than measured: it sleeps rnd % cap with cap = min(4 + 2*retry, 20) (dlm/dlm_caw.c:8112-8118), so expected sleep per call is cap/2 and the cumulative expectation over an unlock with R retries (calls fire at retry 2..R) is R=2 ~4 ms, R=3 ~9, R=4 ~15, R=5 ~22, R=6 ~30, R=7 ~39.  Subtracting that from the observed residues leaves 22.7/41.0/68.6/86.6/108.9 ms — i.e. it explains only about 15-25%, and the remainder is still convex, which the burst-density finding above accounts for.  backoff_ms= (0.65.0) will replace this MODEL with a MEASUREMENT; do not treat the model as the answer. || SESS481 THE find_slot HYPOTHESIS IS WEAKENED BY A STRUCTURAL MEASUREMENT — NOT DEAD, BUT DO NOT BUILD ON IT.  New tool tools/caw_slot_census.py reads the CAW slot table straight out of the SCST backing file (/home/steve/disk.img) on the target host: no rig time, no lock, read-only, cannot disturb a run.  (tools/caw_slotdump cannot do this — it speaks SG_IO and so needs an initiator.)  The base is exact rather than guessed: chk_mxfs reports disklock_offset=67117056 for this LUN, and lock_region_offset = disklock_offset + MXFS_DISKLOCK_HB_SIZE (64 x 512) = 0x400a000, per dlm/dlm_caw.c:15522 and dlm/disklock.h:125-126.  CENSUS ON THE IDLE TABLE (cluster between chains, 2026-09-04): live=99 (66 INODE, 33 AG), TOMBSTONES=0, empty=65437, LOAD FACTOR 0.0015, and 99 of 99 live slots sit at DISPLACEMENT 0 — every resource is at its computed home, so a lookup costs exactly ONE 16-slot span read.  At that load a linear probe cannot be walking chains and the 9.42 ms/attempt residue cannot be span-read I/O.  THE MEASUREMENT'S OWN LIMIT, stated so nobody over-reads it: this is an IDLE table.  The workload creates 3200 files and tombstones are explicitly skip-but-continue (MXFS_CAW_TOMBSTONE_MAGIC "MXDL", dlm/dlm_caw.h:33), so the open question is whether churn accumulates them during a row.  But even a full 3200-slot working set is load factor 0.05, where expected linear-probe displacement is ~0.03 slots, so the hypothesis needs tombstone accumulation of a wholly different order to survive — and zero tombstones on an idle table is evidence they do not persist.  TWO INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENTS NOW SETTLE IT AND THEY CANNOT BE FOOLED THE SAME WAY: find_ms= (direct, in-kernel, 0.65.0) and the census (structural, offline).  Chain 128 runs BOTH and takes the census immediately after each row, BEFORE the next leg's prep re-mkfs's the LUN.  IF BOTH RETURN NULL the residue is neither the backoff ladder, nor the device, nor the probe walk, and the next boundary to instrument is inside the CAS attempt itself (caw_cas_slot and the lreq/publication machinery it calls) — not a fourth guess at the same three suspects.
ALSO CORRECTED, because it nearly caused a duplicate filing: the block comment at dlm/dlm_caw.c:1436 reads as though the span read is still broken and spanning defaulted OFF.  It is not.  That defect was root-caused (the struct had grown while find_slot indexes the span buffer as an array of it, so every slot past the first decoded 8 bytes off), fixed, and closed as D-CAW-CLAIM-RETRY-EXHAUSTION-SHUTDOWN (critical, 2026-08-01); mxfs_caw_probe_span_enable is 1, and sess481 re-verified ZERO P94-SPAN-DISAGREE across all 32 nodes of a full crash_consistency row.  The comment now carries that epilogue. || SESS481 SECOND CORRECTION — TWO NUMBERS BELOW ARE WRONG AND ONE CLAIM IS RETRACTED.  (1) The figures "0.22 ms per slot read (P297-TKT read_ms/reads)" and "0.37 ms per CAW op (P138-AGWAIT caw_svc_ms/reads)" were derived by dividing sum(read_ms) by sum(reads) ACROSS SAMPLES.  That is invalid: dlm/dlm_caw.c:6908 ASSIGNS acq_read_ms = now - t0 on every poll, so read_ms is the LAST read's duration, while reads is CUMULATIVE — a per-iteration value over a cumulative count.  THE CORRECT DIRECT FIGURES, read as the per-read values they are: P297-TKT read_ms mean 0.77 ms, p50 1, p90 2, max 32 (n=3084); P138-AGWAIT caw_svc_ms mean 1.54 ms, p50 1, p90 4, max 37 (n=423).  The CONCLUSION is unchanged and in fact still comfortable — a slot operation costs well under 2 ms against a 9.42 ms residue — but the specific numbers must not be quoted as 0.22/0.37.  (2) RETRACTED: "the same signature appears on the acquire side: ~242 ms per acquire wait unaccounted".  That came from treating P297-TKT's el_ms (cumulative since wait start) against slept_ms and read_ms (both LAST-value — slept_ms prints last_sleep_ms, dlm/dlm_caw.c:6970).  Mixing them proves nothing in either direction, so the acquire side is now UNKNOWN, not anomalous.  A cumulative sleep total already existed as sleep_tot_ms and simply was not printed.
INSTRUMENTATION ADDED 0.65.0 SO THE ACQUIRE SIDE CAN BE ANSWERED: P297-TKT now also carries read_sum_ms= (new accumulator beside the per-read value, which P-ACQ-STUCK still needs) and sleep_sum_ms= (the pre-existing sleep_tot_ms, now printed).  With those a wait's read and sleep TOTALS can be stated rather than inferred.
WHAT STILL STANDS, AND WHY: the UNLOCK-side residue is totals-against-totals and is unaffected by any of the above — p381_sleep_ms ACCUMULATES (dlm/dlm_caw.c:10675 and :11148, both +=) and wall_ms is measured from a single p381_t0 (:10559).  So "17558 contended unlocks, 616.5 s of node-time = 21.4% of the row's 2880 node-seconds, of which 26.5% is counted backoff sleep and 73.5% (9.42 ms/attempt) is UNACCOUNTED" is sound, and the find_slot hash-chain-walk hypothesis for that residue is untouched.
METHOD RULE THIS RECORD NOW CARRIES TWICE: before dividing any probe field by any other, check whether each is CUMULATIVE or LAST-VALUE.  Two separate wrong root causes in one session came from skipping that check — first naming a subtracted residue after an unmeasured mechanism, then dividing a per-iteration value by a cumulative count. || SESS481 SELF-CORRECTION, READ THIS BEFORE THE TWO PARAGRAPHS BELOW: the claim further down that "~74% of the cost is slot I/O service time" and "~9.6 ms per slot round trip" IS REFUTED, by direct probes on the SAME run.  wall_ms minus sleep_ms is not slot I/O; it is UNACCOUNTED, and it was labelled wrongly.  The direct service-time measurements from tests/evidence/run_crash_consistency_20260904T000831Z say a slot round trip is FAST: P297-TKT read_ms=2374 ms over reads=10756 gives 0.22 ms per slot read (n=3084 samples), and P138-AGWAIT caw_svc_ms=651 ms over reads=1754 gives 0.37 ms per CAW op (n=423).  Against a subtraction estimate of 9.42 ms/attempt that means roughly 96% of the non-sleep time in a contended unlock is in NEITHER the counted sleep NOR the device.  The same signature appears on the acquire side: P297-TKT el_ms mean 280.5 ms against slept_ms mean 37.2 and read_ms mean 0.77 — ~242 ms per acquire wait likewise unaccounted.  So the transport is not slow; something inside the CAW protocol's own loops is holding time that no counter sees.
HOST STARVATION IS EXCLUDED as the explanation: clyde has 56 CPUs and the board row recorded hostload=20.26, i.e. ~36% utilisation, so sleep overshoot from CPU oversubscription cannot account for it (30 VMs x 4 vcpu = 120 vcpu over 56 cores is 2.1x allocated but nowhere near saturated at that load).
WHERE IT MUST BE, FROM THE SOURCE: p381_t0 is stamped at dlm/dlm_caw.c:10559, AFTER the clear-window wait (lreq_clr_begin_wait, :10524), so wall_ms brackets only the retry loop.  The loop body contains exactly two unmeasured things: (1) caw_inode_backoff (:10566) sleeps WITHOUT being added to p381_sleep_ms — but it returns early for retry < 2 (dlm/dlm_caw.c:8069) and the MEDIAN unlock has retries=1, so it cannot explain the median gap of wall p50 20 ms against sleep p50 7 ms; (2) find_slot (:10567), which re-walks the resource's hash chain in MXFS_CAW_PROBE_SPAN = 16-slot span reads (dlm/dlm_caw.c:1427-1434) ON EVERY RETRY, even though the retry already holds slot_idx from the previous iteration.  HYPOTHESIS (not yet proven, do not patch on it): the unlock's cost is the repeated hash-chain walk, not the CAS and not the backoff.  If so the fix is cheap and local — a retry re-reads the ONE slot it already located instead of re-walking the chain — but it must be measured first.
INSTRUMENTATION LANDED 0.65.0 (UNBUILT at filing): P381-UNLK-CONTEND now also carries find_ms= and backoff_ms=, bracketing both call sites, so wall = sleep + find + backoff + residue is a closed account.  tools/caw_unlock_audit.py harvests it, prints the residue EXPLICITLY as unaccounted rather than mislabelling it, and refuses to call it slot I/O; it reports find_ms as NOT INSTRUMENTED for pre-0.65.0 logs so an old capture cannot be read as a new one.  Chain 128 (tests/sess481_chain128_create_cost.sh) builds it.
METHOD NOTE for whoever reads this next: the wrong attribution came from dividing a SUBTRACTED residue by attempts and naming the quotient after a mechanism nobody had measured.  A residue is not a measurement of the thing you suspect is in it.  The direct probes that refuted it were already shipping and cost nothing to harvest. || SESS481 CORRECTION TO FIX DIRECTION (b) BELOW, MADE BEFORE ANYONE BUILDS ON IT: the per-field-versioning idea does not work, and the reason is on-disk.  dlm/dlm_caw.h:35 sets MXFS_CAW_SLOT_SIZE = 512 and dlm/dlm_caw.h:321 carries a _Static_assert that sizeof(struct mxfs_caw_lock_slot) == 512 — one slot is EXACTLY ONE SECTOR, which is the granularity of the SCSI COMPARE-AND-WRITE.  The compare therefore covers all 512 bytes, i.e. every peer's waiter bit, not just the single uint32_t generation at dlm_caw.h:152.  Re-versioning fields inside the slot cannot help: any byte a peer writes anywhere in the sector miscompares every other node's in-flight RMW.  The false sharing is at the CAW PRIMITIVE's granularity, not at the struct's.  So (b) is really: SPLIT THE SLOT ACROSS SECTORS — holder state in one sector, waiter registration in another, so a releaser's bit clear and a waiter's registration are no longer the same compare-and-write.  That is an on-disk format change to a structure the architecture pins (the CAW slot table is fixed at 65536 slots on disk), so it needs a format version and a RULE-5 design review before any code.  It is not a reason to prefer (a); the two are independent and (a) is measurable first. || SESS481 MEASURED — THE BACKOFF-LADDER HYPOTHESIS BELOW IS REFUTED; THE COST IS SLOT I/O SERVICE TIME.  The discriminating measurement the next_step asked for already exists in the shipping build: P381-UNLK-CONTEND (dlm/dlm_caw.c:11238, added sess380 for D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE) reports per contended unlock: retries, miscmp, sleep_ms, wall_ms and a full miscompare-cause breakdown.  Harvested from tests/evidence/run_crash_consistency_20260904T000831Z/kernlog_test{1..32}.gz (0.64.37, sv EAD72FC7EC56BA505829901, 32 nodes, one 90 s crash_consistency row) — 17558 contended unlocks fleet-wide:
  retries   sum=30560  mean=1.7  p50=1  p90=3  max=12
  miscmp    sum=30560  mean=1.7  p50=1  p90=3  max=12
  sleep_ms  sum=163349 mean=9.3  p50=7  p90=20 max=94
  wall_ms   sum=616544 mean=35.1 p50=20 p90=78 max=471
  cause: contended=30487 (99.8%), multigen=28879 (94.5%), holders=1605, benign=73, noreg=3, and fast/ident/selfbits/removed/yieldto/control ALL ZERO.
THE SPLIT: mean wall 35.1 ms against mean sleep 9.3 ms leaves ~25.8 ms per unlock that is NOT the backoff ladder.  At mean 1+retries = 2.7 attempts that is ~9.6 ms per attempt, i.e. per slot read-modify-write round trip against the shared LUN.  So the escalating jitter accounts for about 26% of the cost and the remaining ~74% is slot I/O service time.  Removing the ladder — which sess5 proved orphans slot bits and convoys the cluster — could at best recover a quarter of this defect.
FLEET SCALE: 616.5 s of node-time inside contended unlocks against 32 nodes x 90 s = 2880 node-seconds of run, i.e. 21.4% of all node-time in that row is spent inside a contended unlock.
THE MECHANISM THE CAUSE BREAKDOWN NAMES: multigen is 94.5% of miscompares — the slot's generation moved between our read and our compare-and-write.  Every one of 26-28 peers is writing waiter bits into the SAME slot, and one version counter appears to cover the whole slot, so any peer write invalidates every other node's in-flight RMW.  With an RMW window of ~9.6 ms and 26-28 peers mutating, the window is far longer than the inter-arrival time of peer mutations, so miscompare is the normal outcome rather than the exception.  This is false sharing at the slot level, not lock contention: the releaser and the waiters are touching logically disjoint fields.  NOTE selfbits=0 and ident=0 across all 17558 samples — no unlock lost a race to its own bits, and none was a benign identical rewrite.
TWO FIX DIRECTIONS, NEITHER YET RULED: (a) reduce the SERVICE TIME of a slot operation — ~9.6 ms per round trip is 10-50x what the NVMe-backed SCST/iSCSI path should cost, and under this workload the device queue is loaded by the inode-acquire fast poll (mxfs_caw_inode_fastpoll, DEFAULT ON, ~32 slot reads per waiter per wait x 31 waiters against the one hot slot), so the poll storm is a live suspect for inflating the very service time this defect measures; (b) stop the false sharing — if waiter bits and holder bits were separately versioned (or in disjoint sectors), a releaser's bit clear would not miscompare against waiter churn at all, and the retry term would collapse without touching the ladder that sess5's evidence requires.
CONSEQUENCE FOR D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE: sess481's ceiling ruling on that record says lock-HANDOFF tuning cannot make the crash_consistency row pass, and that stands.  But this measurement shows the fastpoll A/B queued there may matter through a different route than the one it was ruled against: not by shortening the handoff, but by unloading the device queue that sets slot-operation service time, which is inside the WORK term.  Read chain 127's result with that in mind. || NOT YET PROVEN -- do not patch on this paragraph. The leading hypothesis is the anti-CAS-storm unlock backoff: mxfs_caw_unlock_backoff (dlm/dlm_caw.c:534) is DEFAULT ON and, on an INODE-unlock CAS miscompare, sleeps a node-phased retry-escalating jitter of 1..~15 ms and keeps retrying (wall-clock bounded rather than count-bounded, dlm/dlm_caw.c:10458-10459) instead of returning -EIO. That behaviour is deliberate and load-bearing -- with it OFF, sess5 measured an unlock losing 100 tight retries against 8-node waiter-bit churn, orphaning the slot bit and convoying every peer 300 s+ on a lock nobody held. So the escalating backoff must NOT simply be removed. Under the crash_consistency workload the releasing node is CAS-ing a slot that 26-28 peers are concurrently writing waiter bits into, so miscompares are the norm rather than the exception and the escalation ladder is climbed on nearly every release. Competing candidates that the measurement does not yet exclude: target-side COMPARE-AND-WRITE emulation cost in SCST, the CAW command queueing behind the fastpoll read traffic of 31 waiters on the same slot (mxfs_caw_inode_fastpoll, DEFAULT ON, adds ~32 slot reads per waiter per wait), forced-unit-access/flush ordering on the CAW command, or scheduling delay before submission.
defects.found: sess481, measured on the 0.64.37 board run 20260904T000831Z (mxfs.ko srcversion EAD72FC7EC56BA505829901), 32 nodes / caw, crash_consistency row.
defects.next: 1) THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT, before any patch: instrument the wire unlock to separate software retry from device service time. Count, per unlock: CAS attempts, miscompares, total sleep time in the backoff ladder, and the submit->complete latency of each individual CAW command. If sleep time dominates, the ladder is the cause and the fix is to shorten/replace the escalation (e.g. bounded immediate re-CAS on a miscompare whose delta is only a waiter-bit change -- caw_unlk_delta_is_registration at dlm/dlm_caw.c:10396 already classifies exactly that case, and mxfs_caw_unlock_fastretry / _max=4 / _ms=8 at dlm/dlm_caw.c:223-238 already exist but default OFF). If device service time dominates, the cause is at the target and the fix is elsewhere. 2) In the SAME run collect SCSI opcode / sector-range / queue-depth counts so the fastpoll read traffic on the hot slot can be separated from the CAW traffic. 3) Do NOT disable mxfs_caw_unlock_backoff to make the number look better: sess5 proved that path orphans slot bits and convoys the cluster.

defects.summary: The UNMOUNT AG-release path publishes AG grants to peers without the drain pipeline the invariant requires, and does so BEFORE this node's metadata is pushed to the platter. mxfs_dlm_ag_force_release_all (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~49924) runs exactly ONE drain -- mxfs_dlm_ag_drain_alloc_buflist -- before its mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock. The cooperative release path runs NINE steps before its unlock: drain_alloc_buflist, drain_inode_buffers, blkdev_flush_epoch, drain_meta_buffers, blkdev_flush_epoch, xfs_log_force(XFS_LOG_SYNC), a second drain_meta_buffers (the sess43 fix), a bounded meta_pending wait for in-flight bios, and a final flush. The unmount path omits eight of the nine, and mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock (dlm/v5_mount.c ~15071) is a pure release primitive -- a TCP unlock or a CAW slot CAS behind a release gate -- so nothing internal covers the omission.
defects.evidence: SESS482 THE ORDERING CLAIM, VERIFIED EXHAUSTIVELY RATHER THAN BY LINE-RANGE SEARCH (this is the load-bearing fact of the whole record, so it was checked twice by different means). Grepping the WHOLE of pal/linux/xfs_super.c for xfs_ail_push / xfs_log_force / xfs_log_quiesce returns call sites at only lines 981 and 1051 (both inside xfs_fs_sync_fs, which the VFS runs before put_super), 1253, and 1797 -- every one of them BEFORE xfs_fs_put_super begins at line 1919. Line 1938 is a comment, not a call. So between the start of put_super and the AG release at 2066 there is no AIL push, no log force and no log quiesce anywhere in this file, and the two non-trivial helpers called in that window were checked individually: mxfs_iclus_purge_all (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~57569) contains no ail_push, log_force, blkdev_flush, drain, bwrite or iflush, and mxfs_sb_late_dirty_prearm is a prearm, not a flush. The next quiesce is mxfs_departure_quiescing at 2173 and then xfs_unmountfs at 2175 -- both AFTER the release. Two independent corroborations that this ordering is real and not an artefact of reading: (1) D-SB-PERNODE-DIVERGENT-WHOLE-LOG-LOST-UPDATE-0133 measured the same inversion from the other side, P-SB-SUMMARY-LOCK rc=-19 on 96/96 attempts because 'xfs_fs_put_super tears the DLM down (m_mxfs_dlm=NULL, v5 shutdown) BEFORE xfs_unmountfs -> xfs_log_quiesce where the lock lived'; (2) the STANDALONE DLM mount path does the opposite and says so -- dlm/mount.c ~2732 releases the cached AG lock with the comment 'flush dirty AG metadata to disk before the bulk DLM release below. Must happen while DLM is still alive' immediately before mxfs_dlm_release_all / mxfs_dlm_caw_release_all. That path got the ordering right; the kernel put_super path is the one that did not. || Source-proven, by reading each site rather than inferring: the unmount release loop and its single drain at xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~49924-49970; the nine-step cooperative pipeline at ~49457-49710; mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock's body at dlm/v5_mount.c ~15071 confirming it is a pure release primitive; the call at pal/linux/xfs_super.c:2066 and xfs_unmountfs at :2175 in the same function, with no AIL push or log force between the function's start and 2066; the rel_epoch asymmetry at ~39140 versus ~49956 and its consumers at xfs/xfs_inode.c ~8531 and ~10051; and the audit's four early exits at ~42868 onwards. Negative evidence, stated as such and now known to be uninterpretable: zero occurrences of 'site=unmount' across all 938 retained evidence directories -- which, until the 0.67.0 counters run, cannot be distinguished from the audit having declined every call.
defects.mechanism: TWO DISTINCT EXPOSURES, both following from one ordering fact. THE ORDERING: the call is made from pal/linux/xfs_super.c:2066 inside xfs_fs_put_super, and xfs_unmountfs -- where the synchronous log quiesce, AIL push and buftarg drain happen -- is at line 2175 of the SAME function. Nothing between the top of put_super and 2066 pushes the AIL or forces the log. (A) PEER READS STALE: the AG is published as free while this node's AG-meta may still be in-core-ahead-of-disk. The cooperative path's own sess43 comment states this consequence exactly, for exactly the step omitted here: the just-dirtied AG-meta -- 'AGI (agi_unlinked / freecount), AGF (freeblks), inobt/finobt' -- is 'left in-core-ahead-of-disk at unlock ... so the peer's FUA read at acquire MISSES them -> stale-behind AGI unlinked-list head ... -> xfs_iunlink_remove_inode corruption + shutdown'. (B) WE CLOBBER THE PEER, which may be the sharper one: after the grant is released at 2066, xfs_unmountfs at 2175 pushes THIS node's AIL. A peer that acquired the AG in that window and modified AG-meta is durably REVERTED by our later writeback -- the same durable-clobber shape b_mxfs_relepoch exists to prevent for directory blocks. An asymmetry makes (B) worse: the cooperative release records pag_mxfs_rel_epoch from pag_mxfs_grant_epoch before zeroing it (~39140), while the unmount path zeroes pag_mxfs_grant_epoch (~49956) WITHOUT setting pag_mxfs_rel_epoch, so the retiring-token guards that read it (xfs/xfs_inode.c ~8531, ~10051, both gated on rel_epoch != 0) are inert on this path. WHY THE HARDENING MISSED THIS PATH, which is the class lesson: D-AGI-UNLINKED-CROSSNODE-RECOVERY-SHUTDOWN (CLOSED) records the sess385 fix as 'drain_alloc_buflist + drain_inode_buffers now run BEFORE the first drain_meta_buffers, with a blkdev flush between, so the AGI is written AFTER the dinodes it points at'. That ordering work went into the COOPERATIVE path. The unmount path was not brought along, and there are two release paths reaching the same primitive.
defects.found: sess482, by auditing Architectural Invariant #1 ('no on-disk DLM unlock without a completed drain pipeline') against every call site of mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock. Not from a failing run.
defects.next: SESS485: THE FIX FOR THIS RECORD AND FOR D-UNMOUNT-AG-GRANTS-PUBLISHED-BEFORE-METADATA-QUIESCE-0483 IS ONE CHANGE, LANDED 0.69.3 (scratch sv CDF771BA78E0A190B600393; see that record's sess485 entry for the full design and the GPT review). What this record asked for is now in mxfs_dlm_ag_force_release_all (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c): the release is two-phase — phase 1 runs drain_alloc_buflist + drain_inode_buffers + drain_meta_buffers for every AG under held grants, then one xfs_log_force(SYNC), the sess43 second drain_meta_buffers pass and ONE mxfs_blkdev_flush_epoch for the whole unmount (not three per AG: the RULE 0 concern in step 1 of the sess482 plan is answered by flushing once), and phase 2 flips state and calls mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock per AG. The ordering half — exposure (B), our later AIL push clobbering a peer — is removed at the source: put_super now runs xfs_unmountfs_prepare, the sealed SB summary sync and an explicit log force + xfs_ail_push_all_sync + xfs_buftarg_wait BEFORE the release, so there is no later AIL push of anything dirty. Step 4 of the sess482 plan (count dirty-at-release) exists as ags_drained on P482-UMOUNT-AGREL plus P485-UMOUNT-DRAIN per AG, expected 0 after the quiesce. Step 5 (exposure B needs a cross-node test) is superseded: with nothing written after publication there is no clobber to observe, and the after-publication counters on P483-AGFREE-WINDOW are the witness. CLOSE TOGETHER WITH 0483 on chain 133's verdict (tests/sess485_chain133_agfree_hoist_ab.sh), never separately: the two records are the drain half and the exclusion half of one defect.

defects.summary: On the 0.69.2 unmount ordering (AG grants published, then the final SB summary sync and xfs_unmountfs), 23 of 32 nodes that closed 400 unlinked-but-open files and ran umount in the same shell command NEVER RETURNED from umount within the 240 s budget. Every one of the 23 printed P482-UMOUNT-AGREL (the grants were published) at 04:30:12Z and then nothing further that the sweep captured — no P-SB-SEALED, no P483-AGFREE-WINDOW, no P483-AGMETA-AFTER-AGFREE (so no AG-metadata write was issued after publication before the stall). The 9 nodes that completed did so in about one second and had no inactivation left at put_super. The 23 hung nodes were then power-cycled by the next leg's prep, and node journals are volatile, so where they were stuck is UNKNOWN. On 0.69.3 (the D-0483 hoist) the identical workload unmounted 32/32 in 15 s, which is regression evidence for the new ordering and is NOT a disposition of this record: the changed ordering could avoid several unrelated waits.
defects.evidence: tests/evidence/sess485_agfree_hoist_s485a/base/work.txt: 32 nodes report made=400 held=400; 9 report 'RC=0 UNMOUNTED' (test2,5,7,9,13,15,28,31,32); 23 report no rc. base/p483_testN.txt for each of the 23: exactly two lines, P482-UMOUNT-AGREL ags_seen=63 ags_released=1 and P482-AGIFC-AUDIT-COVERAGE calls=1 ran=1, both at 04:30:12; the sweep ran at ~04:34 while the nodes were still hung, so the absence of any later matching line is real for the patterns the filter carried (P483-|P485-|P482-UMOUNT-AGREL|P482-AGIFC-AUDIT-COVERAGE|P-AGIFC-RELEASE-MISMATCH|P-SB-SEAL-|P-SB-SUMMARY-FINAL) — the filter did NOT carry hung-task, P-SB-SUMMARY-LOCK, P6S-ARM-REFUSED or CAW-poll lines, which is why the stall site is unknown. base/chk.txt rc=4 with 404 ERROR lines was taken on a NON-QUIESCENT image (23 mounts still up mid-unmount) and is not a platter verdict. The fix leg on the same harness, same prep, same workload: umount wall 15 s, 32/32 clean, chk 0 errors.
defects.mechanism: SESS487 LAP 3 MEASURED (chain 135 s487a base leg, frozen 0.69.2, 28/32 hung, stacks captured before reboot — tests/evidence/sess485_agfree_hoist_s487a/base/hang_test*.txt, kjournal_test*.txt; prose digest in the sess487 ccmemory): candidate (b) IS the fleet-wide shape and the holder's stall is the AIL. 26/28 umount tasks: state S in caw_nudge_wait <- caw_acquire_poll_sleep <- caw_wait_for_grant <- caw_lock_body <- mxfs_dlm_caw_lock <- mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock <- mxfs_sb_summary_lock <- mxfs_sb_summary_final_sync <- xfs_fs_put_super (waiting for the cluster-wide SB summary EX lock); 1/28 (test10) the same chain inside the slot read. 1/28 (test1) — the ONLY node with a P-SB-SUMMARY-LOCK line, i.e. the holder — state D in xfs_ail_push_all_sync <- xfs_log_quiesce <- put_super, with 480 P126-XFSAILD-SKIP-AGMETA lines after its P482-UMOUNT-AGREL (xfsaild refusing dirty AG-metadata items for AGs whose grant it had published), 460 P88-PUBOB-RECLAIM-REFUSED, 370 P141-UNLK-EXCLR; the 27 waiters log P-SB-SUMMARY-BAST (refused while held, D-0537 rule). The 4 nodes that reached the lock before test1 unmounted in ~1 s. No hung-task warnings, no shutdowns. Candidates (a) and (c) and sess487's (d) are NOT what the stacks show (no AG acquire, no inode DLM acquire, no iclus path in any umount or worker stack). GPT RULE-5 ruling (sess487): occurrence reproduced; SB-lock amplification PROVEN; the chain 'post-publication inactivation -> dirty AG-meta AIL item for a published AG -> refused by xfsaild -> xfs_ail_push_all_sync never completes' is strongly supported but strict proof needs item/LSN correlation (the P126 line carries no item identity — filed as D-AIL-UNHELD-GRANT-SKIP-PERMANENT-SILENT-PIN-0487 next step 1). The lock scope itself is filed as D-SB-SUMMARY-LOCK-HELD-ACROSS-UNBOUNDED-LOG-QUIESCE-FLEET-CONVOY-0487. On 0.69.3 the same workload unmounted 28/28 measured nodes cleanly (4 unmeasured by a harness bug, no kernel hang on them). || SESS487 CANDIDATE (d), code-derived, UNMEASURED: on 0.69.2 mxfs_iclus_purge_all ran BEFORE the inactivation flush inside mxfs_sb_summary_final_sync (0.69.3 moved the purge after the flush, sess485 memory). purge_all (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~57697) removes and kfrees every inode-cluster lock object of the mount WITHOUT releasing their on-disk grants (those are swept by caw release_all inside v5_shutdown), so an inactivation that then takes a cluster lock (mxfs_iclus_lock ~57015) builds a NEW object at disk_mode NL over a slot that still carries this node's own EX bit: the claim self-EDEADLKs, fan_out has nothing to arm, and the SELFCLEAR escape refuses while any covered sibling is active — which with hundreds of siblings in the same clusters being inactivated concurrently is the normal state — so the caller retries into the documented '32 nodes starved 380s+' livelock shape (P-ICLUS-SELFCLEAR 'NOT cleared' ratelimited). defects.summary: The directory LEAF hash index (a derived structure) can be left durably inconsistent with the directory's DATA blocks after a node death and foreign replay: readdir lists a name whose hashed lookup returns ENOENT, or the hash index reflects an unlink whose data block still carries the dirent. Since sess22 MXFS has masked the lookup face with mxfs_dir2_datascan_lookup (xfs/libxfs/xfs_dir2_leaf.c ~1842): on every ENOENT in a multi-node directory it linearly reads EVERY data block looking for the name, and the remove path has a twin (mxfs_dir2_leafless_removename) that expunges a dirent the leaf does not reference. On 2026-09-04 the heal fired for real (P22-DATASCAN-HIT) in two events: (1) 08:36:45-51, dir ino 75513091, names node17_f42.md5..node17_f45.md5 (the LAST four adds of one node) at data block 58 of 63, healed on test1/14/15/16 (76 lines; the five run directories 083456Z..085524Z that carry them share one boot journal), a hole in the direction DATA-AHEAD-OF-LEAF; (2) 10:49:14-21, dir ino 117440640, names pre_0001/0011/0021/0031/0041_xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx at block 0 of 3 on test2/test4 — this one is the D-0492 crash-durability CONTROL lap s493f on the deliberately buggy 0.70.9 build (RESULT FAIL unlinked-reappeared 5/5): block 0 reverted below the victim's fsync'd unlinks while the leaf kept their removal, LEAF-AHEAD-OF-DATA, and the heal resurrected dirents pointing at freed inodes (P26-IGET-FAIL err=-2). Event (2) is the closed D-0492 defect reproduced on purpose; event (1) is the live population on a current build. Either direction is the same class: after death+replay the directory's data and index blocks sit at different points in history. The root that leaves them torn was never ledgered: the heal made the lookup face disappear from every board row.

defects.mechanism: UNPROVEN, two candidates (RULE-5 review sess496). (1) Durability cut at a kill: MXFS destages directory DATA blocks OUT-OF-LOG at grant release (direct write + flush) while the LEAF block's update travels through the CIL; if the node dies after the data flush but before the CIL record carrying the leaf update is forced (or before the leaf home write), the peer's foreign replay recovers the last committed leaf state, which predates the tail adds — data present, hash entries absent, durably. The 'last N adds of one node' shape and the persistence across replays fit this. (2) Stale foreign replay: a foreign log slice carries an OLDER image of the same leaf block and replay applies it over a newer home image without a globally ordered per-buffer veto (the D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES family). The no-crash occurrence (pre_0041 in chain-139 rows) says at least one path forms holes in live operation: candidates are the release drain writing a stale leaf image, a leaf rebuild/compaction or block->leaf/leaf->node conversion omitting entries, or a late notification-driven invalidate replacing an in-core leaf with a stale platter image. Consequences today: (a) every ENOENT lookup in a shared directory whose coherency key moved pays an O(dir) cold data-block walk — measured p90 20, max 35 reads per create lookup, the 4.85 ms term that keeps the crash_consistency board row red; (b) the heal is name-specific, so any attempt to gate it (e.g. per-tenure) turns a hole for name B into a DUPLICATE dirent on create(B) or an ENOENT on unlink/rename of B; (c) a lookup path that does not route through the heal (any caller bypassing xfs_dir_lookup_args' ENOENT tail) sees the hole.

defects.next:
SESS577: ONE CANDIDATE DISPOSED BY REASONING, THE DECISIVE INSTRUMENT NOW EXISTS, AND 232 CLEAN WITNESSES AT 2/TCP INCLUDING ACROSS A NODE DEATH. RECORD STAYS OPEN.

CANDIDATE 1 (durability cut at a kill: DATA destaged out-of-log at release while the LEAF update is still in the CIL) IS DEAD, and not for lack of reproduction. A design consult established that under a log force that actually covers the transaction, a skipped LEAF home write is not a durability hole at all: recovery supplies the LEAF update, so the crash cut data=T / leaf=T-1 is harmless. The only premise that could have rescued the candidate was that the log force does not really persist, since the journal writes ride bio REQ_PREFLUSH/REQ_FUA (xfs_log.c 2889 and 2906) rather than the explicit SCSI WRITE(16)+FUA helper this project built because the target drops those bio flags. That premise was checked and does not apply: pal/linux/xfs_super.c 3264 declares a COHERENCE-ONLY durability domain in which target power loss is explicitly out of scope, and this defect is NODE death, which is in scope, where the journal lives in the target coherent cache and the survivor reads it. So the force is sufficient for the in-scope failure mode and candidate 1 cannot produce this tear.

A THIRD REPAIR WAS FOUND, AND IT SAT EXACTLY WHERE THE MEASUREMENT HAD TO BE TAKEN. This record names two masks, the datascan lookup heal and the leafless removename, and every prior experiment toggled those through dir_datascan_heal. mxfs_dir_rebuild_leaf_from_data is a third, on a SEPARATE knob (dir_leaf_rebuild, default 1), fired from xfs_dir_createname gated on a flag armed once per cross-node tenure and consumed BEFORE that tenure first mutation. The leaf it finds there is the one the node ACQUIRED from the handoff. It rebuilt that leaf from the data blocks and reported only the rebuilt count, so a directory that arrived torn was made whole in place and never reached a board row. That is why every instrument aimed at this defect, all of which look after recovery, found nothing: the repair was consuming the measurement at the one point an incoherent acquisition is visible.

WHAT LANDED, 0.79.0: the rebuild now snapshots the acquired hashval/address set before overwriting it and diffs it against the derived set in one merge pass over entries already in hand. missing means present in the data and absent from the acquired index, which is the readdir-lists-it / lookup-ENOENTs face. extra means the index references a dirent the data does not carry. Both outcomes are reported, P496-ACQ-DIVERGE and P496-ACQ-CLEAN, because an instrument that speaks only on failure cannot be distinguished from one that never ran. Report-only, no behaviour change, no extra I/O, and the repair is untouched. Detection is now separable from repair, which the earlier ruling on retiring the masks required and which nothing in the tree previously provided.

MEASURED, AND NON-VACUOUS. Lap s577a, tests/sess493_d0492_crash_durability.sh at 2 nodes over TCP, build 77B44618AD2DA40BC1A3C38, MODARGS dir_datascan_heal=0 with the harness own capture confirming heal=0 on every node, so a leaf hole would have failed the verify instead of being repaired at lookup. 12/12 rounds, victim test1 destroyed with the attempt standing, survivor fenced and replayed, RESULT PASS missing=0 extra=0, replay_complete=1, refused=0, quarantine=0, shutdown=0. On the survivor: 196 acquisition censuses on the lap shared directory and 33 on the earlier shared-dir reuse workload, 229 total, EVERY ONE CLEAN, zero divergence. The coverage check is exact, 229 censuses against 229 rebuilds, so the instrument fired on every repair rather than going silent. A separate earlier run of dir_reuse_coherency gave 36 more clean censuses against 36 rebuilds and PASSED 2/2 at 106s of a 120s budget, so the census costs nothing measurable.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, STATED PLAINLY. It is a bounded negative, not a disposition. 38 further rebuilds declined on directory format, so the window covers single-leaf directories only and says nothing about node-format ones. The diff ran against this node in-core data blocks, not the platter image, because the platter-union arm is behind dir_leaf_rebuild=2 and that arm is known delete-unsafe, so it was deliberately not enabled. The lap is SINGLE-WITNESS by construction at two nodes. And the live population in this record, node17_f42..f45.md5 on dir 75513091, came from a 32-node workload that this shape does not cover. The victim own pre-crash census is unrecoverable in any case because its journal is volatile and it was power-cycled.

NEXT, IN ORDER. 1) Extend the census to node/BTREE-format directories, since the rebuild bails there and that is where the original 32-node evidence lived; the bail counter already tells you how much population is being skipped. 2) Get a durable-source comparison without enabling the delete-unsafe union: read the platter image for the diff only, never feeding it into the rebuilt leaf. 3) Repeat laps for a witness count rather than trusting one. 4) The remaining live candidate is stale foreign replay applying an older leaf image over a newer home image; the census now gives the before-and-after pair at the acquiring node that this hypothesis needs, so instrument the replay decision for leaf buffers and correlate its disposition against the next acquisition census on the same directory.

defects.summary: A node whose inode acquire waits behind a LIVE peer's grant for longer than its retry budget (TCP: 3 attempts x 60 retries x 1 s = 180 s; CAW: 120 s base liveness-extended to a 480 s cap) shuts its OWN filesystem down (mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin arm (3), 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable ... shutting down filesystem', SHUTDOWN_CORRUPT_INCORE), withdraws, and is then fenced by the survivor for the withdraw. Measured on the 2-node TCP ship shape: test1 held ino 131 with its release drain paused (D-512 T2 pausepoint, 300 s) while the rejoined test2 ran md5sum on the file; test2 logged P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE x180 / P36-RETRY x177 over 184 s (retries_left 59->0 three times, P36-STACK x3), then 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable: ino=131 mode=3 rc=-110 comm=md5sum' at 197.28 s uptime, 'Corruption of in-memory data (0x8) at mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin' (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:34562), P-SESSION-POISON, P-WITHDRAW, P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP; test1 fenced it (EXCLUSIVE_WRITE_GATE) and test2 self-fenced (P131-SELF-FENCE PR_CONFLICT_FENCED) at 255 s. test1's pause ended normally at 17699.76 (P-D512-RELPAUSE-END, 323 s after P-D512-RELPAUSE at 17376.19), i.e. the holder released 140 s after the requester had killed itself. The pause was injected, but any release drain that outlasts the budget (a large dirty file on a slow LUN, a holder throttled by the target) produces the same outcome: a reader of a file another node is writing crashes its mount, loses its own dirty data, and must be remounted. A slow release is a performance fact; the requester's suicide is a stability defect.
defects.evidence: tests/evidence/20260905T113200Z_d0287_2node_s517g/dmesg_test2_boot_live_s518.txt (test2's whole post-restart boot: mount 0.85 s, admitted at active_count=2, md5sum ino=131 PR from 13.80 s to 197.23 s, shutdown 197.28 s, self-fence 255.20 s); dmesg_test1_live_s518.txt (P-D512-RELPAUSE 17376.19 -> P-D512-RELPAUSE-END 17699.76, P163-WITHDRAW-SEEN 17678.97, second P164-DEAD-NOTE 17682.87, 525 'unknown node' heartbeats from the withdrawn zombie mount after 17688.94); d0287_2node_s517g.console (fails=3: pause-end seen=0, md5 differ, 1 shutdown on test2).
defects.mechanism: Code-proven sess518. xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin: the slow path calls mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed 3 times (attempt<3, 50 ms apart); each descends to mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock -> mxfs_dlm_lock -> mxfs_dlm_lock_retries(60) on TCP (dlm/dlm.c: dlm_lock_impl remote arm sends LOCK_REQ, pending_wait(MXFS_LOCK_ACQUIRE_WAIT_MS=1000) -> -ETIMEDOUT -> P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE/P36-RETRY, re-send; the last retry returns -ETIMEDOUT) or mxfs_dlm_caw_lock on CAW (120 s base, P-WAIT-EXTEND while holders_alive_fn says the blockers heartbeat, MXFS_CAW_WAIT_HARDCAP_MS=480000 hard cap, then -ETIMEDOUT). The timeout classifier then has three arms: (1) quarantined domain -> EIO no shutdown; -EHOSTDOWN (holder/master dead and RECOVERY_BLOCKED/refused) -> EIO; (2) a dead slot bit pending recovery -> park (P240-QUAR-PARK); (3) everything else -> 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable' + xfs_force_shutdown(SHUTDOWN_CORRUPT_INCORE). Arm (3) never asks whether the party the request waits on is alive: on TCP the requester cannot see the remote master's holder table at all (dlm.c:4202 comment), and on a local master the holders are named (P-LKTIMEOUT-HOLDER) but their liveness is not consulted. A live holder mid-release therefore reads exactly like a coordination failure. The bounded second-inode acquire (P-ABBA-BOUNDED-TIMEOUT) and the recovery-context requeue (P-RECOV-ACQ-REQUEUE) return before the classifier and are not affected.

defects.summary: When both nodes of the cluster unmount at the same time, each node's clean departure sends its remaining grant releases to their master, which is the peer, and the peer has already begun its own teardown and drops LOCK_RELEASE messages (P-TEARDOWN-MSG-DROP: after ctx->mounted clears only NODE_LEAVE and RELEASE_ACK pass). The releaser resends three times and then waits the whole 3 s ack bound (P-TAUTH-RELEASE-WAIT unacked=N after 3000ms) before completing the unmount, so a whole-cluster shutdown costs every node 3 s plus the quiesce (4.5 to 8.9 s per unmount measured against a native XFS unmount of well under a second), and the peer-mastered ACTIVE records of the departed incarnation stay on the platter for the next mount to import as blockers and release as residue (P-TAUTH-IMPORT-RESIDUE) instead of being retired at departure. 0.75.17 fixed the single-departure shape (the ACK was being dropped); the concurrent shape drops the RELEASE itself.

Each node is the master of half the pages, so half of every node's releases are addressed to a peer that is itself past the quiesce. What is NOT yet measured: the cost the retained records impose on the next whole-cluster mount without a re-mkfs (import-residue count and its wall), and whether MODE=serial unmounts (the control) complete in the sub-second the quiesce alone needs.

The takeover's platter pass is now ~2.4 s for 206 MiB (about 86 MiB/s) and its 212 page prepares+activations another 2.4 s; both are recovery-time costs on the survivor after a DEATH, not unmount costs. STILL OPEN FOR MECHANISM (2): the concurrent-unmount LOCK_RELEASE drop at a tearing-down master (v5_mount.c ~1158 passes only NODE_LEAVE + RELEASE_ACK through the quiesce; the releaser resends every MXFS_DLM_RELEASE_RETRY_MS=1000 ms and mxfs_dlm_wait_release_acks bounds at 3 s). The idle parallel laps show no wait because an idle mount has no cross-mastered grant left; the post-workload parallel unload (chain s550, WORKLOAD=agmeta_stale_leak_2node) is the measurement for it. Design under consideration: pass LOCK_RELEASE through the quiesce once the departing node's own release_all walk has finished (no local entry can then be promoted; process_remote_release only commits the retirement on a page this node still masters and acks), until its GOODBYE; a page already PREPARED by handoff_depart refuses the commit and the ack says REMASTER, so the releaser re-routes as today. || SESS544 ATTRIBUTED from the P-DEPART-WORK lines (s545d test2, s545b test1, s544g test2): purge_ms=4568/3969/4412 and takeover scan_ms=4371/3975 over scanned=26426 pages (cand=0-5, pages_prepared=0) — each pass reads BOTH copies of every page (2 x 26426 x 4 KiB = 206 MiB) at the LUN's ~50 MiB/s, twice per departure = 8-9 s, for a handful of candidates. FIX SHAPE (measurements first): (a) the purge needs no platter scan — a page can only be ACTIVE(self) through this node's own cache (commit/activate require the cached page ACTIVE(self)), so walk the cached pages instead of the region; (b) the takeover's candidate selection needs only each copy's 128-byte header (auth_node/authority_epoch), so scan headers (26 MiB, ~0.5 s) and read full pages only for candidates; (c) both scans share one pass. Verify: P-DEPART-WORK purge_ms + takeover_ms under 500 ms on the 26426-page rig, unmount wall under 1 s serial, and the same records retired (cand and imported_dropped unchanged). || SESS544 serial CONTROL measured (tests/fleet_unload_check.sh MODE=serial s545d, 0.75.64 sv 90BA2F91, idle fresh mount, tests/evidence/20260908T214051Z_unload_s545d): first node out (test1, peer still up) umount 619 ms, no release wait; LAST node out (test2) umount 4776 ms with NO release wait either — its timeline: P-SB-SEALED at +0.08 s, P-TAUTH-PURGE-OWNER +0.38 s, P304-PR-WORKER +0.53 s, then nothing until P-TAUTH-TAKEOVER / P-DEPART-WORK / P-RELALL-* / P-GOODBYE-SENT / P-SB-SEAL-OK all at +4.75 s. In the parallel case (s545b test1, 8466 ms): PURGE-OWNER at +4.4 s, TAKEOVER/DEPART-WORK/GOODBYE-SENT at +8.4 s. So the unmount wall is dominated by the departure ledger passes (the peer's purge + takeover over the whole tauth region, ~4 s each, run on the departing node for the peer that left before it, serialized ahead of its own release_all/GOODBYE), plus the 3 s unacked-release wait only in the concurrent shape. Two mechanisms: (1) the sole-survivor/last-out node runs the departed peer's purge+takeover passes (~4 s of region reads) BEFORE its own departure work, and the first-out node in the parallel case does the same for its peer; (2) the dropped LOCK_RELEASE at a tearing-down master. Both are RULE 0 unmount pace; native umount is sub-second. defects.summary: A clean unmount of one node while its peer stays mounted takes 35-80 s on the TCP transport, spent handing the departing node's authority-ledger pages to the survivor one page at a time (P-TAUTH-HANDOFF why=view-change, about 12 ms per page, 6700 pages), and for that whole window the survivor's lock requests to the departing master go unanswered: its periodic superblock-cover worker retried an EX acquire of the summary lock once a second for 32 s (P36-RETRY retries_left 59 down to 28, a P36-STACK wait-site dump on the first timeout), and its own later umount timed out once taking PR on the root inode. Native XFS unmounts in about a second; nothing corrupts and nothing shuts down, but a survivor workload that needs any resource the departing node masters stalls for the length of the handoff.
defects.evidence: Measured 2026-09-13 on 0.85.1 build 8330C6DFDB0B731E3308020, two nodes/TCP, the cold-check epilogue of tests/d0946_disklive_knob_vs_aging.sh (umount A with B mounted, then umount B). s615d: test2 saw P-TAUTH-DEPARTING-RX from test1 at 1625.27 (test2 uptime), then P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE/P36-RETRY on type=1 ino=754974721 (the SB summary lock, comm=kworker/2:0, req=EX, master=test1) every 1.02 s from 1626.72 to 1658.46 (32 retries), test1's P163-CLEAN-DEPART observed at 1661.15, the cover write then completed at 1661.22 as sole survivor; test2's own umount ran 1658.28-1661.71. s615e: test1's P-TAUTH-HANDOFF why=view-change page=0 at 2141.07 (test1 uptime) through P-GOODBYE-SENT at 2221.03 and DLM shutdown complete at 2221.04 = 80 s, 6771 handoff lines in the ring; test2's umount P36-RETRY ino=128 mode=PR retries_left=59 at 1909.85 (one timeout, then served). The lap wall rose from 107 s (0.75.128, s574iwr, no cold check) to 203 s / 238 s with the epilogue, most of it the unmount. Evidence: tests/evidence/d0957_s615_test2_lockwait.txt, tests/evidence/d0957_s615_test2_calltrace.txt, tests/evidence/d0957_s615_test1_depart.txt, tests/evidence/d0946disklive_s615d.console, tests/evidence/d0946disklive_s615e.console. Related: D-0925 (both nodes unmounting at once, 3 s waits), the sess593 ledger-page takeover measurement (13 ms/page inside recovery-complete) which is the death-side mirror of this clean-departure handoff. || sess616 (0.85.3 414769E4): the same handoff window also stalls a MOUNT: in the cold-check epilogues of d0952coh s616b/s616c, test2's remount right after test1's remount timed out once taking EX on the root inode (P36-STACK ino=128 mode=EX comm=mount at test2 uptime 5127 and 5336, mxfs_iget_root_fallible <- xfs_mountfs), and in s616d its rejoin mount timed out twice on the AG lock (P-LKTIMEOUT-REMOTE type=3 ino=0 master=37494790 at 5370/5371) while test1 was handing 6700 ledger pages to it (P-TAUTH-HANDOFF why=view-change from test1 5681.88). Each mount then succeeded.
defects.next: 1. Time the unmount itself: add UMOUNT_A wall to the d0946 cold-check epilogue and to depart_takeover_unmount.sh, and count P-TAUTH-HANDOFF why=view-change lines between P-TAUTH-DEPARTING and P-GOODBYE-SENT on the departing node, so the per-page cost and the page count are one line per lap. 2. Establish why a page costs ~12 ms (one round trip per page? a synchronous commit per page?) with a probe that stamps the handoff of one page from send to ack; a batched or bulk handoff is the obvious shape but must be designed against the ledger's single-writer rule (D-0341, D-0347). 3. Decide whether lock requests to a node that has announced departure should be re-routed to the successor master as soon as the departing node stops serving them, instead of retrying against it once a second until it is gone; the survivor's cover worker and umount both waited the full window. 4. Verify with both nodes' dmesg windowed to the departure marks, and with the survivor running a workload that touches resources the departing node masters.
defects.impact_why: Pace: the departing node's page handoff took 35-80 s (6771 pages at about 12 ms, s615e) and every stalled request on the survivor was then served: the SB cover worker consumed 32 of its retries (retries_left 59 down to 28) and completed at 1661.22, test2's own umount timed out once (retries_left=59) and was served, both unmounts returned; nothing corrupted, hung or shut down. The measured stall stays inside the 180 s acquire budget; a residue that pushed the handoff past that budget would be new evidence and re-adjudicates this.

defects.summary: On the TCP transport a node mounting while its peer is up waits a full BAST period, about 10 s, for its EX request on the root directory inode (ino 128), because the peer holds the root at PR (cached, state GRANTED) and its release only arrives on the next BAST cycle; the mount therefore takes 10 s longer than the operation costs. A file read on the rejoined node also waited 1.56 s on a PR acquire in the same laps. Nothing hangs and nothing shuts down; this is pace, not stability, and does not block the 2-node TCP release bar.
defects.evidence: Measured 2026-09-13 on 0.85.5 module 45B8EB0F812B0167A4CCF9E, 2 nodes/TCP, during the D-0966 verification laps (tests/d0952_sole_create_rejoin_coherency.sh s617a-s617e): test2 (mounting/rejoining) dmesg at 7380 and 7471: P-LKTIMEOUT-HOLDER type=1 ino=128 ag=0 holder=<test1 id> hmode=PR hstate=2 held_ms=1046, 2070, ... 10262 queued_ms same (we=<test2 id> req=EX) once per second for 10 s, then P36-STACK ino=128 type=1 ag=0 mode=EX comm=mount (first timeout, dumping wait site) and P34-ACQ-SLOW ino=128 isdir=1 req_mode=5 dur_ms=10288 attempts=1 rc=0; and at 7431 P36-STACK ino=8388753 type=1 ag=0 mode=PR comm=cat then P34-ACQ-SLOW ino=8388753 isdir=0 req_mode=3 dur_ms=1560 attempts=1 rc=0. 12 P36-RETRY lines on test2 in that window. The lap consoles record B_MOUNT_RC=0 PHASE3 wall=4-5 s for the in-lap rejoin, so the 10 s waits fall in the cold-check remounts or the prep; the timestamps are in the test2 ring (uptime 2h at 07:13 UTC) and not yet in a per-lap capture.
defects.next: 1) Capture the survivor's side of the 10 s window: which BAST the root PR release answers (P-DIRBAST/P70-BP for ino=128 on test1 around the peer's mount) and why the first BAST does not release a cached, uncontended PR at once (a demote-on-first-BAST for the root should cost milliseconds). 2) Read mount's root EX request: whether it needs EX at all (upstream reads the root inode; the EX is MXFS's) and whether a PR would do. 3) Fix at the proven cause, then measure mount wall with a mounted peer before/after on the same build; budget the mount at 2x the lone mount.
defects.impact_why: Pace: the mount's root EX waited one BAST period (P34-ACQ-SLOW ino=128 dur_ms=10288 attempts=1 rc=0) and a read waited 1.56 s (rc=0); B_MOUNT_RC=0 on every lap, nothing hung or shut down. The record's own summary states it is pace, not stability.

defects.summary: The survivor's recovery completion still holds P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE and the exclusive-write gate behind mxfs_dlm_ledger_purge_owner, a SERIAL PER-PAGE durable pass over every page holding a record of the dead owner, measured at 4.6 ms a page: 4869 candidate pages took 22.4 s. Unlike the page takeover that used to sit next to it, this purge IS safety-required inside the barrier — the held-failure gate must see its result before the dead slot is republished, because a slot-indexed shared bit would otherwise alias to the slot's next occupant — so it cannot simply be deferred. Its cost is proportional to workload residue exactly as the takeover's was, so the same aged filesystem that produced a 7984-page takeover will produce a purge of the same order. SEPARATELY OBSERVED IN THE SAME WINDOW AND NOT YET EXPLAINED: two whole-ledger purges of the SAME {node, slot} ran concurrently and completed 18 microseconds apart with overlapping candidate sets (cand=4869 cleared=3650 total_ms=22443, and cand=4098 cleared=2439 total_ms=19096), so roughly 19 s of the 22.4 s may be duplicated work by two threads rather than one pass that is simply large.

The s58h losses were the harnesses' 90 s join bound killing mount(8) while the purge was still running (MOUNT_RC=124), a budget failure, not a hang: the cost is proportional to residue and bounded by it.
