Its recovery of the victim is INLINE: with the snapshot parked by the injector the bootstrap refused the mount (P-BOOT-FENCE-UNPROVEN -> P-BOOT-MOUNT-REFUSED, and then, on both laps, the guest panicked in the refused mount's unwind — a separate stability record, D-A-REFUSED-MOUNT-FREES-THE-DLM-CONTEXT-UNDER-ITS-FENCE-RETRY-WORKER, fixed in 0.89.70); without the injector it completes the recovery and no guard stands for the second unmount (the whole-cluster restart laps, e.g. tests/evidence/20260908T230313Z_restart_s556, are that measurement). So a fresh incarnation whose view excludes the victim either recovers the victim before it masters anything or does not mount. THE ENUMERATION IS NOW COMPLETE FOR TWO NODES. Producer (b) needs a LIVE master for a page whose authority is a dead incarnation under judgement; on two nodes a live node masters such a page only by (i) recovery completion, which retires the guard; (ii) a fresh view without the victim, which is the bootstrap above; or (iii) the victim's own rejoin under its old incarnation's parked recovery, whose slot claim the admission barrier refuses (s133d). Producer (a) needs a live REMOTE master whose own prepare is parked on a dead authority — a third identity, or a rejoined victim, which is (iii) again. A dead member keeps mastership of its pages until its recovery completes (v5_refresh_active_nodes, no dead-node filtering), so every request on them fails fast on the transport (s130c -ENOTCONN, s146f no transition) and never enters the transition wait. THEREFORE the stalled-transition wait for a non-fallible caller is not reachable on a two-node cluster, and this record is narrowed to 3 nodes from its own evidence: nothing here is disposed. WHAT REMAINS, ON THREE NODES: the design question above (a persistently failing snapshot parks a recovery with no terminal verdict, and the waiter consults no RECOVERY_BLOCKED verdict for the page's authority in either producer), the SB summary lock registration (0.89.69, built as D0499912B01369316097E83, still unexercised by any lap), and the other non-fallible callers. The rig for that is 3/tcp; its lap is the original arm with a THIRD node as the live master of the victim's page.
defects.impact_why: A caller the fallible oracle does not name waits forever on a page transition that never advances, and the only thing that ends the wait is a SIGKILL — which is the stability case the release bar refuses. It is scoped verify rather than stability because the one hang measured through it (a survivor's put_super under a terminal quarantine, 2/tcp, 0.89.43) needed a SECOND condition that 0.89.44 removed, and no lap has yet produced a permanently stalled transition from any of the other -EAGAIN sources that remain reachable.

defects.summary: Six harnesses decide verdicts by counting kernel-log probes that cannot appear, because the code emitting them is not in the built module. A probe absent from mxfs.ko is a guaranteed silence, and a harness that counts it reads that silence as a measurement of the system rather than of itself.
defects.evidence: Measured 2026-09-21 on tree 0.89.58/0.89.59, build F3199FE2112E215C2FBB787, kernel 6.8.0-101-generic, with tools/probe_audit.sh (written for this, and it reproduces the finding in one call). Of 1594 distinct probe names written as string literals in the kernel-built sources (xfs dlm pal mxfs_clayer), 1577 are in mxfs.ko. EIGHT of the absentees are counted by harnesses. SEVEN OF THEM HAVE ONE CAUSE: mxfs_disklock_recovery_begin (dlm/disklock.c:6374) was retired - it logs P238-RECOV-BEGIN-RETIRED and returns -EPROTO at :6421, and the ~185 lines after that return, which contain P234-RECOV-BEGIN-FAIL, P234-RECOV-FENCED, P234-RECOV-OWNED, P234-RECOV-UNREADABLE, P237-RECOV-INC-MISMATCH, P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED and P237-RECOV-SUPERSEDED, are unreachable and were dropped. P238-RECOV-BEGIN-RETIRED, the line immediately BEFORE the return, is present in mxfs.ko, which is what proves the function is compiled and the rest of it is not. Confirmed at the object as well as the module: 'strings -a dlm/disklock.o | grep -c P234-RECOV-FENCED' is 0, and disklock.o predates mxfs.ko, so this is not link staleness. The harnesses: tests/incarnation_mismatch_probe.sh counts FOUR of them (P234-RECOV-FENCED, P237-RECOV-INC-MISMATCH, P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED, P237-RECOV-SUPERSEDED); tests/sess448_chain61_incarnation_zero.sh counts three; tests/sess448_chain62_probe_sweep.sh counts one; tests/recov_takeover_retry_probe.sh counts P234-RECOV-OWNED. THE EIGHTH IS NOT EXPLAINED AND THAT IS ITS OWN FINDING: P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE (pal/linux/kern.c:1105), counted by tests/hotslot_contention.sh and tests/mass_umount_stall_probe.sh, is absent from pal/linux/kern.o although it SURVIVES THE PREPROCESSOR - 'make M=/src/mxfs pal/linux/kern.i' then 'grep -c P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE pal/linux/kern.i' is 1, and the control P-FUA-READ-RETRY from the same loop is 1 in both the preprocessed source AND the object. kern.o is up to date (a forced rebuild of that one object produced no recompilation and no change). So the compiler eliminated the branch that emits it, and the guard it sits behind - budget_ms < 0 from mxfs_pal_io_budget_remaining_ms (kern.c:961), which returns -1 on an exhausted registered budget - is data-dependent on a task hash table and jiffies, with no if(0), no always-false local and no false #if anywhere over it. Not investigated in this record, and listed only so they are not re-discovered as defects: P49-INSTR is behind a deliberate 'if (0 && ...)' with a comment saying so; P122-STALE-AGWRITE-SUPPRESSED/-REFRESH-FAILED sit behind a local bool never assigned true, superseded by the P124 preventer which a later session made log-only; P73-ILOCK-STUCK is an uncalled static function; P133-DREVAL-DYING is in xfs/xfs_mxfs_dentry.c, which is not in the Kbuild object list at all. None of those four is counted by any harness.
defects.next:
ITEM 2 IS NOW MAPPED LINE BY LINE AND THE SURFACE IS MUCH SMALLER THAN THIS RECORD'S SUMMARY SAYS. All six harnesses were read: 17 occurrences of the eight absent probes in total, and THIRTEEN OF THEM CANNOT AFFECT A VERDICT. tests/sess448_chain61_incarnation_zero.sh:25 and tests/sess448_chain62_probe_sweep.sh:18 pass the names to a sweep whose counts are only echoed - neither file contains a single [ / test / -eq on any of them, and chain62 contains no PASS/FAIL/RESULT line at all. tests/recov_takeover_retry_probe.sh:208 uses P234-RECOV-OWNED only as one alternative in the grep that FILLS its capture; the four counts it then takes (:217-220) are of P234-RECOV-NOTOURS, kind=TAKEOVER, kind=TOKEN-MISMATCH and P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE, and its verdict (:225-247) reads only those. tests/hotslot_contention.sh:107,111 and tests/mass_umount_stall_probe.sh:287,341 print the P302 count with printf and assign it to nothing; both verdicts are budget comparisons on a latency file (hotslot :101/:118 on the lat file, mass_umount :228/:348 on the walls file). tests/incarnation_mismatch_probe.sh:429-435 is a 33-name printed census, teed and never tested.

EXACTLY ONE ASSERTION IS MADE VACUOUSLY TRUE BY AN ABSENT PROBE, AND IT IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. tests/incarnation_mismatch_probe.sh:456 sets UNOBS from a count of P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED, and :476 asserts that UNOBS equals 0 or sets rc=1 - an assertion that the probe NEVER FIRES. The code emitting it was deleted with the rest of the retired recovery_begin, so that assertion cannot fail. It fails toward good news, silently, and it is the whole of this record's real risk.

TWO MORE ARE WEAKENED BUT NOT VACUOUS, and the difference matters: :458 and :459 build DESC_0 and DESC_E1 from a grep -aE alternation of P236-FENCE-(INTENT|CERTIFIED|SEALED) and P234-RECOV-FENCED, tested at :477, :493 and :504. Three of the four alternatives are live probes, so those counts still move; what they have lost is the ability to notice a P234-RECOV-FENCED line, which cannot occur anyway. They are over-broad patterns, not guaranteed zeroes.

THE FIX IS THEREFORE SMALL AND SPECIFIC, not six harness rewrites: (1) at :476, either delete the assertion or re-point it at the probe the LIVE path emits for the same question - the P238/P236 family that fence_intent, fence_certify, recovery_claim and recovery_takeover actually log - and say in the code which was chosen and why; (2) at :458-460, drop the dead P234-RECOV-FENCED alternative so the pattern says what it matches; (3) leave the census at :429-435 alone, or mark the dead names in it, since it is output and not a measurement. DO NOT RE-ENABLE DEAD CODE TO MAKE ANY OF THESE FIRE.

ADD THE BUILD GATE WHILE THERE: tests/iomap_revalidation_hook_reached.sh (0.89.60) ABORTs when the probe it counts is not a string in mxfs.ko, which is the shape that makes this class impossible rather than merely fixed once. tools/probe_audit.sh --gate is the same check for a list of probes.
defects.impact_why: ITEM 1 IS NOW MEASURED AND THE ANSWER IS THAT NO DISPOSITION RESTS ON ONE OF THESE VERDICTS. The record's own next step made this the question that decides its bar. CHANGELOG.md (1.27 MB) contains ZERO mentions of any of the six harnesses - 'grep -cF' per basename returns 0 for incarnation_mismatch_probe, sess448_chain61_incarnation_zero, sess448_chain62_probe_sweep, recov_takeover_retry_probe, hotslot_contention and mass_umount_stall_probe, re-run in the parent shell because it is a disposition-critical negative. That is the decisive channel: removing a record refuses to run without --why and prints the CHANGELOG entry to paste, so a removal resting on one of these harnesses would have named it there. In data/defects.json the six appear only as PENDING WORK - 'REMAINING for FIXED AND VERIFIED: the record's own probe shape', 'queued as chain 61', 'NEXT: 3) build + replay ... and assert' - and in one recorded outcome, 'RESULT FAIL BOTH ARMS'. A FAIL produced by counting an absent probe cannot launder a defect away; it can only invent one, which is the safe direction. So the defect is a property of the test suite and not of mxfs.ko: the module is correct here, recovery_begin is retired on a design ruling and refuses loudly with P238-RECOV-BEGIN-RETIRED. It corrupts no data and hangs no node, and nothing shipped rests on it. WHAT WOULD REVERSE THIS: any future disposition that cites one of the six before they are fixed. This is a scoping decision and closes nothing - the record stays open and the six harnesses still have to be pointed at the live path or retired.

defects.summary: mxfs_pal_io_budget_remaining_ms() can never return the negative value that means 'this task's I/O budget is already exhausted', because the conditional that produces it is typed unsigned. pal/linux/kern.c:972 read 'left = (d <= 0) ? -1 : jiffies_to_msecs(d)'; jiffies_to_msecs returns unsigned int, so the usual arithmetic conversions make the whole conditional unsigned int, the -1 becomes 4294967295, and that widens into the long as a large POSITIVE number. Every caller therefore reads an expired budget as ~49.7 days remaining.
defects.evidence: Measured 2026-09-21 on tree 0.89.58, build F3199FE2112E215C2FBB787, kernel 6.8.0-101-generic. THE COMPILER IS THE INSTRUMENT AND IT ANSWERED TWICE. (1) The probe the exhausted path logs, P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE (pal/linux/kern.c:1105), is in the preprocessed source and NOT in the object or the assembly: 'make M=/src/mxfs pal/linux/kern.i' then 'grep -c P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE pal/linux/kern.i' is 1, while 'strings -a pal/linux/kern.o | grep -c' the same name is 0. The control P-FUA-READ-RETRY, a pr_warn in the SAME loop, is present in all three (11 occurrences in the assembly). kern.o was up to date - a forced rebuild of that one object produced no recompilation. (2) In the emitted assembly the whole arm is gone, not just its string: 'grep -c $-62' (the -ETIME return) is 0 and 'grep -c p_fuadl_n' (the static ratelimit counter inside the arm) is 0, while 'grep -c $-110' is 5, so immediates of that shape are emitted elsewhere in the same file. GCC deletes 'if (budget_ms < 0)' only if it has proved the value cannot be negative, which is exactly what the unsigned conditional guarantees. THE CONSEQUENCE IS NOT MERELY A MISSING LOG LINE, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS: at kern.c:1111-1119 a budget_ms > 0 takes the branch that sets cmd_j = msecs_to_jiffies((unsigned int)budget_ms) and cmd_retries = 0. With budget_ms stuck at 4294967295 whenever the deadline HAS passed, the per-command timeout is the largest the conversion can produce, at precisely the moment the caller was supposed to give up. The retry loop is bounded - 'if (fua_try >= 20)' at :1137 returns -EIO - so this is 21 attempts at an unfireable timeout rather than an infinite loop, which is why it is high and not critical. NO FIELD FINGERPRINT WAS FOUND, AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN TREATED AS ABSENCE OF THE DEFECT: the retry line prints budget_ms=%ld, so an affected lap would show budget_ms=4294967295, and 'grep -ho budget_ms=[0-9-]* tests/evidence/*.console' returns nothing at all - the retry path itself has not been exercised in any captured console, so the field is silent on the question either way. THE FIX IS IN 0.89.59 AND IS VERIFIED STATICALLY: 'left = (d <= 0) ? -1L : (long)jiffies_to_msecs(d)'. Recompiling that one object takes 'strings -a pal/linux/kern.o | grep -c P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE' from 0 to 1 - the compiler restoring the branch it had proved unreachable is the before/after. ===== REACH, READ FROM EVERY CALL SITE 2026-09-22 (0.89.63): THE EXHAUSTED-BUDGET BRANCH IS UNREACHABLE ON THE TCP TRANSPORT. mxfs_pal_io_budget_remaining_ms() is static to pal/linux/kern.c and has exactly one caller, the FUA-read retry loop in mxfs_pal_scsi_read_fua_bdev (kern.c:1119). It returns a negative value only for a task that REGISTERED a budget, and the only registration in the tree is mxfs_verify_begin (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:8049, 'grep -rn mxfs_pal_io_budget_enter' over xfs dlm pal mxfs_clayer names no other), whose only consumer is mxfs_dlm_verify_rawmode (:8118) -> mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_held_rawmode (dlm/v5_mount.c:22037). That function answers per transport: on TCP it returns mxfs_dlm_held_mode(ctx->dlm, &res), which reads the dlm.c local mirror under table_rwlock (dlm/dlm.c:9623) and issues no I/O; only the CAW branch (mxfs_dlm_caw_held) reaches the on-disk slot and hence a FUA read. So on TCP no budgeted task ever enters the FUA-read loop, budget_ms is never computed for one, and neither the defect (an expired budget read as ~49.7 days) nor its probe (P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE) can occur. The record's own observation agrees: 'grep -ho budget_ms=[0-9-]* tests/evidence/*.console' returns nothing across every captured lap, TCP laps included. The 2/any classification was a keyword default, not a measurement; the transport is caw from this reading. The fix (0.89.59) is built into every transport regardless, and tools/probe_audit.sh --gate P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE exits 0 on build 06AC7CB42624D7E279F66AF (step 1 of the next-step, done).
defects.next: STEP 1 IS DONE: after the s140 queue drained, make modules built 06AC7CB42624D7E279F66AF and 'tools/probe_audit.sh --gate P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE P290-AUTH-REFUSED-DATA' exits 0 (both strings in the module). WHAT REMAINS IS THE LIVE ARM, AND IT IS A CAW ARM: the only budgeted FUA read in the tree is the CAW held-mode verify (see the reach reading appended to the evidence), so the reproduction runs on a CAW rig - 2/caw is enough - not on TCP, where the loop is never entered under a budget. Build it as previously specified: dlm_verify_deadline_ms set to a few ms so the budget expires inside the retry loop, a knob in kern.c that injects N transient failures ahead of scsi_execute_cmd so the loop iterates at all (none exists yet; the record's earlier text assumed one), a workload that drives the CAW verify probes (any contended inode on a 2/caw mount), and three separate assertions: P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE appears; the caller returns -ETIME (P302 is logged, P-FUA-READ-ERR with tries=21 is not, for that lba); and the P-FUA-READ-RETRY line's budget_ms is the small positive remainder and never 4294967295. The verify breaker (P303) must open and the mount must stay healthy - a skipped sample is the historical fail-open answer, not an error. THE SWEEP FOR THE SAME SHAPE IS DONE AND CLEAN; do not repeat it. THE CAUSE IS PROVEN AND THE FIX IS WRITTEN AND STATICALLY VERIFIED; WHAT IS OWED IS A LIVE REPRODUCTION, AND IT NEEDS AN INJECTOR THAT DOES NOT YET EXIST. NOT YET REBUILT INTO mxfs.ko: the s133 lap queue was running on F3199FE2112E215C2FBB787 when this was found and relinking mid-queue splits a sweep across two builds. 1) AFTER THE QUEUE DRAINS: make modules, then 'tools/probe_audit.sh --gate P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE P290-AUTH-REFUSED-DATA' must exit 0. That is the cheapest verification that both of this version's fixes are in the thing the nodes load, and it costs no rig time. 2) THE LIVE ARM. The path needs a registered budget (mxfs_pal_io_budget_enter) that has EXPIRED, and a FUA read that fails at least once so the retry loop is entered - on a healthy rig neither happens, which is why no console has ever printed a budget_ms at all. Build it from the knobs that already exist for making a FUA read fail under queue pressure, arm a short budget on the reading task, and assert three things separately: P302-FUA-READ-DEADLINE appears; the call returns -ETIME rather than -EIO after 21 tries; and the per-command timeout in the P-FUA-READ-RETRY line is a plausible number rather than 4294967295. The third is the one that would have caught this without the compiler. 3) THE SWEEP FOR THE SAME SHAPE IS DONE AND IT IS CLEAN - DO NOT REPEAT IT. Scope: xfs/ dlm/ pal/ mxfs_clayer/ tools/, all *.c and *.h, 450 files. Three patterns were searched function-scoped, not file-scoped, because a file-wide search of this shape produces 77 candidates that are all name reuse across different functions - every one of those was read to its declaration and every one is a signed type. (a) A ternary with a negative literal on one arm and an unsigned-returning helper on the other: 71 raw hits where the other arm is ANY function call; 69 are safe because the callee returns int or bool (atomic_read included - it returns int, so it is NOT this shape), or because a u16 from be16_to_cpu is integer-promoted to int before the usual arithmetic conversions apply, or because the arms are comparison results, or because the widening arm is ALREADY explicitly cast, as at xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:32033. (b) An unsigned-declared variable tested < 0 or >= 0: 1 hit, pal/linux/xfs_buf.c:4789, read to its declaration at :4778 which is 'int slot, k;' - a false positive from the scanner mis-bracketing nested blocks. (c) A negative sentinel assigned into an unsigned-declared variable: 0 hits, narrow and broadened. NO OTHER INSTANCE OF THE CATASTROPHIC SHAPE - a stored value with a later dead < 0 branch - EXISTS IN THE SWEPT TREE. TWO SITES SHARE THE SYNTAX AND NEITHER HAS THE CONSEQUENCE, recorded so they are not re-found and re-investigated: xfs/xfs_log.c:4638 'iclog ? be64_to_cpu(iclog->ic_header->h_tail_lsn) : -1' inside a DEBUG-only dump, and xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:26187 'tip ? xfs_ipincount(tip) : -1' where xfs_ipincount is a macro casting to unsigned int. Both are variadic printf arguments, stored in nothing and compared to nothing, and both happen to print correctly - the first through %llx where the bit pattern is identical, the second through %d where 4294967295 read back as a 32-bit int is -1. They are left alone deliberately. What is worth knowing for the future is the latent trap in the second: xfs_ipincount's '((unsigned int) atomic_read(...))' will produce this defect the first time its result is stored in a signed variable that is later tested negative.
defects.impact_why: The per-task I/O deadline was added so a FUA read under queue pressure fails instead of retrying without bound. It cannot fire: the exhausted signal is converted to a large positive remaining-time, so at the instant the deadline passes the caller hands that value to msecs_to_jiffies and issues the SCSI command with the LARGEST possible timeout - up to 21 times. A task in that state is hung for as long as the transport takes to give up, which is the failure the deadline exists to bound, and a node with a hung coherency read is a node that cannot make progress.

defects.summary: mxfs_dlm_open_last_close returns early when the node is alone (mxfs_v5_dlm_is_single_node), so a last close does not clear an open mark this node published while multi-node (i_mxfs_open_pub, set by the P90 release path). The mark is durable in this node's slot; a peer that joins later reads the file as still open here and defers its reap of an unlinked-while-open inode until some release of that inode by this node publishes the absolute (clear) state — if this node never takes a grant on the inode again, no such release comes. Class 'durable' in the sole-survivor inventory: must be maintained regardless of membership.
defects.evidence: Code: xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c mxfs_dlm_open_last_close (guard at the i_mxfs_open_pub/is_single_node check; the census attributes it to mxfs_dlm_open_clear_ride), publication at the P90-OPEN-PUBLISH arm (only while !is_single_node). Classified in tests/criteria/sole_survivor_sites.json during the guard-census disposition. Not yet measured on the rig: whether a joining peer's reap can reach this node's cached/NL state to force the repairing release.
defects.next: Instrument first: 2/tcp lap — B opens file F and a BAST from A makes B publish (P90); A unmounts; B closes F alone; A remounts, unlinks F (or finds it orphaned), and measure whether F's inode is reaped and after how long, logging the open mark at each step. If the mark persists, drop the single-node skip so the lone last close drives the same ride/clear it drives when multi-node, and re-run the lap. ===== CAUSE PROVEN and a fix built (0.89.75, 219A9E4F28D8A8AA943C9D9), NOT YET DISPOSABLE. tests/open_mark_lone_close.sh: s170a lone arm DEFECT (A deferred the free 4x on B's mark, open_holders=0x2, no fd anywhere), s170b multi control CLEAN. Two layers: mxfs_dlm_open_last_close's single-node early return (removed; s170c then logged the clear ride but the release went out with op=0 mask=0x2, still DEFECT) and the release-side open publication gated on multi-node (CLEAR half ungated; s170d lone CLEAN, s170e multi CLEAN, suite s170g 29/29 PASS). BLOCKED by D-TCP-OPEN-UNLINK-HELD-FD-READS-EMPTY-AFTER-PEER-UNLINK-S170F: d0977 arm B read empty bytes through a held fd on this build; until that is shown to predate the change, the release-side change must be treated as a suspect and this record stays open. Also queued: tests/open_mark_lone_close.sh arm openalone (B opens alone, A joins and unlinks; B's fd must read the original) written but not yet run.
defects.impact_why: measured s170a: the stale mark makes the rejoined peer defer freeing an unlinked inode every 30 s reap retry — an inode and its space are leaked; no data was lost or corrupted and no node crashed, hung or shut down, so it does not cross the 2-node TCP release bar (integrity/stability). Taken out of the gate by user decision 2026-09-23.

defects.summary: Possible window in the single-to-multi join: mxfs_bmbt_tenure_end_evict skips the D-0975 tenure-end eviction of cached bmbt blocks while the node is alone, relying on the join (mxfs_dlm_join_prepare under freeze_super -> mxfs_dlm_drop_clean_cached_blocks) to drop every clean cached block. Readers are not blocked by the freeze, so a tenure that caches a bmbt block after prepare's drop and ends before the view flips would be skipped and survive into multi-node, where a peer can free and reuse that address — the D-0975 stale-extent-map shape.
defects.evidence: Code reading only (guard-census classification): xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c mxfs_bmbt_tenure_end_evict single-node early return; mxfs_dlm_peer_joined_flush / mxfs_dlm_invalidate_cached_views ordering; freeze held until mxfs_dlm_join_commit. Not observed; reachability of a tenure END on a lone node inside that window (grants are cached and nothing BASTs a lone node) is not established.
defects.next: Establish or disprove reachability: count, at join_commit after the flip, clean cached bmbt buffers whose bb_owner inode holds no grant (a probe in the commit path). Drive a join while the incumbent runs a read-heavy workload that evicts inodes (drop_caches) during the freeze. Zero across a stressed campaign plus a proof that no tenure can end between prepare's drop and the flip disproves it; any count means drop clean bmbt buffers again after the flip. ===== 0.89.75 instruments (build EAB6CDDD85B3FFA7B7CF052): P-JOIN-BMBT-CENSUS at mxfs_dlm_join_commit (clean cached bmbt blocks, and those whose owner holds no grant), injector dbg_join_flip_delay_ms (holds between prepare's drop and the flip), driver tests/bmbt_join_window_repro.sh (A mounts alone, 400-extent punched file, B joins, a loop on A works inside the window). Reachability by code: the tenure-end site 'reclaim' is mxfs_dlm_evict in xfs_reclaim_inode, reached from the superblock shrinker, which a freeze does not stop. Runs: s169c mode 1 (read then drop_caches, 5 cycles in the window) census bmbt_cached=0 orphans=0; s169d read-only 5 cycles bmbt_cached=0; s169e POSITIVE CONTROL mode 2 (drop_caches then read) bmbt_cached=0 -> CONTROL-FAIL. So no run has put a bmbt block in the cache inside the window, and the census is not yet shown able to see one; every clean result so far is VACUOUS. Leading explanation, unverified: drop_caches only makes the inode reclaimable and the next read RECYCLES it with its in-core extent tree intact, so no bmbt block is re-read; alternatively MXFS's owner-keyed bmbt eviction at acquire keeps them out. NEXT: prove the census can see a cached bmbt block at all (e.g. count at a point where one is certainly cached — right after xfs_iread_extents of a btree fork), then force a genuine re-read inside the window (wait for the inode to leave the radix tree before reading, checked with the live icache), and only then judge the window.
defects.impact_why: user decision 2026-09-23: not a release gate. Basis: a hypothesis from code reading, never observed; the directed exerciser never placed a bmbt block in the window (s169c/d/e vacuous, positive control failing). If it is ever shown real, its shape (a stale extent map served after a peer reuses the address) is an integrity defect and the impact must be re-adjudicated.

defects.summary: Plain file creates in a directory private to one node, with the peer mounted and no contention on that directory, run at ~34 per second on the 2-node TCP rig: 2112 creates in 61.8 s on test1 and 2496 in 65.5 s on test2. Native XFS makes thousands per second on the same hardware, so this is far past the 2x-native ceiling.
defects.evidence: Suite s168b (tests/evidence/suite_2tcp_s168b.log, build 0.89.75 C909FCF51806E7AB09E7A46), alloc_witness pre-fill: tests/evidence/alloc_witness/20260923T015830Z/rank1.txt 'FILL affine_ag=0 files=2112 carved=1 wall_ms=61794', rank2.txt 'FILL affine_ag=1 files=2496 carved=1 wall_ms=65479' — a bash ': > file' loop in $MNT/alloc_witness/fill_rN, one directory per node. The row used 108 s of its 120 s budget because of it. Earlier rows show the same order: alloc_witness phase 2 made 200 creates in ~4.1 s (s166e), and the shared-directory phase 1 ~33/s per node.
defects.next: Measure native XFS on the same LUN with the same loop for the ceiling. Then profile one node's private-dir create loop (the per-create phases: dialloc/CAW inode reservation, the grant on the new inode, the directory's grant, log force) to find where ~29 ms per create goes; the related shared-directory records attribute most blocked time to the CAW inode-grant wait.
defects.impact_why: a create rate is pace only: the fills that measured it completed every create with no error, loss or crash (s168b alloc_witness PASS, chk_clean release=CLEAN)

defects.summary: Deleting 500 small files on one node that the other node created took 30.4 s on the 2/tcp Proxmox pair (pve9-2 deleting pve9-1's files), ~16 unlinks/s. Native XFS removes 500 files in well under a second, so this is far past 2x native.
defects.evidence: tests/evidence/pve9_release_0.89.80/del_f_138.log ('real 0m30.444s', del_rc=0), tests/evidence/pve9_release_0.89.80/create_f_194.log (500 created on pve9-1), tests/evidence/pve9_release_0.89.80/count_194.log (0 after the remote delete). 0.89.80, PVE 9 kernel 6.17.2-1-pve, QNAP LUN over in-guest iSCSI.
defects.next: Time the same rm on the creating node (local) and on the peer to split lock-handoff cost from unlink cost; then instrument per-unlink lock acquire wait (the directory and each inode move from the creator to the deleter) to name where the ~60 ms per file goes.
defects.impact_why: pace only: every file was deleted and both nodes agree on the result (count 0 on the creator after the remote delete); the 2-node TCP release bar is data integrity and stability, not pace

defects.summary: When a mount with no peer= option cannot discover a live peer (multicast blocked or unrouted), it retries the root inode lock for ~30 s, shuts its filesystem down, withdraws, and mount(8) reports 'can't read superblock' (rc 32). The kernel log says why (discovery broadcast failed, P-MEMB-SETTLE-TIMEOUT: 1 active foreign slot but lease sees only 1 node), but the user-facing error points at the superblock, not at discovery or the peer= option that fixes it.
defects.evidence: 0.89.84, Ubuntu 24.04 6.8.0-101, test3/test4 on the QNAP LUN, 2026-09-24 12:53-12:54 UTC: multicast DROP rules left on both nodes by an aborted harness round; test3 mounted alone, test4's plain mount logged 'discovery broadcast failed: -1' every 1-2 s, P-MEMB-SETTLE-TIMEOUT at +11 s, three 'lock request failed after 60 retries ... ino=128 mode=EX', 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable: ino=128 ... shutting down filesystem', P-WITHDRAW, P960-REFUSED-MOUNT-NOCOVER; mount printed "can't read superblock on /dev/sda", rc=32, wall ~40 s. Nothing was written (P960 quiesce writes no SB summary); test3 unaffected. tests/evidence/packaged_round/ubuntu_0.89.84_20260924T075303/plain_mount_test4.log
defects.next: When the membership settle sees an active foreign slot that discovery never reached, refuse the mount at that point with a distinct errno and a kernel message naming the cause and the fix (peer=<address>), instead of proceeding into lock retries that end in a filesystem shutdown.
defects.impact_why: The mount fails closed: it withdraws before completing, writes nothing (P960-REFUSED-MOUNT-NOCOVER), and the live peer keeps running; no data is lost or corrupted and no node crashes or hangs. The defect is the misleading error and the 40 s spent reaching it.

defects.summary: A node that crashes mid-unmount after its peer has unmounted cleanly takes 130-145 s to mount again, spent in the whole-cluster bootstrap's two ~64 s frozen-table observation windows (P-BOOT-SCAN-FROZEN) before it may declare the total outage and fence its previous incarnation; when both nodes mount at once, the one that loses the bootstrap claim is refused after ~68 s with EBUSY (P-BOOT-MOUNT-REFUSED rc=-16), which mount(8) reports as 'Transport endpoint is not connected'.
defects.evidence: tests/crash_mid_umount_remount.sh on 0.89.85 (srcversion C46F4EF317B7E80B3DDAE03), test1/test2, QNAP LUN (wwn-0x6e843b6393a5a6ed918bd4f4fdb8e7d6), 500 files written and synced on the victim, peer unmounted cleanly, victim destroyed 1 s into its unmount. ARM=alone (tests/evidence/crash_mid_umount_remount/alone_20260924T114811): victim's mount 143153 ms; P306 LU-reset fence admitted at 156.2 s uptime, certified 157.3 s, foreign replay of 502 manifest entries, P-BOOT-RECOVERY-COMPLETE 163.3 s; peer then mounted in 7215 ms. ARM=together (together_20260924T115312): peer became bootstrap owner and completed recovery (138740 ms); victim refused, P-BOOT-MOUNT-REFUSED rc=-16 at 87.4 s, mount(2) 'Transport endpoint is not connected'. Both arms: platter before recovery 504 allocated inodes, after 504, chk_mxfs clean, all 500 files visible from the peer. The 0.89.84 first sighting (packaged_round ubuntu2404_0.89.84_20260924T094458) was the same shape, confounded by the mount being issued while the node booted. Two earlier runs of the reproducer read the wrong LUN (/dev/sda, the LIO bench target) and are void.
defects.next: Reproduce without the lease bug: crash one node of a mounted 2-node TCP pair mid-unmount (sysrq-c on the guest during umount), remount it with peer= while the peer also mounts, and time each phase from dmesg: fence admission, certification, replay start, mxfs_slice_stabilize exit, mount return. Read what mxfs_slice_stabilize waits for and what satisfies it when the only other node is itself mounting. ===== Correction after reading xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:298: the mount task's msleep inside mxfs_slice_stabilize, captured 0-4 s after 'foreign replay of dead slot 0' began, is the designed stability proof (mxfs_fr_stab_passes=2 re-reads, mxfs_fr_stab_interval_ms=2000, deadline 45 s), not evidence of a stall. The measured delay is the fence admission: the victim's own key was already absent and the peer was registered, so no LU-reset fence could be admitted until the peer's mount gave up. The reproduction must mount the crashed node only after it has finished booting, and must separate 'peer idle and mounted', 'peer unmounted' and 'peer mounting concurrently'. ===== Two separate fixes: the frozen-table window length (why two ~64 s windows when the only other node is known to have departed cleanly — its GOODBYE/clean slot release is on disk), and mapping P-BOOT-MOUNT-REFUSED to an errno and message that tell the operator to retry once the bootstrap owner finishes.
defects.impact_why: Measured in both arms: no data lost (504/504 inodes, 500/500 files, chk_mxfs clean before and after recovery), no node crashed, hung or shut down; every mount returned, the slow one completing recovery and the refused one returning EBUSY. What remains is mount pace after a total outage and a misleading refusal errno.

defects.summary: tests/suite/fio_perf.sh takes 104-112 s of its 120 s budget on 2/tcp, so an ordinary rise in host load exhausts it: the 0.89.86 suite run failed it BUDGET_EXHAUSTED on both nodes.
defects.evidence: 2/tcp, test1/test2, QNAP LUN. 0.89.85 suite (C46F4EF317B7E80B3DDAE03): PASS 107s/120s, seqW=102MiB/s seqR=173MiB/s randW=28832iops randR=30515iops, hostload 8.57. 0.89.86 suite (67FB1FBF8A0DED66E87731F, tests/evidence/suite_2tcp_0.89.86.log): FAIL nodes_pass=0/2 states:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED=2 hostload=8.27. Same build rerun twice (tests/evidence/suite_2tcp_0.89.86_fio_rerun{1,2}.log): PASS 112s/120s (seqW=109 seqR=142 randW=28809 randR=31137, hostload 25.73) and PASS 104s/120s (seqW=111 seqR=112 randW=26954 randR=32574, hostload 24.99). Throughput is the same across builds; only the wall's margin is thin. The 0.89.86 change (the owned-metadata gate) touches unpublished-inode grants, which a fio job on existing files does not reach. 0.89.88 suite (4F12CE2378A09CD0A647E46, tests/evidence/suite_2tcp_0.89.88.log): FAIL BUDGET_EXHAUSTED=2 hostload=10.06, the other 29 tests PASS. Same build after a fresh prep, rerun twice (tests/evidence/suite_2tcp_0.89.88_fio_rerun{1,2}.log): PASS 105s/120s (seqW=111 seqR=192 randW=26652 randR=23641, hostload 20.12) and PASS 104s/120s (seqW=112 seqR=125 randW=27454 randR=25405, hostload 12.41) - the same margin and throughput as 0.89.86.
defects.next: Find where the 104-112 s goes before touching the budget, which must not be widened: read fio_perf.sh's job list and per-phase timing (fixed-runtime jobs vs fixed-size), time each phase on one run, and compare the fixed-size phases against native XFS on the same LUN with fio_perf_vs_xfs's numbers. If the jobs are time-based, the budget's derivation is what is wrong and must be re-derived from the jobs' runtimes; if they are size-based, the slow phase is the defect.
defects.impact_why: Pace only: in every run, failed or passed, fio completed its I/O on both nodes, the suite continued, and no node crashed, hung, shut down or logged a BUG/Oops; no data check failed.
